title: Assign equivalent column definitions when applied to all columns to a row instead
description: ## Prework - [*] Read and abide by **gt**'s [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [*] Search for duplicates among the [existing issues](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues) (both open and closed). ## Proposal When applying a style to an entire row of cells, each cell receives the style in the output HTML. This artificially inflates the HTML file size. One way to reduce this bloating is to identify common elements that exist across the entire row, and apply that style to the row -`` - rather than each cell - ``. Consider the following minimal example: --- title: 'gt test' output: html_document date: "2026-06-08" --- ```{r include = FALSE} library(tidyverse) library(gt) ``` ```{r echo = FALSE} mtcars %>% gt() %>% tab_style( style = cell_text(weight = 'bold'), locations = cells_body(rows = 2:4) ) ``` Rows 2-4 have the same **bold** formatting. That style is applied to each cell as highlighted by the red arrow. However, I've manually edited row 6 with the style applied at the row level, as highlighted by the green arrow. This enhancement might seem minimal when creating a couple of tables. However, in my practical example I'm creating an HTML that contains 100+ tables displayed in a nested `{.tabset}` arrangement. As such, only a single table is visible to the end user. All tables have the same structure, with only row formatting (no column-specific formatting). However, the 100+ tables result in a ~20Mb output. This file size could be reduced some pre-cleaning is done to apply column/cell styles common to an entire row at the row level.

title: Remove leading zero for small numeric values
description:
Hi,
In my field, we often work with numeric values that go between -1 and 1. In that situation, we often have values that would have a zero before a period, which we'd want to take out from the table. This would be similar to the fmt_number(drop_trailing_zeros) option, but I guess it would be to drop a leading zero instead. For instance, "0.75" would become ".75".
Thanks for considering!

title: markdown bulleted list in cell - duplicated text
description:
## Prework

* [x] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
* [x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue.

## Description

In a `gt` table within a quarto document, with a column formatted using `fmt_markdown()`, I see unexpected text duplication when the cell contains _only_ a bulleted (or numbered) list and no lead-in text above. This duplication doesn't appear in the viewer pane when executing the code cell in RStudio, only when rendering the full document to html. I have raised the issue with the quarto devs in https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/14397 and been referred here. 

## Reproducible example

````{qmd}
---
title: "reprex_gt_md"
editor_options: 
  chunk_output_type: console
---

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(gt)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-test
#| tbl-cap: "test"

dat_demo <-
  tribble(   
    ~Col_A,      ~Col_B,
    'A',  'Plain sentence',
    'B',  'Sentence with
    
- bullet point 1
- bullet point 2',
    'C',  '- bullet point 1
- bullet point 2',
    'D', ' 
- bullet point 1
- bullet point 2')

tbl_demo <- gt(dat_demo) |>
  tab_options(
    #, quarto.disable_processing = TRUE # stops duplicate text in row C, but breaks cell stripe formatting
  ) |>
  fmt_markdown(columns = 2) |>
  cols_width(Col_A ~pct(10))

tbl_demo
```
````
## Expected result

Text in row C, Col_B should look like

- bullet point 1
- bullet point 2

not

bullet point1bullet point2
- bullet point 1
- bullet point 2

I've tried various options for whitespace placement, different bullet symbols, etc as outlined in the documentation but so far the best solution I have is in Row D, where a non-breaking space is inserted above the list. This still adds an empty line.

The `
` is not parsed correctly. ## Reproducible example ```` --- title: "Gt interactive or not tables not correctly displaying if header in tabset" format: html engine: knitr --- ```{r} #| label: libs-import library(gt) library(tidyverse) library(quartabs) ``` ```{r} #| include: false #| label: blank-allows-gt-to-work gt::gt(mtcars) |> gt::opt_interactive() ``` ```{r} #| results: asis #| label: display-tabs-nointeractive mtcars |> nest_by(cyl) |> rowwise() |> mutate( cyl_gt = list( gt(data) |> tab_header( title = "Title", subtitle = "Subtitle" ) ) ) |> quartabs::render_tabset(cyl, cyl_gt) ``` ```{r} #| results: asis #| label: display-tabs-interactive mtcars |> nest_by(cyl) |> rowwise() |> mutate( cyl_gt = list( gt(data) |> opt_interactive() |> tab_header( title = "Title", subtitle = "Subtitle" ) ) ) |> quartabs::render_tabset(cyl, cyl_gt) ``` ```` I'm using package `quartabs` for this. It's a wrapper for including figs and tables in tabset in quarto. I've tried the *classic* hacks from [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/73585417/iterating-to-create-tabs-with-gt-in-quarto) or [here](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/2370). ``` instead of the header correctly displayed with the correct style. In addition, if the GT tables are not interactive, the header is displayed but without the formatting (`tab_style` for example) ```` ```{r} #| include: false #| label: blank-allows-gt-to-work gt::gt(mtcars) |> gt::opt_interactive() ``` ```` is recommended by the vignette of `quartabs` [here](https://sayuks.github.io/quartabs/vignettes/get_started.html#tables-1) to resolve javascript dependencies. title: Intigration of ODS export
description:
## Prework

- [x] Read and abide by **gt**'s [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Search for duplicates among the [existing issues](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues) (both open and closed).

## Proposal

First of all, thank you very much for your great work. Have you considered adding an export option for the ODS file format? ODS is an open ISO standard for tables that is becoming increasingly common in the EU. For example, [Germany has made open document formats (including ODS) mandatory](https://blog.documentfoundation.org/blog/2026/03/20/big-news-germany-has-just-made-odf-mandatory/). This means that government administrations and offices will require data to be submitted in an open standard format. ODFs are fully documented and presumably a more straightforward implementation than OpenXML (Microsoft). It would be fantastic if you could consider adding an export option.

title: tab_style() location argument does not match location of behavior if input data is a grouped data frame
description:
## Description
When creating a gt() from a grouped data frame and calling tab_style() to color-code body cells with conditional logic, the location of the color-code is incorrect. I am using R version 4.4.1, dplyr version 1.2.0, and gt version 1.0.0. Thanks for any advice!

## Reproducible example

_Note that the "color_code" column spits out the correct color code to aid in finding mismatches._

```{r}
library(dplyr) 
library(gt) 



create_dummy_data <- function(seed){
    set.seed(seed)
    dummy_data <- data.frame(
                             person = sample(c("Jane", "Lily", "Kathy",
                                                        "Dave", "Cliff", "Harry",
                                                        "Trey", "Lana", "Rosie",
                                                        "Eric", "Scott"),
                                                      size = 50,
                                                      replace = TRUE),
                             total_flags = sample(0:5, 50, TRUE))

    dummy_data 
}

create_table <- function(dummy_data){
    dummy_data |>
      mutate(color_code = case_when(
        total_flags <= 1 ~ "🟢",
        total_flags > 1 & total_flags < 4 ~ "🟡",
        total_flags >= 4 ~ "🔴"
      )) |>
      group_by(person) |>
      gt(groupname_col = "person") |>
      cols_label(total_flags = "Total Flags",
                 color_code = "Case Code") |>
      tab_options(ihtml.active = FALSE, container.height = pct(100),
                  row_group.as_column = TRUE,
                  container.overflow.x = TRUE,
                  container.overflow.y = TRUE) |>
      opt_interactive(use_page_size_select = TRUE,  use_sorting = TRUE,
                      use_filters = TRUE,
                      use_search = TRUE, use_resizers = TRUE,
                      use_highlight = TRUE)  |>

    tab_style(
      style = cell_fill(color = "#4cbb17"),
      locations = cells_body(
        columns = total_flags,
        rows = total_flags <= 1)) |>
    tab_style(
      style = cell_fill(color = "#e3c565"),
      locations = cells_body(
        columns = total_flags,
        rows = total_flags > 1 & total_flags < 4)) |>
      tab_style(
        style = cell_fill(color = "red"),
        locations = cells_body(
          columns = total_flags,
          rows = total_flags >= 4))
  }


dummy_data3 <- create_dummy_data(1031)
create_table(dummy_data3)

sessionInfo()
```




## Expected result

The cells in total_flags should be colored according to the emoji next to them.

The issue: `gt_split()` works properly in version 1.2, but not 1.3. ## Reproducible example * [X] Post a [minimal reproducible example](https://www.tidyverse.org/help/) so the maintainer can troubleshoot the problems you identify. A reproducible example is: * [X] **Runnable**: post enough R code and data so any onlooker can create the error on their own computer. * [X] **Minimal**: reduce runtime wherever possible and remove complicated details that are irrelevant to the issue at hand. * [X] **Readable**: format your code according to the [tidyverse style guide](https://style.tidyverse.org/). ``` packageVersion("gt") [1] ‘1.3.0’ ``` ``` gt::gt(Orange) |> gt::gt_split(row_every_n = 6) ``` ## Expected result This code should have produced six tables with data from the Orange dataset. title: `tab_stubhead()` errors in RTF when there are fewer labels than columns
description:
## Prework

* [ ] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
* [ ] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue.

## Description

Thanks for all the efforts to support flexible output types! We noticed the following issue for RTF specifically:

For tables with multi-column stub (multiple rowname_col's and/or row_grp_as_column = TRUE), we can use `tab_stubhead()` to define the labels. These can be one label for all columns, one label per column, or no labels. All works well in HTML but doing 1 label or no labels fails in RTF:

``` r
library(gt)

# Both stubs labeled - OK
tab1 <- exibble |>
  gt(
    rowname_col = c("group", "char")
  )|> 
  tab_stubhead(
    label = c("Group","Char")
  ) 

tab1 |> 
  gt::gtsave("test.rtf")

# Both stubheads labeled w/ empty strings - OK
tab2 <- exibble |>
  gt(
    rowname_col = c("group", "char")
  )|>   
  tab_stubhead(
    label = c("","")
  ) 

tab2 |> 
  gt::gtsave("test.rtf")

# One stubhead label - Error
tab3 <- exibble |>
  gt(
    rowname_col = c("group", "char")
  ) |>   
  tab_stubhead(
    label = c("Group / Char")
  ) 

tab3 |> 
  gt::gtsave("test.rtf")
#> Error in `x[[i]]`:
#> ! subscript out of bounds

# No stubhead labels - Error
tab4 <- exibble |>
  gt(
    rowname_col = c("group", "char")
  )

tab4 |> 
  gt::gtsave("test.rtf")
#> Error in `x[[i]]`:
#> ! subscript out of bounds
```

title: Latex issue error "shortstack" with as_latex()
description:
### Description


Calling  as_latex() on a gt table that uses summary_rows()/grand_summary_rows() plus stub styling (cells_stub_summary(), cells_stub_grand_summary()) throws a LaTeX error:
Error in if (!grepl("\\shortstack[l]", x, fixed = TRUE)) { : argument is of length zero}.
This used to work with older gt versions ( such as 1.0, but not after ! ).

### Reproducible example
```
library(gt)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

df <- tibble(
  grp = c("G1","G1","G2"),
  row = c("r1","r2","r3"),
  level = c("1A","2A","1A"),
  val = c(1,2,3)
)

tbl <- df |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = level, values_from = val, values_fill = 0) |>
  gt(rowname_col = "row", groupname_col = "grp") |>
  summary_rows(columns = where(is.numeric), fns = list("Sous total" = ~sum(.))) |>
  grand_summary_rows(columns = where(is.numeric), fns = list("Total général" = ~sum(.))) |>
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold", align = "right"),
    locations = list(cells_stub_summary(), cells_stub_grand_summary())
  ) |>
  tab_spanner(label = "Group BOB", columns = c(`1A`, `2A`)) |>
  cols_label(starts_with("1") ~ "")

as_latex(tbl)
```


as_latex(tbl) should return valid LaTeX without error; summary rows and their stub styling should render normally. Works well on html output. 

Thanks so much for your help and for maintaining gt.

title: `cells_stub(columns = NULL)` does not target all stub columns
description: ## Prework * [x] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md). * [x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue. ## Description The help file for `cells_stub()` `columns` argument states: "The stub columns to which targeting operations are constrained. By default (NULL), all stub columns are targeted for backward compatibility." However in the following example, only the first stub column is right-aligned: ``` exibble |> gt( rowname_col = c("group", "char") )|> tab_style( style = list( cell_text(align = "right") ), locations = list(cells_stub(columns = NULL)) ) ``` I am able to right-align all stub columns by passing the column names explicitly: ``` exibble |> gt( rowname_col = c("group", "char") )|> tab_style( style = list( cell_text(align = "right") ), locations = list(cells_stub(columns = c("group", "char"))) ) ``` I'm not sure if this is a bug in `cells_stub()` or if the documentation needs updating. Thanks!

title: Exporting a gt table to html with spaces in column names produces invalid html headers attributes
description:
## Prework * [x] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md). * [x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue. ## Description Exporting a gt table to html with spaces in column names produces invalid html header attributes. The generated `header` attributes for `td` tags are not correctly coded and therefore reference non-existing `id`s. ## Reproducible example ```R library(gt) # Version 1.1.0 sep_character <- "_" # Data frame with spaces in columns df <- data.frame( `married_low income` = c(30, 2), `married_high income` = c(30, 4), `single_low income` = c(20, 1), `single_high income` = c(20, 2), col = c("age", "hsize"), check.names = F ) table <- gt(df, rowname_col = "col") |> tab_spanner_delim(delim = sep_character) html <- table |> as_raw_html(inline_css = F) writeLines(html, "gt.html") ``` ## Output ```html
married
single
low income high income low income high income
age 30 30 20 20
hsize 2 4 1 2
``` The produced table correctly renders to this: But there are some problems concerning accessibility: In line 17 the column "married_low income" gets coded to id="married_low-income". But in line 25 the element is referenced incorrectly by `headers="married_low income"`. The header attributes for the other columns are also incorrecly coded. ## Expected result The columns should be coded to id and header attributes exactly the same way. E.g. `id=married_low-income` and `headers="married_low-income"` Thank you for your help! @olhaau @ysaidani

title: `tab_spanner()` unnecessarily reorders columns when `gather = TRUE`
description:
## Prework * [x] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md). * [x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue. ## Description When calling `tab_spanner()` with the `gather = TRUE` argument, columns are reordered to match the order they were specified in the `columns` argument. They do not maintain their existing order in the table. ## Reproducible example ``` r library(gt) data.frame(a = 1, b = 2, c = 3) |> gt() ```
a b c
1 2 3
Adding a `tab_spanner()` with `gather = TRUE` (the default) reorders the columns. ``` r data.frame(a = 1, b = 2, c = 3) |> gt() |> tab_spanner("Spanner", columns = c(c, b), gather = TRUE) ```
a
Spanner
c b
1 3 2
Compare with `gather = FALSE`, where columns preserve their existing order even though they are specified out of order in the `columns` argument. ``` r data.frame(a = 1, b = 2, c = 3) |> gt() |> tab_spanner("Spanner", columns = c(c, b), gather = FALSE) ```
a
Spanner
b c
1 2 3
Created on 2025-11-17 with [reprex v2.1.1](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) ## Expected result I believe that the columns should have stayed in the order the appeared in the original table, based on this text from the `?tab_spanner` help file: > `gather` > Gather columns together⁠ > `scalar` // default: `TRUE` > An option to move the specified columns such that they are unified under the spanner. Ordering of the moved-into-place columns will be preserved in all cases. By default, this is set to TRUE. This suggests to me that when `gather = TRUE`, columns may be moved so that all items covered by the `tab_spanner()` are adjacent, but their order should be the same as before they were moved. In the case in the reprex above, the order of columns changed even though no column needed to be moved to make all spanned columns adjacent. In the toy example above, the solution is obvious: one can simply reorder the `columns` argument. But this becomes more complicated if e.g. using multiple tidyselect helpers. Given this, I think either - the `tab_spanner()` function should be refactored to ensure that the relative order of `gather`ed columns are preserved, or - if this is intended behavior, the help file for `tab_spanner()` should be edited to make this clear. ## Session info

title: [accessibility] table header formatting in .docx export
description: ## Prework * [x] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md). * [x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue. ## Description Currently, `gt` tables exported to Word don't arrive with correctly labelled row or column headers. Admittedly, I've had trouble ascertaining the criteria that determine whether a table in Word is accessible (online sources differ; I'll provide more detail below), but it seems to boil down to two elements: 1. Under **Table Layout**, the option needs to be selected to **Repeat Header Rows**. a. `gt` already does this -- thank you! 😄 2. Under **Table Design**, the **Header Row** checkbox must be checked (and the **First Column** checkbox if the first column contains row labels, aka a stub). a. `gt` does _not_ currently do this. ☹️ ## Reproducible example (.qmd) ````` --- title: "a11y-test" format: html: embed-resources: true docx: toc: false --- ```{r setup, include=FALSE} knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE) library(gt) ``` A simple table: ```{r} iris |> dplyr::group_by(Species) |> dplyr::summarise(Length = mean(Petal.Length), Width = mean(Petal.Width)) |> gt(rowname_col = 'Species') |> tab_header(title = 'Iris petal width') ``` ```{r echo=TRUE, message=TRUE} sessioninfo::session_info() ``` ````` Yields a document where: The **Repeat Header Rows** option is selected 😄 But the **Header Row** and **First Column** boxes are not checked ☹️ ## Expected result I expected the table to mark the first row as the header row (by default) and the first column as well (because I specified a stub with row labels in my call to `gt`). ## More about tables in Word Different sources specify different criteria for making tables accessible in Word documents. [Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/video-create-accessible-tables-in-word-cb464015-59dc-46a0-ac01-6217c62210e5) and [Penn State](https://accessibility.psu.edu/microsoftoffice/microsofttableheaders/) only specifies using the **Header Row** checkbox. Other sources like [UC Riverside](https://sdrc.ucr.edu/accessible-word-tables) only mention the **Repeat Header Rows** toggle, while a few sources like [Perkins School for the Blind](https://www.perkins.org/resource/creating-accessible-table-word/) specify additional steps. From my own (manual, non-exhaustive) testing, it appears the **Header Row** checkbox is essential, and whether or not the **Repeat Header Rows** toggle is essential, it's certainly good practice that makes tables easier to read. ## Session info ``` sessioninfo::session_info() ─ Session info ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── setting value version R version 4.4.1 title: gtsave() not saving as .png apparently due to change in headless Chrome
description:
## Description

gtsave() is not saving as .png.  It appears that this is due to a change in headless Chrome.  The error received is:

```
Error in `with_random_port()`:
! Cannot find an available port. Please try again.
Caused by error in `startup()`:
! Failed to start chrome. Error:
Old Headless mode has been removed from the Chrome binary. Please use the new Headless mode (https://developer.chrome.com/docs/chromium/new-headless) or the chrome-headless-shell which is a standalone implementation of the old Headless mode (https://developer.chrome.com/blog/chrome-headless-shell).
Run `rlang::last_trace()` to see where the error occurred.
```

I do note that there is already an issue open for gtsave() not saving as png [#1060 ](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/1060) but this appears to be a different issue.

## Reproducible example

reprox <-
  gtcars |>
  dplyr::select(model:drivetrain) |>
  dplyr::slice(1:10)|>
  gt() 

reprox |> 
  gtsave("reprox.png")

## Expected result

This should have produced a gt table.

title: Multi-line column labels are justified for format typst
description:
## Prework

* [x] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
* [x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue.

## Description

Multi-line column labels are justified for format `typst`, which is inconsistent with other output formats.

- It seems that `typst` justifies multi-line text in tables by default. Can be turned-off with `#show table: set par(justify: false)` as [described here](https://github.com/typst/typst/issues/2951#issuecomment-1857689437). 
- Text alignment and justification seem to be handled separately in`typst` hence using `gt::tab_style()` to change text alignment does not have an impact on justification in `typst` output. 

## Reproducible example

````
---
title: "Typst Tables Justify Test"
format: typst
execute: 
  echo: false
  warning: false
---

```{r}
library(gt)
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}
df <- tibble(
  "Long name with words" = c(1, 2, 3),
  "Another long name" = c(4, 5, 6),
  other = 1:3,
  other2 = 2:4,
  other3 = 3:5,
  other4 = 4:6,
  other5 = 6:8
)
```

## Current Output

```{r}
gt(df)
```

## Desired Output

```{=typst}
#show table: set par(justify: false)
```

```{r}
gt(df)
```


```{r}
sessionInfo()
```
````

## Expected result

Multi-line text in tables are not justified in typst format. Attached pdf shows current and expected/desired result. Session info is included in attached PDF. 


[typst_table_test.pdf](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22912648/typst_table_test.pdf)

## Description

After updating to `gt` version 1.1.0, I can no longer load the package. `library(gt)` fails with this error message:

```
Error: package or namespace load failed for 'gt':
 .onLoad failed in loadNamespace() for 'gt', details:
  call: str2expression(readLines(system.file("latex_unicode/latex_unicode_conversion.txt",
  error: <text>:35:0: unexpected end of input
33:   "\U00BF"='\\textquestiondown',                    # character ¿",

   ^
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In readLines(system.file("latex_unicode/latex_unicode_conversion.txt",  :
  invalid input found on input connection 'C:/Users/Matthew/AppData/Local/R/win-library/4.5/gt/latex_unicode/latex_unicode_conversion.txt'

  incomplete final line found on 'C:/Users/Matthew/AppData/Local/R/win-library/4.5/gt/latex_unicode/latex_unicode_conversion.txt'

# Try and load:

```

Since there isn't an issue about this already, I have a sneaking suspicion that this error won't reproduce so easily for others. So, here's the output from my machine (`sessionInfo()` included):

## Investigation

Taking a peek at the file, it looks like `readLines` is getting tripped up when it encounters a `U+FFFD` ("Replacement Character," `�`) in `latex_unicode_conversions.txt` (`0xEF 0xBF 0xBD` in UTF-8). It only emits a warning, not an error; but it also stops reading the file, which causes `str2expression` to fail completely trying to parse the vector. I find it odd that `readLines` would fail here, since `U+FFFD` is a totally normal Unicode character, and I would _assume_ that `readLines` should support Unicode/UTF-8 just fine... but I guess not? I tried loading the file myself with `encoding = "UTF-8"`, but that didn't work either.

The top of the file has a comment that says it was "copied from [`pylatexenc/latexencode/_uni2latexmap.py`][pylatexenc]," seemingly in PR #1996. It would appear that whatever script/tool was used to convert the Python dictionary into an R vector was not Unicode/UTF-8 aware. For example, on the line that trips up `readLines`, the original file [had `U+00C0 À`][c0original], encoded as `0xC3 0x80` in UTF-8. It looks like the script tried to convert `0xC3` and `0x80` as separate codepoints, [giving `�` and `\u0080`][c0new]. The lines immediately after show the same thing with `�\u0081`, `�\u0082`, etc. The `latex_unicode_conversions.txt` file was updated in #2042, but it looks like this specific issue wasn't caught.

I suspect that the specific issue of `readLines` getting tripped up by a `U+FFFD` might be platform-specific, which would explain why no tests ran into this issue (since not being able to load the package is a pretty glaring issue!). I'm more than willing to provide additional system information and do additional testing to get to the bottom of this.

- [x] Search for duplicates among the [existing issues](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues) (both open and closed).

## Proposal

Currently, when use_filters = TRUE in opt_interactive(), filter inputs are automatically added for all columns in the table.
It would be useful to have control over which columns are filterable.

For example, in a Shiny app I use a column to store action buttons. A search bar is still generated above that column, even though filtering on it doesn’t make much sense.

Instead of accepting only a boolean for use_filters, it would be great if the argument could also accept a tidyselect-style input (e.g. -column_name, etc.) to specify which columns should have filters enabled.

title: `latex unicode conversion` leads compiling error for CJK document
description:
## Prework

* [x] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
* [x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue.

## Description

`latex unicode conversion` leads compiling error for CJK document. Only gt 1.1.0 has this issue, gt 1.0.0 does not.

## Reproducible example

````
---
title: "quote test"
date: today
lang: zh
engine: knitr
format:
    pdf:
        pdf-engine: xelatex
        keep-tex: true
---

```{r}
library(gt)

df <- data.frame(
    'en' = c('\'test\'', '"test"'),
    'zh' = c('“测试”', '‘测试’')
)

gt(df)
```
````

For gt 1.1.0, it generates the follow latex code:

```
\begin{table}
\fontsize{12.0pt}{14.0pt}\selectfont
\begin{tabular*}{\linewidth}{@{\extracolsep{\fill}}ll}
\toprule
en & zh \\ 
\midrule\addlinespace[2.5pt]
'test' & \textquotedblleft测试\textquotedblright \\ 
"test" & \textquoteleft测试\textquoteright \\ 
\bottomrule
\end{tabular*}
\end{table}
```

There is no spacing between latex code and text characters in `\textquotedblleft测试\textquotedblright`, which make this an `Undefined control sequence`. I think this issue may be related with the follwing code: https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/77c3bb9945e37da877c6ee3c76f2edde02379a4e/R/helpers.R#L3130-L3147.

## Expected result

Should be compiled successfully.

title: `gt::cols_width()` can't find a variable when set within a function
description:
## Description `gt::cols_width()` seems not to find a variable of column names when created within a function. ## Reproducible example ``` r # create a small example tibble ex_tbl <- gt::gtcars |> dplyr::select(c("mfr", "model", "year")) |> dplyr::filter(dplyr::if_any("year", \(x) x == 2015)) |> dplyr::slice_head(n = 2) |> gt::gt() # store a vector of column names as a variable wide_cols <- c("mfr", "model") ``` These work fine: ``` r ex_tbl |> gt::cols_width(c("mfr", "model") ~ gt::pct(45)) ```
mfr model year
Ferrari 458 Speciale 2015
Ferrari 458 Spider 2015
``` r ex_tbl |> gt::cols_width(tidyselect::all_of(wide_cols) ~ gt::pct(45)) ```
mfr model year
Ferrari 458 Speciale 2015
Ferrari 458 Spider 2015
Wrapping the same code in a function seems to work... ``` r format_tbl <- function(gt_tbl) { wide_cols <- c("mfr", "model") gt_tbl |> gt::cols_width(tidyselect::all_of(wide_cols) ~ gt::pct(45)) } ex_tbl |> format_tbl() ```
mfr model year
Ferrari 458 Speciale 2015
Ferrari 458 Spider 2015
But actually it is reading the variable in from the external environment. If we delete the variable and try the function again, it doesn't work: ``` r rm(wide_cols) ex_tbl |> format_tbl() #> Error in `gt::cols_width()`: #> ℹ In argument: `tidyselect::all_of(wide_cols)`. #> Caused by error: #> ! object 'wide_cols' not found ``` even though the variable is created within the function This seems like an issue with `gt::cols_width()`. A similar function with `gt::cols_align()` works fine: ``` r format_tbl <- function(gt_tbl) { wide_cols <- c("mfr", "model") gt_tbl |> gt::cols_align("right", tidyselect::all_of(wide_cols)) } ex_tbl |> format_tbl() ```
mfr model year
Ferrari 458 Speciale 2015
Ferrari 458 Spider 2015
Perhaps it has to do with how the expression syntax in `cols_width()` handles its environment? title: Problem with UTF-8 characters, PDF output, v1.1 regression
description:
## Prework

* [x] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
* [x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue.

## Description

Using gt within a Quarto document, PDF output, `pdf-engine: xelatex`, I get errors and/or incorrect table formatting with gt 1.1 when the cell content includes accented characters. The new version is changing characters like `’` to `\textquoteright` and isn't adding a space or `{}`, resulting in errors with names. And `é` is converted to `\\'e`, which TeX interprets as a table linefeed instead of an accented e. Part of the reason for using `pdf-engine: xelatex` is to avoid any utf-8 translations.

This is a regression from v1.0, which does not have any of these errors with the same document.

## Reproducible example

* [x] Post a [minimal reproducible example](https://www.tidyverse.org/help/) so the maintainer can troubleshoot the problems you identify. A reproducible example is:
    * [x] **Runnable**: post enough R code and data so any onlooker can create the error on their own computer.
    * [x] **Minimal**: reduce runtime wherever possible and remove complicated details that are irrelevant to the issue at hand.
    * [x] **Readable**: format your code according to the [tidyverse style guide](https://style.tidyverse.org/).

````
---
title: "GT Test"
engine: knitr
execute:
  message: false
  warning: false
  echo: true
  eval: true
format:
  pdf:
    pdf-engine: xelatex
    keep-tex: true
---

```{r}
library(tibble)
library(gt)

sessionInfo()

tribble(
  ~name, ~finish_time,
  "Chloé Laplantine", "4:37:12",
  "Trent O’Shell", "5:15:46",
) |>
  gt()
```
````

## Expected result

I expect the table to render, with the original UTF-8 characters. For example, here's what the TeX looks like for the table when using gt 1.0:

````
\begin{table}
\fontsize{12.0pt}{14.4pt}\selectfont
\begin{tabular*}{\linewidth}{@{\extracolsep{\fill}}lr}
\toprule
name & finish\_time \\ 
\midrule\addlinespace[2.5pt]
Chloé Laplantine & 4:37:12 \\ 
Trent O’Shell & 5:15:46 \\ 
\bottomrule
\end{tabular*}
\end{table}
````

With gt 1.1, the TeX looks like the following, which causes a linefeed between Chlo and the accented character, and TeX quits at \textquoterightShell (since that's not a TeX command).

````
\begin{table}
\fontsize{12.0pt}{14.0pt}\selectfont
\begin{tabular*}{\linewidth}{@{\extracolsep{\fill}}lr}
\toprule
name & finish\_time \\ 
\midrule\addlinespace[2.5pt]
Chlo\\'e Laplantine & 4:37:12 \\ 
Trent O\textquoterightShell & 5:15:46 \\ 
\bottomrule
\end{tabular*}
\end{table}
````

title: text_transform and ampersands
description:
## Description

Not sure if this is an issue with gt's `text_transform()` or with my code, but when I try to use `text_transform()` and stringr's `str_to_title()` convert strings containing ampersands into title case the ampersand is converted into the html character entity '\&'.

## Reproducible example
```
# Create tibble with strings containing ampersands
table_values <- tibble(
  pairs = c("MAC & CHEESE", "STRAWBERRY & VANILLA", "LEMON & GINGER")
)

# Create gt table and transform strings to title case
table_values |>
  gt() |>
  text_transform(
    fn = function(x) {
      str_to_title(x)
    },
    locations = cells_body(columns = pairs)
  )

# Note that the str_to_title() function on its own produces the correct result
str_to_title(table_values$pairs)
```

## Expected result

The strings should be converted to title case while preserving the ampersands, as when the `str_to_title()` function is used outside of `gt()`.

* [x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue.

## Description

When a table with a left-aligned stub is output to RTF, the stub becomes right-aligned.

## Reproducible example

```
exibble |>
     gt(
         rowname_col = "row",
         groupname_col = "group",
         row_group_as_column = TRUE
     ) |> 
    tab_style(
        style = list(cell_text(align = "left")),
        locations = list(cells_stub(), cells_row_groups())
    ) |> 
    gtsave("test.rtf")
```

title: Cryptic message when overwriting docx file
description:
## Description

gt cannot overwrite a .docx file saved in a shared Dropbox folder, and returns a cryptic error message if the file already exist.

There are no problems overwriting .docx files saved in local folders.

Related: https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/1726

## Reproducible example

```
# DropBox shared folder
infp <- file.path(paperdir, "test.docx")
mtcars %>% tibble::as_tibble() %>% gt::gt() %>% gt::gtsave(infp)
mtcars %>% tibble::as_tibble() %>% gt::gt() %>% gt::gtsave(infp)
```

Error message:

> Unknown output format doc
> Pandoc can convert to DOCX, but not to DOC.
> Error: pandoc document conversion failed with error 22

```
# Local folder
infp <- file.path("test.docx")
mtcars %>% tibble::as_tibble() %>% gt::gt() %>% gt::gtsave(infp)
mtcars %>% tibble::as_tibble() %>% gt::gt() %>% gt::gtsave(infp)
```

No problem

## Expected result

The docx file should have been overwritten without error messages

title: `fmt_percent` does not match with `filters` in `opt_interactive`
description:
## Description of the bug

When using `fmt_percent` and `opt_interactive(use_filters = TRUE)` in a table, the values that are filtered do not match the values shown by the table. They match the values without applying `fmt_percent`. That, is, if you want to filter a value of 26%, in the filter you must type 0.26. This is not very intuitive when navigating the report, especially for people that did not participate in the preparation of the report.

Describe the bug clearly and concisely. 

## Reproducible example

```r
library(dplyr)
library(gt)

penguins |> 
    count(island, species) |> 
    mutate(prop_species = n / sum(n), .by = island) |> 
    gt() |> 
    fmt_percent(prop_species) |> 
    opt_interactive(use_filters = TRUE)
```

## Expected result

The value entered in the filter should match the value shown in the table. That is, when typing 26, the rows with 26% should be filtered.

## Session info

  gt()
  
gt_grp <- gt_group(gt_tbl, gt_tbl) |>
  cols_align(
    align = "center"
  )

`

title: Do not let gt perform Markdown processing when in a Quarto context
description:
When gt does Markdown processing, it uses `markdown::mark()` but I've recently become aware that this now uses `litedown::mark()`. This has implications for reference processing so this needs to be looked at.

Also, when inside a Quarto render, `mark()` is still called. This is shown with this example that issues `Warning in replace(z): Reference key(s) not found: tbl-kable-equation` (which comes from `markdown::mark()`).

```r
data.frame(
  Feature = c("Formatting", "Math", "References", "Media"),
  Example = c(
    c("**Bold**, *italic*, and `code`"),
    "$\\int_{a}^{b} f(x) \\, dx$",
    "See @tbl-kable-equation for example of a table",
    "{{< video https://www.youtube.com/embed/wo9vZccmqwc >}}"
  ),
  Notes = c(
    "Basic markdown formatting",
    "LaTeX math expressions",
    "Cross-references to other document elements",
    "Embedded media using shortcodes"
  )
) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_markdown(columns = "Example")
```

In the Quarto context, we should not do any Markdown processing. I think the exception is if `tab_options(quarto.disable_processing = TRUE)` is used.

# Save PNG file to disk

  filename = filename,
  plot = plot_object,
  device = "png",
  dpi = 100,
  width = 5,

)

title: Add SI-system to 'system = ' when 'suffixing = TRUE' in fmt_number()
description:
Please add the SI-system when suffixing numbers with fmt_number().

`fmt_number(suffixing = TRUE, system = "SI")` then the suffixes would be 1E3: k, 1E6: M, 1E9: G, 1E12: T and so on.

It would be even greater, when this also works with small numbers, e.g. 0.001 becomes 1m, 0.000001 becomes 1µ and so on.
List of prefixes: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metric_prefix#List_of_SI_prefixes

title: numeric filters with opt_interactive
description:
Is it possible to include the ability to apply some basic logical filters on numeric columns when using opt_interactive with use_filters = T? Currently, use_filters creates an search box at the top of the column, which is not so useful for numeric columns.

Use cases include:

- Filter a statistics table by a p-value threshold
- Restricting table view to a numeric range by column

I suppose very sophisticated interaction could be imagined, such as combining logical filters across columns, but I would be happy with a simple ability to filter a numeric column for now.

For reference, the DT package provides a similar ability, but is restricted to providing range sliders for numeric columns. The DataTables package that DT is based on is highly customizable, though.

title: Can `data_color` accept anonymous functions
description:
Hi, I am wondering if there is any functionality to support applying `data_color` to multiple columns using anonymous functions. That's probably not obvious what I mean - this is my use-case

I have 1-2 reference columns and many columns that I would like to color based on some condition involving those reference columns and the target columns. For example, this is what I would like to do, using my understanding of the existing `data_color` API:

```
gt::gt(
  mtcars
) |> 
  gt::data_color(
    columns = c(vs), # target 1
    rows = vs > wt 
  ) |> 
  gt::data_color(
    columns = c(am), # target 2
    rows = am > wt 
  ) |> 
  gt::data_color(
    columns = c(gear), # target  3
    rows = gear > wt  
  ) 
```

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e1a06241-f570-4217-8584-78c28a172a0e)

But because I have so many columns, and often I do not know what their names are ahead of time, I would like to iterate with something like an anonymous function:

```
gt::gt(
  mtcars
) |> 
  gt::data_color(
    columns = c(vs, am, gear), # target 1
    rows = ~. > wt 
  ) 
```

Is this functionality existing, or planned? 

My current work around is to add some special characters beforehand based on conditions (using a long tidy df and mutate -> pivot_wider) and then apply [tab_style_body](https://gt.rstudio.com/reference/tab_style_body.html) using regex, that way I don't need to reference the reference columns at all.

title: Inconsistent Column Width Adjustment with `opt_interactive()`
description:
## Prework

* [x] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
* [x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue.

## Description

Using opt_interactive(), if I try to change the columns width with cols_width(), the specified column's width does not change as expected. Instead, the width of the adjacent column is changed. The issue seems to occur only when `rowname_col` is passed to gt(). For example, in the code below using the gtcars data, adding cols_width(mfr ~ px(20)), the width of mfr doesn't change, but the width of year becomes 20px.

![Without rowname_col](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6481cf56-5c6a-436a-8b4a-20999520e062)
![With rowname_col](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8e873466-21cf-42bc-8b5b-fafcc0a265e7)

Moreover, it's possibly unrelated, but I also noticed that when rowgroups are present, opt_interactive() adds an extra empty column to the left of the table. Notice how, without opt_interactive(), the car's model is directly below the rowgroup header, while with opt_interactive() there is extra space.

![groupname_but_not_interactive](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c5224363-bc7e-4acc-b2d2-9f222b26345f)
![with_groupname_col](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c4522e84-c6cc-4d8e-8591-2cbc505aa4cf)

## Reproducible example

```r
library(gt)
library(dplyr)

gtcars_short <- gtcars |>
  group_by(ctry_origin) |>
  slice_head(n = 1) |>
  ungroup()

gtcars_short |>
  gt() |>
  cols_width(
    "mfr" ~ px(20),
  ) |>
  opt_interactive() |>
  tab_header("Without rowname_col, all good")

gtcars_short |>
  gt(rowname_col = "model") |>
  cols_width(
    "mfr" ~ px(20),
  ) |>
  opt_interactive() |>
  tab_header("With rowname_col, width of `year` changes instead of `mfr`")

gtcars_short |>
  gt(rowname_col = "model", groupname_col = "year") |>
  cols_width(
    "mfr" ~ px(20),
  ) |>
  tab_header("Without opt_interactive(), there is no extra space")

gtcars_short |>
  gt(rowname_col = "model", groupname_col = "year") |>
  cols_width(
    "mfr" ~ px(20),
  ) |>
  opt_interactive() |>
  tab_header("With groupname_col, an extra empty column is added")
```

## Expected result

I expected the width of the `mfr` column to change, but instead the width of `year` changed. The column that changes seems to always be the one next to the specified one. It looks like adding rownames with opt_interactive() causes an unintended shift of the columns to the left.

## Description

`gt::data_color()` produces the following error when used in a Shiny app that is exported with shinylive:

`Error: Failed to compute colors for column <column name>`

## Reproducible example

* [x] Post a [minimal reproducible example](https://www.tidyverse.org/help/) so the maintainer can troubleshoot the problems you identify. A reproducible example is:

```r
ui <- shiny::fluidPage(
  gt::gt_output("demo_table")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$demo_table <- gt::render_gt({
    mtcars |>
      gt::gt() |>
      gt::data_color(
        columns = "mpg",
        palette = "BrBG"
      )
  })
}

shiny::shinyApp(ui, server)
```

Suppose this app lives in a folder called "myapp", run `shinylive::export("myapp", "site")` and then `httpuv::runStaticServer("mysite")`

title: gt::fmt_markdown renders incorrectly in Quarto document
description:
If we assign the value "" (no space) to certain cells in a data frame, gt will correctly display those as blank cells when rendering the table in RStudio, but if rendering in Quarto, those values are considered non-existent, and the remaining values are (erroneously) recycled. The easy fix is to convert those values to " " (with space). I'm not sure if this is really a bug, perhaps an inconsistency; but one that could have large effects on the output. Below is a Quarto document with examples of the issue (gt version 1.0.0, quarto version 1.7.24, R version 4.5.0):

[originally posted here: https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-r/issues/231]

~~~text
---
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
---

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

library(gt)
```

```{r}
#| echo: true

# Output is correct, but `test` is not formatted
data <- mtcars[1:5, ]
data$comment <- c("test", "`test`", "", "test", "")
data |> 
  gt()
```

```{r}
#| echo: true

# "" (no space) in comment treated as non-existent, so vector is (erroneously) recycled
data <- mtcars[1:5, ]
data$comment <- c("test", "`test`", "", "test", "")
data |> 
  gt()|>
  fmt_markdown(columns = comment)
```

```{r}
#| echo: true

# " " (with space) in comment, treated as existing; works properly
data <- mtcars[1:5, ]
data$comment <- c("test", "`test`", " ", "test", " ")
data |> 
  gt()|>
  fmt_markdown(columns = comment)
```

```{r}
#| echo: true

# Another option: NA + sub_missing (but format is different)
data <- mtcars[1:5, ]
data$comment <- c("test", "`test`", NA, "test", NA)
data |> 
  gt()|>
  fmt_markdown(columns = comment) |> 
  sub_missing(columns = comment, missing_text = "")
```
~~~

## Description

Hey guys! Been using `as_gtable()` for a while now and since I found out about it, it has been an absolute game changer. Within my organization, we rely on pdf generation for which this function has been incredibly useful. However, when rendering gtables that use `gt_img_rows()` I can't get the images rendered, while, for example, in the shiny apps they do. I would love to know why it isn't working, or if I can do something about it.  Here's my reprex:


## Reproducible example

library(gt)

library(gridExtra)

game_recap_layout <- function(data){
  
  gt_box_score <- box_score_data %>% 
    gt() %>% 
    tab_header(
      title = md("**Final**")
    ) %>%
    opt_align_table_header(align = 'left') %>% 
    cols_align(
      align = 'center',
      columns = everything()
    ) %>%

      locations = cells_body(
        rows = runs == max(runs),       # highlight the winning team's row
        columns = runs             # ...only the runs column (or remove 'columns' to highlight entire row)
      )
    ) %>%
    tab_style(
      style = cell_text(size = "20px", weight = "bold"),
      locations = cells_title(groups = "title")
    ) %>% 
    
    # Some optional styling to mimic a clean scoreboard look
    tab_options(
      table.border.top.style             = "hidden",
      table.border.bottom.style          = "hidden",
      table.border.left.style            = "hidden",
      table.border.right.style           = "hidden",
      column_labels.border.top.style     = "hidden",
      column_labels.border.bottom.width  = px(1),

      table_body.border.bottom.style     = "hidden",
      table_body.border.top.style        = "hidden",
      table.layout = 'auto',

    ) %>% 
    cols_label(

      xbh = 'XBH',
      batting_average = 'BA',
      obp = 'OBP',
      slg = 'SLG',
      ops = 'OPS'
    ) %>% 
    gt_img_rows(
      columns = logo_url, height = 30
    ) %>%
    fmt(
      columns = c(batting_average, obp, slg, ops),
      fns = function(x) {
        formatted <- format(round(x, 3), nsmall = 1)
        gsub("^0", "", formatted)  # Remove leading zero
      }
    ) 
  
  gt_box_score_grob <- gt::as_gtable(gt_box_score, plot = FALSE, text_grob = grid::textGrob)
  
  # ----- Layout ------
  layout_matrix <- matrix(c(
    1
    # 7,7,8,8,
    # 9,9,10,10
  ), ncol = 1, byrow = TRUE)
  
  final_layout <- arrangeGrob(
    grobs = list(
      gt_box_score_grob

}

dev.off()
``` 
## Expected result

The result I expect is the images to be rendered inside the gtable instead of the raw URLs. As I mentioned before, this works perfectly fine on shiny apps.

* [x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue.

## Description

I am using add_significance_stars() with a {gtsummary} table in a Quarto document. When I render in-line output, the p-value footnote looks good. However, when the entire document is rendered as HTML or Microsoft Word, the stars disappear at the footnote, and the text becomes italicized and bold (as in the attached image). I hypothesize that the stars account for a markdown sign for italicized and bold. I am not sure if this is a bug or there is a workaround. 
I reported this issue in [gtsummary's repository](https://github.com/ddsjoberg/gtsummary/issues/2180) but the developer told me that this issue may related to gt.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7162df6a-841c-4688-99fe-3cd37fb70534)

library(gtsummary)
#> Warning: package 'gtsummary' was built under R version 4.4.3

trial |>

```

## Expected result

The asterisks should appear and the texts are not italicized and bold.

title: When character column starts with string suggesting list, and gt::fmt_markdown() enabled, Quarto renders contents twice
description:
## Prework

* [x] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
* [x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue.

## Description

If I pass a data frame with a character column, and that character column starts with strings used for lists in markdown (e.g.  "1. " or "-"), and apply `  gt::fmt_markdown()` to the relevant column, then the contents of each row is repeated twice if I render the table in a Quarto html document. 

If I just render it with `gt`, the issue does not appear e.g. in Rstudio's preview pane. 

Strictly speaking, the issue may not be in `gt` itself, but is seemingly the result of the interaction between `gt`, `pandoc`, and `quarto`, so not sure where best to report. 

In the real world, this happens when I use `gt` to report legal documents with lines occasionally starting with numbered provisions, and I rely on `fmt_markdown` to keep some parts of the text highlighted.  

## Reproducible example

````
---
title: "Test gt render with quarto"
format: html
editor: source
---


```{r}
tibble::tibble(a = c("1. a", 
                     "2. b")) |> 
  gt::gt() |> 
  gt::fmt_markdown(columns = "a")
```


```{r}
tibble::tibble(a = c("- a", 
                     "- b")) |> 
  gt::gt() |> 
  gt::fmt_markdown(columns = "a")
```

````

## Expected result

Expected: when I render the html document with Quarto, I'd expect to see it the same as I see it when I preview `gt`'s results, with text appearing once as given.

title: opt_interactive adds unwanted tab_spanner rules
description:
## Description

Additional spanner lines are added to columns that don't have a spanner title when the interactive form of a gt table is generated.

## Reproducible example

The following example prints a spanner and horizontal rule covering `cyl`, `disp` and `hp` from `mtcars`:

```
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)

mtcars %>%
  slice_head(n = 10) %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  tab_spanner(
    label = 'Engine',
    columns = c(cyl, disp, hp)
  )
```

Here is a visual of the output:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/321f29ef-b774-49be-9871-2f5ee79aa5f4)

If we add `opt_interactive()` in the pipeline, the spanner rules are not as clear:

```
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)

mtcars %>%
  slice_head(n = 10) %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  tab_spanner(
    label = 'Engine',
    columns = c(cyl, disp, hp)
  ) %>% 
  opt_interactive()
```

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/740c3ef1-b43e-4235-ab74-432cfbfdeea6)

At first glance, the spanner rules now span the entire table horizontally. A mild separation between the requested and additional spanner rule is visible. But it's nearly invisible, making the spanner rule useless.

## Expected result

I'd expect the horizontal rules under the `opt_interactive()` interface to match that without the interactive option active. Moreover, the loss of continuity in the display makes the spanner not helpful.

title: Warnings on package load in Positron
description:
## Prework

* [x] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
* [x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue.

## Description

When loading {gt} in Positron the `info_google_font()` function causes the warning **"cannot be translated from 'ANSI_X3.4-1968' to UTF-8, but is valid UTF-8"** to be repeatedly fired. This partly/largely a Positron issue with encoding, and is reported at https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/4539, specifically relating to how R/Ark/Positron is interpreting the information contained in either the `gt:::google_font_tbl` data and/or the resulting `info_google_fonts.rds` object. Posting here in part to flag to others experiencing the issue what the cause is.

This is similar to a previous issue I experienced with {knitr} throwing an ANSI_X3/4-1968 to UFT-8 error. It does not happen in the R GUI or RStudio. Based on the discussion about the previous {knitr} issue, it is also likely that this isn't occurring for all Positron users. A full dump of the Positron debug messages is provided in the issue in that repo.

## Reproducible example

The issue occurs when either loading {gt} via `library(gt)` or a `gt::fun()` type call.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/13682f09-9625-450e-802e-02d431fbb1f3)

This then results in a series of warnings being fired, which after inspection appear to be font designer names (limited to first 10 for brevity):

```
There were 50 or more warnings (use warnings() to see the first 50)
> warnings()
Warning messages:
1: input string 'Juan Pablo del Peral, Huerta Tipográfica' cannot be translated from 'ANSI_X3.4-1968' to UTF-8, but is valid UTF-8
2: input string 'Juan Pablo del Peral, Huerta Tipográfica' cannot be translated from 'ANSI_X3.4-1968' to UTF-8, but is valid UTF-8

After checking this wasn't triggering from any of the {gt} dependencies I searched deeper inside of the {gt} source code since these names weren't coming up on a search of the code on Github itself. This leads me to believe the issue either occurs in the generation of the underlying table/gt object or in the interpretation of the object when it's being loaded. title: Numbered table captions broken
description:
## Description

Up until lately, using the caption argument of gt::gt() worked to get numbered captions when compiling to bookdown::html_document2.

With gt@0.10.0 the following example delivers the expected caption ("Table 1: Cars"). With gt@0.11.1 however, I get "(\#tab:Tab1)Cars".

## Reproducible example

    ---
    title: "Test"
    output: bookdown::html_document2
    date: "2025-01-17"
    ---
    
    ```{r setup, include=FALSE}
    knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = F)
    library(gt)

title: Default latex table position is poor choice in R Markdown
description: ## Prework * [ x] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md). * [ x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue. ## Description In R Markdown, if the `latex_tbl_pos` option is not modified, the table position defaults to `"!t"`. This is not a good default, as it forces the table to the top of the page even when that doesn't make sense. A better default would be `"t"`, which usually puts the table at the top of the page, but might push it to the top of the next page in some circumstances, e.g. on the first page of an article where the article title should be at the top of the first page. ## Reproducible example Run this in R Markdown: ```` --- title: "Mtcars example" output: pdf_document --- ```{r setup, include=FALSE} knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE) library(gt) ``` ## Example Here is some text before the table. ```{r table} head(mtcars) |> gt() sessionInfo() ``` ```` This puts the table above the article title: ## Expected result The table should appear on the next page. This is what happens If `|> tab_options(latex.tbl.pos = "t")` is added to the line generating the table, because LaTeX knows not to put a table before the title. That would be a better default than the current one.

If you write a chunk labeled as a table for cross-references purpose (that is, `#| label: tbl-SOMETHING`), and you output a gt table with a tab spanner, the resulting docx file is invalid.

title: Slow rendering of large tables
description:
## Prework

- [x] Read and abide by **gt**'s [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Search for duplicates among the [existing issues](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues) (both open and closed).

## Proposal

I noticed that certain tables take forever to print, spending most of its time in the little function `rownum_translation()` inside `gt:::build_data()`. Here is a reprex:  

``` r
library(gt)

ncol <- 100
nrow <- 2000
df <- matrix(sample(1:10, ncol*nrow, replace = T), ncol = ncol) |> 
  as.data.frame()

g <- gt(df) |> 
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(color = "red"),
    locations = lapply(1:ncol, \(i) cells_body(rows = df[[i]] > 5, columns = i))
  )

# Profiling (truncated)
Rprof()
dat <- gt:::build_data(g, "html")
Rprof(NULL)
summaryRprof()

#> $by.total

#> "rownum_translation"                 46.86     95.95      0.12     0.25
#> "which"                              40.94     83.82      1.14     2.33
#> "as.numeric"                         38.90     79.65     38.90    79.65
#> (...)
#> 
#> $sampling.time
#> [1] 48.84
```

Indeed, the current `rownum_translation()` seems unneccessarily inefficient, using a for loop to grow a vector:
https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/1e4bae1af102c171a19316bca512db4260592645/R/utils_render_common.R#L65-L79

I believe the entire function body can be replaced with `match(rownum_start, as.numeric(rownames(body)))`. 
On my computer this reduces the runtime of the example from 48 seconds to less than 2 seconds.

I'd be happy to open a PR for this change if you want.

<sup>Created on 2024-11-21 with [reprex v2.1.1](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

title: as_gtable not respecting cols_width in as_gtable when tab_options(table.width = pct(100))?

title: LaTeX tables: column spanner widths are affected by order of the input data
description:
## Prework

* [x] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
* [x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue.

## Description

First, thank you for all the recent efforts to improve LaTeX capabilities! This issue is somewhat related to #1656. 
For tables with a stub and column spanners, the column spanner's width is influenced by the order of the input data.

## Reproducible example

[correct behavior] For the table below, the order of the data columns matches the order of the table columns. Widths are correctly set when rendered to latex:
```
library(gt)
gtcars |> 
  dplyr::select(mfr, model, year, trim) |> 
  dplyr::slice(1:10) |> 
  gt(rowname_col = "mfr") |>
  cols_width(
    mfr ~ pct(55),
    model ~ pct(15),  
    year ~ pct(15),
    trim ~ pct(15)
  ) |>  
  tab_spanner(
    label = "a spanner",
    columns = c(year, trim)
  )
```
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/92b97228-70df-469e-9f5c-4e1a8126c53a)


However, if we move `mfr` (row label) to the last column in the data, the spanner incorrectly inherits the width of the stub column:

```
gtcars |> 
  dplyr::select(model, year, trim, mfr) |>  
  dplyr::slice(1:10) |> 
  gt(rowname_col = "mfr") |>
  cols_width(
    mfr ~ pct(55),
    model ~ pct(15),  
    year ~ pct(15),
    trim ~ pct(15) 
  ) |>  
  tab_spanner(
    label = "a spanner",
    columns = c(year, trim)
  )
 ``` 
 
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/abcdd482-ba70-44af-a11c-011fa7ede94c)

## Expected result

I would expect the spanner widths to be independent of the order of the input data. Tables without spanners and/or stubs seem to work fine regardless of the order of the input data.

title: Border customization (colors & padding)
description:
There are two features that I'm surprised don't extend to table borders (it's quite possible, _and I hope!_ that I'm using them wrong):

1. Padding in margins so that a border doesn't take up the whole cell; an extension of `opt_horizontal_padding` or `opt_vertical_padding`.
2. Ability to use color values from another column to color borders within a specific column using the `from_column` function in the color argument of cell_borders.

For the color-related issue, here is what I attempted and what I recieved:

**SUCCESS**
```
exibble %>%
  gt() %>%
  cols_align(align = "center",
             columns = c("char")) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = list(
      cell_borders(
        sides = c("all"),
        color = c("purple"),
        weight = px(3)
      )
    ),
    locations = list(
      cells_body(
        columns = "char",
        rows = char == "fig"
      )
    )
  )

```

![fig](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ffc325e8-269d-4ad0-82f9-09df5b9da7ee)

**FAILURE**
```
exibble %>%
  mutate(col = case_when(char == "fig" ~ "purple",
                         char == "banana" ~ "yellow",
                         TRUE ~ "white")) %>%
  gt() %>%
  cols_align(align = "center",
             columns = c("char")) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = list(
      cell_borders(
        sides = c("all"),
        color = from_column(col),
        weight = px(3)
      )
    ),
    locations = list(
      cells_body(
        columns = "char",
        rows = !is.na(col)
      )
    )
  )

```

Meanwhile, re: my first question, how can I get borders that look like the orange ones (instead of the black ones that wrap the whole cell)...?

![Rplot_amended](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/237b7a36-84c8-48af-9579-2caf82358a30)

title: More leeway in defining how footnotes are rendered
description:
I have [devised a way](https://github.com/ddsjoberg/gtsummary/issues/2047#issuecomment-2439880248) to print a newline in latex output through the use of makecell, but now I need to control how [the footnote is printed](https://github.com/ddsjoberg/gtsummary/issues/2047#issuecomment-2440385429).

In particular, this  is the  latex output I currently obtain:
```
\makecell{\textbf{Drug A} \\ N = 98}\textsuperscript{\textit{1}}
```

I would like to put the footnote inside the makecell.

But I see that `opt_footnote_spec` has [limited capabilities](https://gt.rstudio.com/reference/opt_footnote_spec.html) and wouldn't allow me to do that.

description:

## Description

THe function `as_latex` is converting `\` into `\\textbackslash{}`, `{` into `\{` and does other latex-escaping that can't be avoided

## Reproducible example

* [X] Post a [minimal reproducible example](https://www.tidyverse.org/help/) so the maintainer can troubleshoot the problems you identify. A reproducible example is:
    * [X] **Runnable**: post enough R code and data so any onlooker can create the error on their own computer.
    * [X] **Minimal**: reduce runtime wherever possible and remove complicated details that are irrelevant to the issue at hand.
    * [X] **Readable**: format your code according to the [tidyverse style guide](https://style.tidyverse.org/).

```
library(gt)
gtcars |>
  dplyr::select(mfr, model, msrp) |>
  dplyr::slice(1:5) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "\\textbf{gtcars}",
    subtitle = md("`gtcars` is an R dataset")
  ) |>
  as_latex() |>
  as.character()
```

```
"\\begin{table}[!t]\n\\caption*{\n{\\large \\textbackslash{}textbf\\{gtcars\\}} \\\\ \n{\\small \\texttt{gtcars} is an R dataset}\n} \n\\fontsize{12.0pt}{14.4pt}\\selectfont\n\\begin{tabular*}{\\linewidth}{@{\\extracolsep{\\fill}}llr}\n\\toprule\nmfr & model & msrp \\\\ \n\\midrule\\addlinespace[2.5pt]\nFord & GT & 447000 \\\\ \nFerrari & 458 Speciale & 291744 \\\\ \nFerrari & 458 Spider & 263553 \\\\ \nFerrari & 458 Italia & 233509 \\\\ \nFerrari & 488 GTB & 245400 \\\\ \n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular*}\n\\end{table}\n"

As you can see, `\` was converted into `\\textbackslash{}`

There should be a `escape` option, like there is for [knitr::kable](https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/knitr/versions/1.48/topics/kable), that prevents escaping.

Yes, I know I can use `md("**my title**")`, but my aim is to output raw LaTeX code that do not have a corresponding Markdown code, in particular for [newlines in cell outputs](https://github.com/ddsjoberg/gtsummary/issues/2047) for example.

title: gt tables as grid tables - patchwork - only works if plot is on the left
description:
The gt tables as grid tables functionality is great.  
However, it appears to *only* work if the plot is on the left, as per the example in the [blog](https://posit.co/blog/everything-new-thats-in-gt-0-11-0/).

```
pizza_gtable <- 
    pizzaplace |>
    dplyr::filter(type %in% c("chicken", "supreme")) |>
    dplyr::group_by(type, size) |>
    dplyr::summarize(
        sold = dplyr::n(),
        income = sum(price),
        .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    gt(
        rowname_col = "size",
        groupname_col = "type",
        row_group_as_column = TRUE
    ) |>
    tab_header(title = "Pizza Sales in 2015") |>
    fmt_integer(columns = sold) |>
    fmt_currency(columns = income) |>
    summary_rows(
        fns = list(label = "All Sizes", fn = "sum"),
        side = c("top"),
        fmt = list(
            ~ fmt_integer(., columns = sold),
            ~ fmt_currency(., columns = income)
        )
    ) |>
    grand_summary_rows(
        columns = c("sold", "income"),
        fns = Sum ~ sum(.),
        fmt = list(
            ~ fmt_integer(., columns = sold),
            ~ fmt_currency(., columns = income)
        )
    ) |>
    tab_options(summary_row.background.color = "gray98") |>
    tab_stub_indent(
        rows = everything(),
        indent = 2
    ) |>
    as_gtable()
```
```
pizza_plot <-
    pizzaplace |>
    dplyr::mutate(date = as.Date(date)) |>
    dplyr::filter(type %in% c("chicken", "supreme")) |>
    dplyr::group_by(date, type) |>
    dplyr::summarize(
        sold = dplyr::n(),
        .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    ggplot() +
    geom_line(aes(x = date, y = sold, color = type, group = type)) +
    facet_wrap(~type, nrow = 2) +
    scale_x_date(date_labels = "%b", breaks = "1 month") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    labs(x = "", y = "Pizzas Sold")
```
```
pizza_plot + pizza_gtable
```
This produces the graph and table side by side as per the blog

## Question

However, if I reverse the order, and want the table on the left and the plot on the right, I get a NULL response and nothing is generated:

```
pizza_gtable + pizza_plot
```

![gt grid table order](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8d3bdca7-e711-417c-ab7e-f10e6085b721)

Is this intended functionality to only work in the specified order?
If possible, I can envision sometimes wanting the chart on the left and the graph on the right.

title: allow ... to be passed to `rmarkdown::pandoc_convert` in `gt_save_docx` (`gt_save`)
description:
At the moment the structuration of `gt_save` forbids passing arguments to the inner `rmarkdown::pandoc_convert` through `...`. (The `...` is unused in the intermediate function `gt_save_docx`.)

Yet this would be in my opinion a low-cost way solve a bunch of issues. In my case it would allow generating landscape tables with a landscape ref doc. If nice use cases emerge, then proper arguments may be discussed in the high level function `gt_save` later.

title: Using `fmt_markdown()` on a factor prints the numeric factor level when the output format is HTML
description:
## Prework * [x] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md). * [x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue. ## Description When `fmt_markdown()` is used on a column that contains factor data, it prints the numeric levels of the factor and not their text labels. This only happens when outputting to HTML, and not with other output formats like latex. I believe this is because the `md()` function, which is used for HTML output, replaces the class of the vector, meaning a factor would lose its factor class and be assigned a new class over its underlying integer type. I believe this could be fixed by having `md()` first convert its input to character, then reclass it. I'd be happy to submit a PR if it would be helpful. ## Reproducible example ``` r library(gt) gt(data.frame(x = factor("TEST"))) ```
x
TEST
``` r gt(data.frame(x = factor("TEST"))) |> fmt_markdown() ```
x
1
``` r gt(data.frame(x = factor("TEST"))) |> fmt_markdown() |> as_latex() |> as.character() |> cat() #> \begingroup #> \fontsize{12.0pt}{14.4pt}\selectfont #> \begin{longtable}{c} #> \toprule #> x \\ #> \midrule\addlinespace[2.5pt] #> TEST \\ #> \bottomrule #> \end{longtable} #> \endgroup ``` Created on 2024-09-17 with [reprex v2.1.0](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) ## Expected result The HTML output should have included the character label for `x` ("TEST") rather than its numeric level (1). - [x ] Search for duplicates among the [existing issues](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues) (both open and closed).

## Proposal

Now gt generates only header of the table from the empty dataframe.
It would be nice to have an option to generate empty table in the way R studio shows empty dataframe - header with message in the body "No data available in table" (or preferably custom message).

I generate many automatic crosscheck dataframes that sometimes are empty. 
(like samples that have combinations of features that shouldn't be present in dataset - potential errors in measurements or data collection).
I automate printing reports from these crosschecks.
When generating pdf, table with only header looks like error in LaTex - it suggests that something is not rendered there properly.
Message in the body "This query returned 0 results" would make it look much more not error-like.

Radek

title: When `pattern` manages NAs in `fmt_icon() |> cols_merge()`, `NA` gets repeatedly appended to the value.
description:
## Prework

* [x] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
* [x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue.

## Description

After passing a table to `fmt_icon()`, if I then `cols_merge()` with a pattern that takes into account NAs, a very large number of `NA` get appended to cells that *don't* have NAs.

## Reproducible example
``` r
library(gt)

data.frame(
  x = c("dice-one", "dice-two", "dice-three"),
  y = c("dice-one", NA, "dice-three")
) |> 
  gt() ->
  base_table

```
### This works
Without using `fmt_icon()`, this works as expected.

```r
base_table |> 
  cols_merge(
    columns = everything(),
    pattern = "({1}<< {2}>>)"
  )
```
![blog_-_drafting_-_RStudio](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ccecf2a7-5f10-4aa7-9a6e-001bd2472bc9)

### This does not work
It also takes a *while* to run, I assume because of all the NAs that are getting appended.

```r
base_table |> 
  fmt_icon() |> 
  cols_merge(
    columns = everything(),
    pattern = "({1}<< {2}>>)"
  )
```
![blog_-_drafting_-_RStudio](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/924ed134-1b10-4866-a71f-6cc6094baf20)

Inspecting the html output for the first row, there were 49,547 `NA`s appended to the cell.

## Expected result

I expected output similar to the working example, but with the icons instead of the names of the icons.

title: The `extract_body()` function extracts a df with stub and hidden columns
description:
The intent of `extract_body()` is to provide a dataframe of body cells with a chosen level of rendering applied to those cells (e.g., formatting, text transformations, etc.). However, it should match the body of rendered table and right now it:

- includes hidden columns
- has no option to exclude non-body cells (i.e., stub cells)

It can be useful to have stub information and the stub can be formatted. But it would be useful to omit the stub cells via an option.

description:
I have been generating tables using my own function in R and saving them with `gt::gtsave()`. Previously, I was able to save the output in the desired dimensions, but recently, the saved tables are not maintaining the same size and aspect ratio. Here’s the relevant part of my code:

    data |>
      polioanalytica::create_gt_table(
        drop_date_col = FALSE
      ) |>
      gt::gtsave(
        paste0(plots_path, "/overview_table.png"),
        vwidth = 3650, vheight = 1800
      )

This code used to produce a table image with correct dimensions similar to [this screenshot][1]. However, now the output looks more like [this one][2], with the layout compressed and the dimensions not preserved.

With no success, I’ve tried adjusting the `vwidth`, `vheight`, `expand` and `zoom` parameters in `gt::gtsave()`. As well as ensuring no changes have been made to my package that could affect table rendering - table looks good when plotting in `rstudio`.

**Questions:**

• What might be causing the saved table to not maintain the correct dimensions?
• Are there any specific settings or parameters within `gt::gtsave()` that I should consider adjusting?
• Could this be related to changes in the underlying gt package, and if so, how can I address it?

Any insights or suggestions would be greatly appreciated! This issue only started happening today, wasn't an issue last week.
