title: Using cur_column() as a way to reference another dataframe or list in summary rows.
description:
I am trying to create summary rows with reference to another data source.

Let's say we have df results that I want to print with summary rows and a dataframe containing different reference values for each column:
```
results <- data.frame(level = c("LQC", "LQC", "LQC", "LQC", "LQC", "LQC", "LQC", "LQC", "LQC", "HQC", "HQC", "HQC", "HQC", "HQC", "HQC", "HQC", "HQC", "HQC"),
                     source = c("A", "A", "A", "B", "B", "B", "C", "C", "C", "A", "A", "A", "B", "B", "B", "C", "C", "C"),
                     val_A = c(30.1822, 33.0850, 32.2722, 27.7168, 29.1946, 29.1808, 33.1962, 32.6243, 31.7900, 1799.5074, 2012.0351, 2054.0858, 1956.2820, 1990.6278, 2081.3730, 1955.4075, 2073.8068, 2076.9238),
                     val_B = c(3.6880, 3.8021, 3.5833, 3.4146, 2.7805, 3.1428, 2.9596, 4.0376, 3.9008, 362.4901, 331.9178, 337.8255, 324.2157, 336.1455, 342.8927, 317.3914, 334.1520, 338.8625))

reference <- data.frame(level  = c("LQC", "HQC"),
                  val_A = c(30, 2000),
                  val_B = c(3, 400))
```

I need summary rows grouped by level and source.
In summary I need accuracy, which will be: mean of the group divided by reference value from different df (or list) multiplied by 100

My idea was to make separate tables for each level and to use `cur_column()` like this:

```
results_LQC <- results |> 
  filter(level == "LQC") |> 
  select(-level)
  
reference_LQC <- reference |> 
  filter(level == "LQC") |> 
  select(-level)

res_LQC_tab <- results_LQC |> 
  group_by(source) |>
  gt()|> 
  summary_rows(columns = matches("val_"),
               fns = list(id = "mean", label = "Mean", fn = "mean"),
               fmt = ~ fmt_number(., decimals = 2)) |> 
  summary_rows(columns = matches("val_"),
               fns = list(id = "acc", label = "Accuracy", fn = ~mean(.)/reference_LQC[[cur_column()]]*100),
               fmt = ~ fmt_number(., decimals = 2, pattern = "{x}%"))|>
  summary_rows(columns = matches("val_"),
               fns = list(id = "cv", label = "CV", fn = ~sd(.)/mean(.)*100),
               fmt = ~ fmt_number(., decimals = 2, pattern = "{x}%"))|> 
  fmt_number(columns = matches("val_"),
             decimals = 2)
```

Unfortunately, `cur_column` does not work in gt.

I think it would be useful to have an easy way to reference data from another df when creating summary rows.
And to make this reference dependent on the column being summarized.

Ideal solution would also allow to reference row according to the group that is summarized...

Regards, Radek

title: fmt_date (and vec_fmt_date) are especially slow (bigD::fdt is not vectorised)
description:
## Prework

- [x] Read and abide by **gt**'s [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Search for duplicates among the [existing issues](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues) (both open and closed).

## Proposal

`fmt_date` is very slow when applied to columns of any length (e.g. see example of 100 cells below)

Possible proposals:

- change bigD so that it doesn't iterate over the input vector(s) - see loop on https://github.com/rstudio/bigD/blob/8fe7727a0c394bd6480c48072f104d14c91058c9/R/fdt.R#L963 
   - this might also require changing fmt_date/bigD to allow timezone to be specified at a vector level?
- change bigD so it doesn't perform so many unnecessary formatting operations 
    - e.g. when `y` is present then it seems like there are 8 calls to `ug_sub` which in turn means 8 calls to `dt_y*` functions plus (on my Windows machine at least) lots of unicode encoding operations
        - the `{y}` calls https://github.com/rstudio/bigD/blob/8fe7727a0c394bd6480c48072f104d14c91058c9/R/fdt.R#L1171C4-L1181C6
        - the `ug_sub` implementation - https://github.com/rstudio/bigD/blob/8fe7727a0c394bd6480c48072f104d14c91058c9/R/fdt.R#L1539C1-L1554C2
- provide an alternative fmt_date function to allow gt users to switch date formatting away from bigD
- provide a performance warning for anyone using fmt_date on more than a few columns/rows

Possibly might also need to look at `fmt_datetime` as that uses bigD for some formatting (but not all)

## Example 

```
devtools::load_all()
library(tidyverse)
library(tictoc)
library(gt)

demo_length <- 100
my_table <-
  tibble(
    Name = # generate random names
      stringi::stri_rand_strings(demo_length, 10),
    Population = round(runif(demo_length, 100000000, 1000000000)),
    Score = runif(demo_length, 0, 1),
    Date = lubridate::now() + runif(demo_length, -1000, 1000)
  )

tictoc::tic("fmt_")
html1 <- my_table |> 
  gt() |> 
  fmt_number(columns = "Population") |>
  fmt_date(columns = "Date", date_style = "m_day_year" ) |> 
  gt:::as.tags.gt_tbl()
tictoc::toc()

tictoc::tic("vec_fmt_")
html2 <- my_table |> 
  mutate(Date = vec_fmt_date(Date, date_style = "m_day_year")) |>
  gt() |> 
  fmt_number(columns = "Population") |>
  gt:::as.tags.gt_tbl()
tictoc::toc()

tictoc::tic("mutate")
html3 <- my_table |>
  mutate(Date = format(Date, "%b %d, %y")) |>
  gt() |> 
  fmt_number(columns = "Population") |>
  gt:::as.tags.gt_tbl()
tictoc::toc()
```  

This formats only 100 date cells and gives output:
```
fmt_: 1.81 sec elapsed
vec_fmt_: 1.67 sec elapsed
mutate: 0.08 sec elapsed
```

profvis shows `bigD::fdt` dominating the time spent in the slower cases:
![image](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/assets/533662/6d85889d-c46b-4984-ba70-136ff2e1dfa1)
![image](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/assets/533662/6ec7152c-9fc6-4463-a282-ec28f6ab73e7)


**Note:** This situation is even worse in interactive where #1528 multiplies the problem

title: Performance of `fmt_*` in Interactive Tables
description: ## Prework - [x] Read and abide by **gt**'s [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Search for duplicates among the [existing issues](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues) (both open and closed). ## Proposal Performance discussion as followup from #1524 Interactive is definitely slower than "standard"... but our big problems were around these `packageVersion` calls (still not entirely sure why they were so slow...) and with some markdown columns. This is (a much tidied up version of) the script I was using to debug our perf issues... ``` library(gt) library(tidyverse) library(tictoc) townyBase <- towny |> dplyr::select(name, starts_with("population")) townyPlain <- function() { townyBase |> dplyr::mutate( Link = glue::glue("{htmltools::htmlEscape(townyBase$name)}") ) } townyHtml <- function() { townyPlain() |> dplyr::mutate( Link = purrr::map(Link, ~ .x |> gt::html()) ) } townyTag <- function() { townyBase |> dplyr::mutate( Link = purrr::map(name, ~ { htmltools::tags$a(href= glue::glue("https://google.com?q={htmltools::urlEncodePath(.x)}"), .x) }) ) } townyTagHtml <- function() { townyTag() |> dplyr::mutate( Link = purrr::map(Link, ~ .x |> as.character() |> gt::html()) ) } townyMd <- function() { townyBase |> dplyr::mutate( Link = glue::glue("[{name}](https://google.com?q={htmltools::urlEncodePath(name)})") ) } townyMd2 <- function() { townyMd() |> dplyr::mutate( Link = purrr::map(Link, ~ .x |> gt::md()) ) } do_timed_call <- function(label, data, extras, final_opt) { tictoc::tic(label) tictoc::tic(paste0(label, "_data")) fetched <- data() tictoc::toc() tictoc::tic(paste0(label, "_creating")) table <- fetched |> gt() |> fmt_integer() |> cols_label_with(fn = function(x) sub("population_", "", x)) |> cols_width( name ~ px(200) ) |> tab_header( title = "Populations of Municipalities", subtitle = "Census values from 1996 to 2021." ) |> tab_source_note(source_note = md("Data taken from the `towny` dataset.")) |> extras() |> final_opt() tictoc::toc() tictoc::tic(paste0(label, "_rendering")) html <- table |> gt:::as.tags.gt_tbl() tictoc::toc() tictoc::toc() list( table = table, html = html ) } p1 <- do_timed_call( "plain", townyPlain, function(tab) { tab |> fmt_passthrough("Link", escape = FALSE) }, identity ) p2 <- do_timed_call( "plain interactive", townyPlain, function(tab) { tab |> fmt_passthrough("Link", escape = FALSE) }, opt_interactive ) p3 <- do_timed_call( "html", townyHtml, identity, identity ) p4 <- do_timed_call( "html interactive", townyHtml, identity, opt_interactive ) p5 <- do_timed_call( "md", townyMd, function(tab) { tab |> fmt_markdown("Link") }, identity ) p6 <- do_timed_call( "md interactive", townyMd, function(tab) { tab |> fmt_markdown("Link") }, opt_interactive ) p7 <- do_timed_call( "md2", townyMd2, identity, identity ) p8 <- do_timed_call( "md2 interactive", townyMd2, identity, opt_interactive ) ``` Output here is: ``` plain_data: 0.05 sec elapsed plain_creating: 0.06 sec elapsed plain_rendering: 0.37 sec elapsed plain: 0.48 sec elapsed plain interactive_data: 0.04 sec elapsed plain interactive_creating: 0.06 sec elapsed plain interactive_rendering: 1.26 sec elapsed plain interactive: 1.36 sec elapsed html_data: 0.08 sec elapsed html_creating: 0.05 sec elapsed html_rendering: 0.4 sec elapsed html: 0.53 sec elapsed html interactive_data: 0.05 sec elapsed html interactive_creating: 0.06 sec elapsed html interactive_rendering: 1.47 sec elapsed html interactive: 1.58 sec elapsed md_data: 0.03 sec elapsed md_creating: 0.04 sec elapsed md_rendering: 3.06 sec elapsed md: 3.13 sec elapsed md interactive_data: 0.03 sec elapsed md interactive_creating: 0.09 sec elapsed **md interactive_rendering: 23.57 sec elapsed** md interactive: 23.69 sec elapsed md2_data: 0.03 sec elapsed md2_creating: 0.03 sec elapsed md2_rendering: 0.36 sec elapsed md2: 0.42 sec elapsed md2 interactive_data: 0.04 sec elapsed md2 interactive_creating: 0.05 sec elapsed md2 interactive_rendering: 1.72 sec elapsed md2 interactive: 1.81 sec elapsed ``` The slowest call by far was `p6`/`'md interactive` which uses `fmt_markdown` - it's 23 seconds compared to the sub 2 seconds for `p8`/`md2` rendering which uses `md()` for rendering the markdown text... The profiler suggested that `render_formats/md_to_html` was doing something (looping?) which was much slower/heavier than `migrate_unformatted_to_html`: | fmt_markdown | md | | ----------- | ---- | | 10x slower | "ok" | | ![image](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/assets/533662/9b563838-3d34-410f-9b06-fd5ae9e6fd2c) | ![image](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/assets/533662/1b93b763-5aa6-40f2-9bd5-33143895808f) |

description:

## Description

We've got one app in test where we were seeing very slow interactive gt rendering times.

I believe the majority of this slowness came from markdown cell rendering - and when I've tried simpler reproduction projects I've generated some profvis outputs that demonstrated this:
![image](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/assets/533662/0bf6eb45-3a0c-40e5-8f29-ff461dbe1fd6)

However... in my real project, profvis is pointing to `utils::packageVersion` as being a significant performance issue - e.g. see:
![image](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/assets/533662/ee40b2a7-d49a-42ad-b425-1507af1614e3)

... but I haven't yet gotten similar results in my test repro projects (yet). I'm not sure why this is - but I'll see if I can work out why "soon" - e.g. perhaps something to do with renv (used in my real project but not in my test repro one)

I'm pausing investigating this for a moment now - but thought I'd open this draft issue/PR now - is this change something gt would be interested in?

## Reproducible example

* [ ] Post a [minimal reproducible example](https://www.tidyverse.org/help/) so the maintainer can troubleshoot the problems you identify. A reproducible example is:

title: Include a `text_pattern` arg for `fmt_image()`
description: Most formatting functions include a `pattern` argument to allow for decoration of the formatted values with string literals. This is missing in `fmt_image()` though the inclusion of a `text_pattern` arg (name changed to help users differentiate this from the `file_pattern` arg) would be useful. With this, we can add text around the image(s).

title: Incorporate static/hoverable value labels on single-bar nanoplots
description: Single-bar nanoplots are now functional but unlike other nanoplots, we don’t have values ascribed to the bars. But we *should*. Many bar plots in tables display a static value that is attached to the bar in some way. Some value should be available but an open question is whether to, by default, (1) display on hover or (2) display always. This can be answered perhaps after some exploration but this exercise may eventually lead to exposing an option for this that works across all nanoplots.

title: Setting cols_width causes column to "disappear"
description:
## Description

I can set the column widths of all but one column. When I set the last column width a column disappears from the table. The reprex and images below will make this more understandable.

## Reproducible example

I have the following tibble named `tdat ` that has columns (Model, name, err_Treated, ..., coverage_Control)

**Model,	name,	err_Treated,	err_Control,	width90_Treated,	width90_Control,	coverage_Treated,	coverage_Control**
Match, A, 12, 8, 5 ,36, 0.91, 0.82
Match, B,	5,	6,	29,	25,	0.87,	0.81
Match, C,	10,	9,	42,	41,	0.79,	0.82
BART, A,	7,	7,	37,	37,	0.89,	0.87
BART, B,	6,	5,	26,	26,	0.87,	0.9
BART, C,	9,	9,	49,	48,	0.93	,0.87

(sorry - I don't know of a better way to reprex this)

I use the following code to create and format a gt() table:
 ``` r
  tbl_cover <-
    tdat |>
    gt(groupname_col = "name") |>
    cols_label(
      err_Treated = "Treated",
      err_Control = "Control",
      width90_Treated = "Treated",
      width90_Control = "Control",
      coverage_Treated = "Treated",
      coverage_Control = "Control"
    ) |>
    fmt_percent(columns = starts_with("cover"), decimals = 0) |>
    # tab_header(str_replace_all(s, "_", " ")) |>
    tab_style(
      cell_text(weight = "bold", align = "left"),
      locations = list(cells_row_groups(), cells_title())
    ) |>
    tab_style(cell_text(align = "center"),
              locations = list(
                cells_body(columns = everything()),
                cells_column_labels(columns = everything())
              )) |>
    tab_style(cell_text(style = "italic"),
              locations = list(
                cells_column_labels(columns = matches("width|cover|err")),
                cells_body(columns = Model)
              )) |>
    tab_style(cell_text(align = "left", indent = px(25)),
              locations = cells_body(columns = Model)) |>
    tab_style(cell_text(color = "transparent"),
              locations = cells_column_labels(columns = Model)) |>
    cols_width(
      # err_Treated ~ px(100),
      err_Control ~ px(100),
      starts_with("cover") ~ px(100),
      starts_with("width") ~ px(100),
      Model ~ px(230)
    ) |>
    tab_spanner(label = "Mean Abs. Error",
                columns = starts_with("err")) |>
    tab_spanner(label = "Interval Width",
                columns = starts_with("width")) |>
    tab_spanner(label = "Coverage",
                columns = starts_with("cover")) |>
    tab_style(cell_text(weight = "bold"),
              locations = cells_column_spanners()) |>
    tab_options(table_body.hlines.color = "#e6e6e6",
                row_group.as_column = TRUE)
```

<sup>Created on 2023-12-17 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

This produces the expected table:
![image](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/assets/25011558/6ab4a470-604d-4066-b278-f4243a871281)

Now I uncomment the line: `# err_Treated ~ px(100)`. In other words, I now assign a width to that final column. Note that it doesn't matter which column is chosen as the last column to assign a width to. The point is that if I assign widths to all-but-one, it works. But when I assign the final width, my last column disappears.

## Expected result

I expected to see a table almost identical to the one posted above, but with the err_Treated column 100 pixels wide.

Instead, the last column of the table disappears (see below):

title: No space between table and footnote in LaTeX if table has a label and caption
description:
## Prework * [x] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md). * [x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue. ## Description When using a table caption and a table footnote in LaTeX, there is no space between the bottom of a table and the footnote because {gt} forces the space to be 0 (see also this by @cscheid at https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/7861#issuecomment-1850309904) ## Reproducible example In this `.qmd` file there's a table with no caption or label: ````qmd --- title: "Table stuff" format: pdf: keep-tex: true --- ```{r} #| echo: false x <- matrix(1:15, nrow = 1) colnames(x) <- LETTERS[1:15] as.data.frame(x) |> gt::gt() |> gt::tab_footnote( footnote = "Here's a note that has good spacing with the bottom of the table", locations = gt::cells_body(columns = D, rows = 1) ) ``` ```` It generates a table like this, with good spacing between the bottom of the table and the top of the footnote:

When adding a caption and label, though, like this: ````qmd --- title: "Table stuff" format: pdf: keep-tex: true --- ```{r} #| label: tbl-testing-caption #| tbl-cap: "Testing" #| echo: false x <- matrix(1:15, nrow = 1) colnames(x) <- LETTERS[1:15] as.data.frame(x) |> gt::gt() |> gt::tab_footnote( footnote = "Here's a note that's really close to the bottom of the table", locations = gt::cells_body(columns = D, rows = 1) ) ``` ```` There's no space between the note and the table:

That's because in the emitted LaTeX, the `\LTpost` command is set to 0 here https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/0db800bf7eeeb2568c1c4423fdcc47412026d6f1/R/utils_render_latex.R#L122-L132 My current hacky workaround is to use etoolbox to insert some vertical space before all minipage environments, since that's where the notes are inserted: ```latex \usepackage{etoolbox} \AtBeginEnvironment{minipage}{\vspace{\baselineskip}} ``` It works okay: ````qmd --- title: "Table stuff" format: pdf: keep-tex: true include-in-header: text: | % Add a little bit of extra space above minipages % for gt table footnotes \usepackage{etoolbox} \AtBeginEnvironment{minipage}{\vspace{\baselineskip}} --- ```{r} #| label: tbl-testing-caption #| tbl-cap: "Testing" #| echo: false x <- matrix(1:15, nrow = 1) colnames(x) <- LETTERS[1:15] as.data.frame(x) |> gt::gt() |> gt::tab_footnote( footnote = "Here's a note that's not close anymore", locations = gt::cells_body(columns = D, rows = 1) ) ``` ````

There's actually a little too much space there now, since I just used `\baselineskip` and didn't hunt around inside the {gt} source to see what the actual regular value is supposed to be. This workaround is okay, but a little heavy handed, since it modifies all minipages and not just table footnotes ## Session info This is with {gt} 0.10.0 from CRAN.
sessionInfo() ``` R version 4.3.1 (2023-06-16) Platform: aarch64-apple-darwin20 (64-bit) Running under: macOS Sonoma 14.1.2 Matrix products: default BLAS: /System/Library/Frameworks/Accelerate.framework/Versions/A/Frameworks/vecLib.framework/Versions/A/libBLAS.dylib LAPACK: /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.3-arm64/Resources/lib/libRlapack.dylib; LAPACK version 3.11.0 locale: [1] en_US.UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8/C/en_US.UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8 time zone: America/New_York tzcode source: internal attached base packages: [1] stats graphics grDevices utils datasets methods base other attached packages: [1] gt_0.10.0 loaded via a namespace (and not attached): [1] digest_0.6.33 utf8_1.2.3 R6_2.5.1 fastmap_1.1.1 tidyselect_1.2.0 magrittr_2.0.3 glue_1.6.2 [8] tibble_3.2.1 htmltools_0.5.6.1 pkgconfig_2.0.3 dplyr_1.1.3 generics_0.1.3 lifecycle_1.0.3 xml2_1.3.4 [15] cli_3.6.1 fansi_1.0.5 vctrs_0.6.3 compiler_4.3.1 rstudioapi_0.15.0 tools_4.3.1 rsthemes_0.4.0 [22] pillar_1.9.0 rlang_1.1.1 ```

title: PDF Output does not support background colors
description:
## Description

PDF output does not include background colors of cells (text colors are not affected by this). The problem seems to be an underlying issue with how {webshot2} aka {chromote} aka Chrome browsers print documents. It seems that by default browsers will not include background CSS (at least that's what this [SO answer](https://stackoverflow.com/a/11243389/13679911) says). 

I can confirm that when I want to print a {gt} table from Chrome manually, I will not get background colors. It is only when I activate the "Background graphics" option in the print window of Chrome, then I get my desired output. So a solution would be to let {chromote} know that it should use that setting when printing something. I couldn't find a way to pass any meaningful option like that to `gtsave()` to get the desired result.

## Reproducible example

``` r
library(gt)
tbl <- towny |> 
  dplyr::slice(1:5) |> 
  dplyr::select(name, land_area_km2) |> 
  gt() |> 
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(color = 'dodgerblue4'),
    locations = cells_body(columns = 1)
  ) |> 
  tab_style(
    style = list(
      cell_fill(color = 'dodgerblue4'),
      cell_text(color = 'white', weight = 'bold')
    ),
    locations = cells_body(columns = 2)
  )
gtsave(tbl, 'img.png') # Works fine
gtsave(tbl, 'img.pdf') # No Background colors
```

title: Add `as_typst()` function to support styled tables in `typst` Quarto output format
description:
## Prework

- [X] Read and abide by **gt**'s [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [X] Search for duplicates among the [existing issues](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues) (both open and closed).

## Proposal

This may be premature given that the `typst` format is pre-release but I figured I'd offer the suggestion now that a `as_typst()` function that supports or enables custom table formatting when using the `typst` Quarto output format could be a great addition.

Some background via [the Quarto documentation](https://quarto.org/docs/prerelease/1.4/typst.html):

>Quarto v1.4 includes support for the typst output format. [Typst](https://github.com/typst/typst) is a new open-source markup-based typesetting system that is designed to be as powerful as LaTeX while being much easier to learn and use.

The Quarto repo already has a related issue for incorporating the [typst-tablex](https://github.com/PgBiel/typst-tablex) library for table formatting: https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/6811 Not sure if that would make a `as_typst()` function unnecessary or if the two could work in concert.

title: Improve docs for `gt::cell_text()` size argument + add support for units class size inputs
description:
## Prework

- [X] Read and abide by **gt**'s [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [X] Search for duplicates among the [existing issues](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues) (both open and closed)

I spotted some issues on text sizes but nothing exactly like this. #1098 highlights some related issues with Word file exports.

## Proposal

I was trouble-shooting some table style issues with a gt table in Microsoft Word and realized that the size parameter for `gt::cell_text()` is more complicated and flexible than I had realized.

When I specify a numeric size and output the table to Microsoft Word using [`{gto}`](https://github.com/GSK-Biostatistics/gto/), the font size in points is always half the size specified, e.g. `size = 24` translates to a font size of 12 pt in the output Word document.

When I specify a size using the `px(12)` helper *or* a character string of digits with no units, e.g. "12" the output table has no font size (effectively 0) and the formatted text is invisible until the size is adjusted.

When I specify a size with a character string that includes units, e.g. "12pt" or "1in", it works exactly as expected—but the option to use a string with the unit included is not mentioned in the documentation as an option. Pixel units as a string "24px" do not work (similar to using the `px()` function).

At a minimum, I think it may be helpful to add the option to use a string with units to the `gt::cell_text()` documentation and add a link to `grid::unit()` for the handy reference on size to point translations.

Potentially, it would also be great to add support for `units` class inputs (similar to ggplot2) but that may be a bigger lift so I could submit it as a separate issue as a longer-term option.

title: Is opt_interactive() compatible with blastula/email packages?
description:
Hi all,

I'm building a tool to deliver local economic data updates to people at my university via email. gt tables without interactivity work well with the `blastula` package, but the tables I'm generating are 36 rows and there's four tables per email. The pagination options in `opt_interactive` render in Rstudio, but not in the viewer tab or in test emails. Here's my code:

```
gt_test_df <- gt(test_df) %>% 
  tab_header(
    title = "Header",
    subtitle = "Source subtitel"
  )
  
opt_test<- opt_interactive(
  gt_test_df,
  active = TRUE,
  use_pagination = TRUE,
  use_pagination_info = TRUE,
  use_sorting = FALSE,
  use_compact_mode = TRUE,
  use_page_size_select = TRUE,
  page_size_values = c(12, 24, 36)
)

blastula::email <- compose_email(
 body = "Test body",
opt_test,
 footer = "This tool is in beta"
)
```

Is it possible to render an interactive table like this in an email? Static tables work but take up a lot of space, and I'd like to save the end user the hassle of downloading an html file.

title: Add visual examples of `opt_stylize()` styles to docs
description:
## Prework

- [x] Read and abide by **gt**'s [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Search for duplicates among the [existing issues](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues) (both open and closed).

## Proposal

`opt_stylize()` has 6 different styles available, but there is no way of knowing what each style looks like without experimenting with the `style` argument. It would be useful to be able to know what each style looks like without needing to iterate through styles locally, similar to how the ggplot2 docs have [visual examples](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/ggtheme.html#ref-examples) of what its built-in themes look like.

I propose either adding these inline to the documentation for `opt_stylize()`, or creating a vignette that has an example of each style.

title: `rows_add()` creates an incorrect stub
description:
## Prework

* [x] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
* [x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue.

## Description

`rows_add()` doesn't handle the rowname and the group correctly.

## Reproducible example

``` r
library(gt)

df <- tibble::tibble(row = "a", group = "g", x = 1)
add_before <- df |>
  tibble::add_row(x = 1) |>
  gt(rowname_col = "row", groupname_col = "group")
add_after <- df |>
  gt(rowname_col = "row", groupname_col = "group") %>% 
  rows_add(x = 1)

title: nanoplot returns Error with LaTeX output
description:
## Description

Nanoplots are seemingly not implemented for LaTeX output, and write HTML to the .tex file. Obviously, this returns in an error when compiling to PDF:

More generally, LaTeX output does seem to be weak. Please note this in your documentation, which only states that LaTeX output is a feature. I do understand the difficulties of LaTeX, but false promises are frustrating.

## Reproducible example

I included the examples from the package documentation as a chunk in an rmarkdown document. See attached (I had to change the extension to upload).

## Expected result

The ramarkdown table correctly shows the table with nanoplot when compiled to HTML. When compiled to LaTeX, the tex file does not compile because HTML code with styling has been dumped to the output.


End
[gt_test.txt](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/files/12866645/gt_test.txt)
 the reproducible example with a call to `sessionInfo()` in the same session (e.g. `reprex(session_info = TRUE)`) and include the output.

## Proposal

Currently the font arguments in gt::opt_table_font() and gt::tab.options() does not allow users to set, which features of the font to use in tables. It would be very useful, if you could specify that a font should use tabular spacing for figures, so all numbers and decimal marks will be correctly aligned on top of each other.

title: `cols_width()` Produces an Error When Using `pct()` inside It in LaTeX/PDF Output
description:
## The Problem

If a user specifies a `cols_width()` value using the `pct()` function and tries to render to PDF, the render will fail with an error at the LaTeX compile stage (exact line number of the error depends on document content):

```         
compilation failed- error
Paragraph ended before \scr@LT@array was complete.
<to be read again> 
                   \par 
l.195 
```

## Expected Behavior

Using a `pct()` call to specify column widths with `cols_width()` when outputting to LaTeX/PDF should not produce an error.

## Actual Behavior

The resulting knitted document produces an error at the LaTeX compilation stage.

## Minimal Reproducible R Script

Compiling this script as its own file should produce the LaTeX error.
Also, by preserving LaTeX output we can visually inspect the generated LaTeX.

```{r}
#' ---
#' output:
#'   pdf_document:
#'     keep_md: true
#'     keep_tex: true
#'
#' ---

library(gt)
library(sessioninfo)

mtcars |> gt() |>
  cols_width(everything() ~ pct(15)) # an arbitrary column width for example purposes
session_info()
```

## The Offending LaTeX Lines

```{latex}
\begin{longtable}{>{\raggedleft\arraybackslash}p{15%}>{\raggedleft\arraybackslash}p{15%}>{\raggedleft\arraybackslash}p{15%}>{\raggedleft\arraybackslash}p{15%}>{\raggedleft\arraybackslash}p{15%}>{\raggedleft\arraybackslash}p{15%}>{\raggedleft\arraybackslash}p{15%}>{\raggedleft\arraybackslash}p{15%}>{\raggedleft\arraybackslash}p{15%}>{\raggedleft\arraybackslash}p{15%}>{\raggedleft\arraybackslash}p{15%}}
```

We can see from the LaTeX above that the `%` is causing all characters following it to be treated as a comment, rather than executable LaTeX.

## Tracing the Problem through `gt`

1.  When a user specifies a percentage with `pct()` inside a `cols_width()` call, the `pct()` call just takes that number and converts it into a string by [concatenating a raw `%` to the number](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/b6d3009ee209b7f342a00cb6e2ac0951c614ebe0/R/helpers.R#L252).
2.  That string value---which includes the raw `%` sign, gets passed to `create_table_start_l()`. On [line 175](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/b6d3009ee209b7f342a00cb6e2ac0951c614ebe0/R/utils_render_latex.R#L175) of that function, if the value of `col_widths[i]` isn't null, we eventually move to [line 186](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/b6d3009ee209b7f342a00cb6e2ac0951c614ebe0/R/utils_render_latex.R#L186C37-L186C61), where `col_widths[i]` gets pasted in seemingly without any check as to whether it contains a raw `%` sign.
3.  At this point `col_widths[i]` will necessarily contain the raw percent sign. So...
4.  The resulting text: `"p{", col_widths[i], "}"` gets passed on to LaTeX, where the LaTeX compiler interprets anything following an unescaped `%` as a comment.
5.  The call to `p{}` in LaTeX never gets a closing brace, because of the comment symbol.
6.  LaTeX fails to compile the document.

## A Temporary Work-Around

Instead of calling `pct()`, a user can specify a string literal with a backslash-escaped `%`, as in this fully reproducible script

```{r}
#' ---
#' output:
#'   pdf_document:
#'     keep_md: true
#'     keep_tex: true
#'
#' ---

library(gt)

mtcars |> gt() |>
  cols_width(everything() ~ "15\\%")
```

title: `gt_split()` Fails with Error on Certain Quarto Output Formats
description:
## Description

When executing a Quarto document, piping a `gt` table through `gt_split()` using the `col_slice_at` parameter should result in two or more output tables, regardless of the output format. Instead the `gt_split()` call fails with an error. The specific error depends on which kind of output format you're trying to render.

Below is a fully reproducible quarto document (`.qmd`) in its entirety containing:

- the expected behavior
- actual behavior
- the bug itself
- a draft fix 
- next possible steps

Sorry about the Error Summary by Format table. It would appear pandoc's [grid tables](https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#extension-grid_tables) don't play nicely with GitHub's markdown rendering engine.

## Reproducible Quarto (`.qmd`) Document

---

---
title: "`gt_split()` Fails with Error on Certain Quarto Output Formats"
format:
  docx: default # renders fine
  html: default # fails with error
  pdf: default  # fails with error
  rtf: default  # fails with error
  epub: default # fails with error
---

# Expected vs. Actual Behavior

## Expected Behavior

When executing a Quarto document, piping a `gt` table through `gt_split()` using the `col_slice_at` parameter will result in two or more output tables, regardless of the output format.

## Actual Behavior

The expression only produces tables in docx output format.
In other formats (I've tested HTML, PDF, RTF, and EPUB), it fails with error messages that differ slightly depending on the format.

## Error Summary by Format

```
+---------------+-------------------------------------------------+
| Format        | Error (Short Form)                              |
+===============+=================================================+
| HTML          | ```                                             |
|               | Error in `if (is.na(table_id)) ...`:            |
|               | ! argument is of length zero                    |
|               | ```                                             |
+---------------+-------------------------------------------------+
| PDF           | ```                                             |
|               | Error in `stop_if_not_gt_tbl()`:                |
|               | ! The `data` provided is not a `gt_tbl` object. |
|               | ```                                             |
+---------------+-------------------------------------------------+
| RTF           | ```                                             |
|               | Error in `stop_if_not_gt_tbl()`:                |
|               | ! The `data` provided is not a `gt_tbl` object. |
|               | ```                                             |
+---------------+-------------------------------------------------+
| EPUB          | ```                                             |
|               | Error in `if (is.na(table_id)) ...`:            |
|               | ! argument is of length zero                    |
|               | ```                                             |
+---------------+-------------------------------------------------+
```

# Reproducing the Bug

## Setup and Session Info

```{r setup}
library(gt)
library(sessioninfo)

session_info()
```

## Code to Reproduce Bug

```{r reproduce-bug}
mtcars |> 
  gt() |> 
  gt_split(col_slice_at = matches("disp"))
```

# Detailed Error Outputs for Non-docx Formats

## HTML Error

```

title: Add ICML export format to `gtsave()`
description:
## Prework

- [X] Read and abide by **gt**'s [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [X] Search for duplicates among the [existing issues](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues) (both open and closed).

## Proposal

I use gt in combination with Microsoft Word to created formatted documents in InDesign. While I have been using the Microsoft Word export format (in combination with the gto package), the import from Microsoft Word to InDesign does not support column spans and the styles for individual parts of the table are not preserved as paragraph or character styles—so there is a a fair amount of manual reformatting required after importing the table.

The alternative option that I'm suggesting would be an export to a ICML format (or potentially a tagged XML file that could work with [InDesign's support for XML import](https://helpx.adobe.com/indesign/using/tagging-content-xml.html)).

I already explored a few different work arounds without success. For example, here is a minimal example showing a basic option for converting from the HTML output to an ICML file:

``` r
library(gt)

gtsave_icml <- function(data, filename) {
  filename_html <- gsub(".icml$", ".html", filename)
  
  gt::gtsave(data, filename_html)
  
  rmarkdown::pandoc_convert(
    input = filename_html,
    output = filename,
    options = "--standalone"
  )
}

tbl <- exibble |> gt()

gtsave_icml(tbl, "gt-tbl.icml")
```

<sup>Created on 2023-10-02 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

Unfortunately, the Pandoc ICML Writer does not currently support many of the rich table formatting options that make gt tables so nice! This issue is documented here: https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/issues/6615

I also attempted to convert the HTML file into an XML file (similar to the process outlined in [this 2014 post](https://networkcultures.org/digitalpublishing/2014/05/15/import-html-into-indesign-via-xml/)) but InDesign supports style mapping to tags—not based on class attributes—so it still doesn't resolve the issue.

I understand that InDesign is not as widely used as many of the other export formats but I figured I'd submit the issue just in case it could be included in a long-term roadmap or if any other users have encountered this challenge and may have some suggestions to try. If anyone else want to take this on, the syntax for tables in InDesign is documented here: https://carijansen.com/indesign-xml-reference-guide/

title: Add get_XXX() functions to extract post-processed results (to facilitate QC work)
description:
At posit::conf(2023), Rich and I talked about this issue and Rich asked me to open a feature request outlining this.

My issue is that while doing Quality Control work for pharmacutical tables, we are often required to show that the table we just produced is identical to one produced under a previous version of the code. Another case is verifying that the table produced by the primary and validation programmer match. However, we can't just compare the guts of the gt object because "there is more than one way to do it."

For example, my primary and validation programmers might have each coded up a table and we need to compare them to show that the displayed outputs are identical:

```
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
# data to be shown, all irrational numbers
test_data <- data.frame(
  group1 = c('A','A','B','B'),
  group2 = c('M','F','M','F'),
  value  = c(1/17, 2/17, 3/17, 4/17)
)

### Two different approaches to making a table and doing the rounding
# Do the rounding first, and then pass into gt
gt1 <- 
  test_data |>
  mutate(value = round(value, digits=2) |> paste() ) |>
  pivot_wider( names_from=group2, values_from=value) |>
  gt()
# Let gt do the rounding for me
gt2 <- 
  test_data |>
  pivot_wider( names_from=group2, values_from=value) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(columns=c('M','F'),  decimals=2)
  

# But even though these tables produce the same result, 
# the internal data isn't the same and I can't just do
# Quality Control work by grabbing internal bits because those
# are the pre-processed information
gt1$`_data`
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   group1 M     F    
#>   <chr>  <chr> <chr>
#> 1 A      0.06  0.12 
#> 2 B      0.18  0.24
gt2$`_data`
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   group1      M     F
#>   <chr>   <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 A      0.0588 0.118
#> 2 B      0.176  0.235
Created on 2023-09-22 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org/)
```

Having a set of get_body(), get_column_labels(), etc that capture and extract the post-processed result so that we can write tests against will be massively beneficial for QC.

title: Incorrect styling of spanners when multiple lines of spanners are displayed
description:
## Description

When I add two spanners and I style them (change fill color) only the first spanner respects the column definition. All other spanners if I change the fill color the whole line is changed not only the desired columns.

## Reproducible example

``` r
library(tibble)
library(gt)

table1 <- tibble(id = 1, y = 2, z = 3) %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  tab_spanner(label = "y & z", columns = c("y", "z")) %>% 
  tab_style(style = cell_fill("red"), locations = cells_column_spanners("y & z"))

table2 <- tibble(id = 1, y = 2, z = 3) %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  tab_spanner(label = "only y", columns = c("y")) %>% 
  tab_style(style = cell_fill("blue"), locations = cells_column_spanners("only y")) %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "y & z", columns = c("y", "z")) %>% 
  tab_style(style = cell_fill("red"), locations = cells_column_spanners("y & z"))
```

title: Inconsistent behavior of `gt::text_transform()` depending on `locations`?
description:
## Prework * [x] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md). * [x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue. ## Description The docs of `gt::text_transform()` say that the locations argument can be any of `cells_body()`, `cells_stub()`, `cells_row_groups()`, `cells_column_labels()`, and `cells_column_spanners()`. I am assuming that I may be abusing the function somewhat by wanting to apply html there. However, the behavior here is somewhat inconsistent. Depending on the value of `locations`, the applied function needs to output different things in order to work. I create three different function that all aim to bold the input text. I know there are other ways to bold column labels, this is a simplified example of what I am actually trying to do. Is there a way to consistently apply html to all locations allowed in `gt::text_transform()`? That's especially a problem if a user applies multiple locations wrapped in a list. ## Reproducible example We create three different helper functions. The first one is simple, just paste text in-between bold tags. The second one applies gt::html but inside apply because htmltools::HTML collapses the input vector. The third one allows exactly this collapse. ``` r # EASY STRING MANIPULATION. WORKS IN CELL BODIES make_bold_1 <- function(text){ paste0("", text, "") } # SPECIFICALLY MAKE IT A HTML STRING # NEEDS LAPPLY BECAUSE htmltools::HTML COLLAPSES THE VECTOR make_bold_2 <- function(text){ lapply(paste0("", text, ""), gt::html) } # SPECIFICALLY MAKE IT A HTML STRING # ALLOW htmltools::HTML TO COLLAPSE make_bold_3 <- function(text){ gt::html(paste0("", text, "")) } example_data <- head(mtcars, 5) gt_tbl <- gt::gt(example_data, groupname_col = "cyl") # OUR EXAMPLE TABLE WITHOUT ANY MODIFICATION nflplotR::gt_render_image(gt_tbl) ``` ![](https://i.imgur.com/qdSBgCS.png) ### MODIFY CELL BODY ``` r # SIMPLE MAKE BOLD WORKS IN CELL BODY gt_tbl |> gt::text_transform(make_bold_1, locations = gt::cells_body()) |> nflplotR::gt_render_image() ``` ![](https://i.imgur.com/UxABpg3.png) ### MODIFY ROW GROUP LABELS ``` r # ... BUT THE LAPPLY VERSION WORKS gt_tbl |> gt::text_transform(make_bold_2, locations = gt::cells_row_groups()) |> nflplotR::gt_render_image() ``` ![](https://i.imgur.com/mlukH1U.png) ``` r # ... COLLAPSING MESSES IT UP gt_tbl |> gt::text_transform(make_bold_3, locations = gt::cells_row_groups()) |> nflplotR::gt_render_image() ``` ![](https://i.imgur.com/v7gaBw3.png) ### MODIFY COLUMN LABELS Neither of the 3 functions work. ``` r gt_tbl |> gt::text_transform(make_bold_1, locations = gt::cells_column_labels()) |> nflplotR::gt_render_image() ``` ![](https://i.imgur.com/9k9vEKb.png) ``` r gt_tbl |> gt::text_transform(make_bold_2, locations = gt::cells_column_labels()) |> nflplotR::gt_render_image() ``` ![](https://i.imgur.com/xqYnkzT.png) ``` r gt_tbl |> gt::text_transform(make_bold_3, locations = gt::cells_column_labels()) |> nflplotR::gt_render_image() ``` ![](https://i.imgur.com/ZfprcTD.png) ### SWITCH TO `gt::cols_label_with` ```r gt_tbl |> gt::cols_label_with(fn = make_bold_1) |> nflplotR::gt_render_image() ``` ![](https://i.imgur.com/ZfprcTD.png) ``` r # THE LIST VERSION ERRORS BECAUSE OF WRONG OUTPUT TYPE gt_tbl |> gt::cols_label_with(fn = make_bold_2) |> nflplotR::gt_render_image() #> Error in `gt::cols_label_with()`: #> ! `fn` must return a character vector. #> Backtrace: #> ▆ #> 1. ├─nflplotR::gt_render_image(gt::cols_label_with(gt_tbl, fn = make_bold_2)) #> 2. └─gt::cols_label_with(gt_tbl, fn = make_bold_2) #> 3. └─cli::cli_abort("{.arg fn} must return a character vector.") #> 4. └─rlang::abort(...) ``` ### THE COLLAPSE VERSION WORKS? ```r gt_tbl |> gt::cols_label_with(fn = make_bold_3) |> nflplotR::gt_render_image() ``` ![](https://i.imgur.com/yaKpHhH.png) Created on 2023-09-06 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)

title: fmt_flag assign wrong flag and ISO code to the Netherlands
description:
## Prework

* [x] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
* [x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue.

## Description

Describe the bug clearly and concisely. 
Hi there. Thank you for the gt() which is brilliant and useful. 
I noticed an issue with the **fmt_flag** function that generates flag icons for countries using their ISO2 country codes. Specifically, there seems to be a bug when it comes to the **Netherlands** (with the correct ISO2 code "**NL**"). The function doesn't display the flag correctly. In an example from April on your [blog post](https://posit.co/blog/new-formatting-functions-in-gt-0-9-0/), the function associates the ISO2 code "NU" with the Netherlands. However, "NU" is actually the code for **Niue**, a self-governing territory of New Zealand. This same error is present in the countrypops dataset, where the Netherlands is associated with the incorrect ISO2 code "NU". As a result, the flag displayed for the Netherlands using **fmt_flag** appears to be the flag of Niue.

## Reproducible example
data.frame(ISO2 =c("NU", "NL", "DE", "IT")) %>%  gt() %>%
  fmt_flag(columns = ISO2)

* [x] Post a [minimal reproducible example](https://www.tidyverse.org/help/) so the maintainer can troubleshoot the problems you identify. A reproducible example is:

    * [x] **Minimal**: reduce runtime wherever possible and remove complicated details that are irrelevant to the issue at hand.

title: Quarto Conditional Content directives appearing in output when using quarto and gt
description:
## Description

I am trying to create a document which rotates a gt() generated table into landscape when rendered as a pdf. Using conditional content works but I am getting 'garbage' in the output. For example when rendering as html I see a spurious back tick at the beginning and `{=html} at the end. The pdf render is clean. Attached is the code to reproduce. title: Add support for custom anchor element attributes to `fmt_url()`
description:
## Prework

- [X] Search for duplicates among the [existing issues](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues) (both open and closed).

## Proposal

I recently realized that the `fmt_url()` function does not allow custom attribute values and has the target attribute hard-coded as "_blank". Adding support for custom attributes to the `fmt_url()` function would add greater flexibility how the links are created. Support for other custom attributes including hreflang, ping, referrerpolicy, rel, and type could be added at the same time.

I used the documentation on the supported attributes for anchor elements ("<a>") from the mdn developer docs as a reference in setting up the validation: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/a#attributes

title: Automatically prefix row groups
description:
## Prework

- [x] Read and abide by **gt**'s [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Search for duplicates among the [existing issues](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues) (both open and closed).

## Proposal

It would be nice to have a function/argument to automatically prefix the names of row groups. Take the example below:

``` r
library(gt)
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)

iris[c(1:2, 51:52), ] |> 
  group_by(Species) |> 
  gt()
```
![image](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/assets/52219252/ab9abd3c-6f15-40f3-8dbb-5c9cdbe1a4c9)

I’d like to prefix the species names with “Panel X:”, where `X` is the panel number, so that the output is:

![image](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/assets/52219252/b8deca0f-655b-4ce4-a190-58611a2dc056)


I asked [on StackOverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/76970016/) but the best answer so far is to deal with the internals of the table object:

``` r
my_gt <- iris[c(1:2, 51:52), ] |> 
  group_by(Species) |>
  gt() 

labs <- unlist(my_gt$`_stub_df`$group_label)

# Stored in a list column
my_gt$`_stub_df`$group_label <- as.list(paste0("Panel ", match(labs, unique(labs)), ": ", labs))

my_gt |>
  tab_footnote(
    "a footnote",
    locations = cells_row_groups(groups = "setosa")
  )
```
![image](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/assets/52219252/1ad83d60-9539-4626-a9c9-e72703532fd2)

Note that simply prefixing the group names in the data itself isn’t a good solution because it changes the way we refer to row groups with `cells_row_groups()`:

``` r
iris[c(1:2, 51:52), ] |> 
  group_by(Species) |> 
  mutate(Species = paste0("Panel ", cur_group_id(), ": ", Species)) |>
  gt() |> 
  tab_footnote(
    "a footnote",
    locations = cells_row_groups(groups = "setosa")
  )
```
```
Error in `resolver_stop_on_character()`:
! The following row group(s) do not exist in the data: setosa.
Run `rlang::last_trace()` to see where the error occurred.
```

## Description

Context:

* multiple footnotes
* some of the footnotes have `locations = NULL`, so that they appear as general footnotes and are not related to a specific table element

In this case, the HTML output works fine:

![image](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/assets/52219252/9097045d-29bf-4c9d-a51e-56284db0bcf1)

But for LaTeX output, there is now an "NA" superscript before the general footnote.

![image](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/assets/52219252/34260612-77b5-4bc7-a3a7-7aa67046dc0f)


## Reproducible example

* [x] Post a [minimal reproducible example](https://www.tidyverse.org/help/) so the maintainer can troubleshoot the problems you identify. A reproducible example is:
    * [x] **Runnable**: post enough R code and data so any onlooker can create the error on their own computer.
    * [x] **Minimal**: reduce runtime wherever possible and remove complicated details that are irrelevant to the issue at hand.
    * [x] **Readable**: format your code according to the [tidyverse style guide](https://style.tidyverse.org/).

``` r
library(gt)
packageVersion("gt")
#> [1] '0.9.0.9000'

out <- mtcars[1, ] |> 
  gt() |> 
  tab_footnote("some general text") |> 
  tab_footnote("some specific text", locations = cells_column_labels(1))

# when we convert to Latex, it adds a "\\textsuperscript{\\textit{NA}}" before

## Proposal

Describe the new feature clearly and concisely. If applicable, write a minimal example in R code or pseudo-code to show input, usage, and desired output.

Currently, gt only allows for a single rowname column to be passed. This creates some difficulties if there is a table where you want to construct a table where there may be a few grouping columns you would like to use as rownames. This can be circumvented a little right now by mutating columns together into the final form you would like, but isnt simple and then requires styling downstream.

What I would like to see/be able to do is pass multiple columns to rowname_col, and make them all part of stub. 

```r
gt::gtcars |>
  gt(
    rowname_col = c("mfr","model","year")
  )
```

The order of the columns listed tells you the order of the columns in the stub, and there could be an option to remove duplicates or not:

```r
gt::gtcars |>
  gt(
    rowname_col = c("mfr","model","year")
  ) |>
 tab_option(rowname_col.remove_duplicates = FALSE) # default to true to remove duplicates
```

I can try to create "screen captures" to represent this if you need more details.

title: Potential Inconsistency in the Coloring Logic of Vertical Borders and Dividing Lines
description:
## Description

I have a requirement for coloring borders and dividing lines from my colleague. You can reproduce it with the code mentioned later. At first glance, it looks a bit messy, and I'd prefer to stick with the already beautiful default scheme of borders and background colors, only needing to add some zebra striping.

However, in practical application, adding conspicuous vertical dividing lines can indeed help readers distinguish vertical content, especially when the row content needs to automatically wrap.

On the leftmost and rightmost borders of the data table, I found that the black borders added later do not cover the default gray borders at the bottom of the column header row. This is inconsistent with the logic of border adjustment and coverage in Excel, and the internal vertical dividing lines of the data frame will cover the gray borders at the bottom of the column header row. Is this an inconsistent border coloring logic within `gt`?

title: row selection reactive variable needed for shiny app
description:
## Prework
couldn't find any similar request in the issue list

## Proposal

There is a `DT` package in R that is adopted from JS datatable package. This means a lot of its features are hidden and have to be passed through nested list(), which is very hard to remember. The only reason we still use DT package is the `input$tabname_rows_selected` reactive variable that is not available in `gt` (as yet). 

I suggest `gt` package to also allow row selection to be detected in a shiny app as an `input$..` variable. Then gt would be a compelling replacement of the DT package.

title: Using gt tables in PDF via Quarto
description: Is there any way to include a gt table in a PDF generated by Quarto that preserves the inline css formatting?  The gt tables display beautifully when rendered as an HTML file, but when rendering to PDF, I get a LaTeX compilation error about "Misplaced \noalign" for \midrule.  If I output the gt table as raw html, it will display in the PDF without any errors but it also loses the css formatting of the lines, the text bolding and colors, etc.  I have tried turning on and off various Quarto options, deleting the tables.tex file, changing knitr options, etc, but nothing fixes the problem.  I have had to resort to saving the gt table as an image and then displaying the image as a figure, but that prevents long tables from printing across multiple pages.  (If I output the gt table as raw html, the LaTeX code uses \longtable and that works, but then the table formatting that is stored as css is gone.)  I have looked for other discussions about this and I've seen references to gt not working well in pdfs, but I can't tell if there is a solution somewhere that I could use.

* [x] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
* [x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue.

## Description

Unable to use `gt_split()` on tables with row groups or row labels. 

## Reproducible example

* [x] Post a [minimal reproducible example](https://www.tidyverse.org/help/) so the maintainer can troubleshoot the problems you identify. A reproducible example is:
    * [x] **Runnable**: post enough R code and data so any onlooker can create the error on their own computer.
    * [x] **Minimal**: reduce runtime wherever possible and remove complicated details that are irrelevant to the issue at hand.
    * [x] **Readable**: format your code according to the [tidyverse style guide](https://style.tidyverse.org/).

1. Trying to split a table with row groups:
```
gtcars |>
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 10) |>
  dplyr::select(mfr, model, year, msrp) |>
  gt(groupname_col = "mfr") |>
  gt_split(row_every_n = 5)
```
produces the error:
```
Error in !is.null(group_id) && !has_two_col_stub && group_row_start ==  : 
  'length = 2' in coercion to 'logical(1)'
```

2. Trying to split a table with row labels: 
```
gtcars |>
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 10) |>
  dplyr::select(mfr, model, year, msrp) |>
  gt(rowname_col= "mfr") |>
  gt_split(row_every_n = 5)
```
produces the error:
```
Error in `table_body[[stub_var]]`:
! Can't extract column with `stub_var`.
✖ Subscript `stub_var` must be a location, not a character `NA`.
```

## Expected result

I would have expected the table to split into 2 tables (would it be based on 5 rows of the body cells?), while retaining the group/row labels.

title: `gt_split()` fails when input gt contains a body-level `tab_style()`
description:
## Prework

* [x] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
* [x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue.

## Description
First of all, thanks for incorporating this functionality! I know it is in development, but I wanted to report an issue that `gt_split()` throws an error when the input gt object contains styling on the body (via `tab_style()`). 

## Reproducible example

* [x] Post a [minimal reproducible example](https://www.tidyverse.org/help/) so the maintainer can troubleshoot the problems you identify. A reproducible example is:
    * [x] **Runnable**: post enough R code and data so any onlooker can create the error on their own computer.
    * [x] **Minimal**: reduce runtime wherever possible and remove complicated details that are irrelevant to the issue at hand.
    * [x] **Readable**: format your code according to the [tidyverse style guide](https://style.tidyverse.org/).

Building on the example from the `gt_split()` help file:
```
library(gt)

gt_example <- gtcars |>
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 10) |>
  dplyr::select(mfr, model, year, msrp) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_currency(columns = msrp) |>
  cols_width(
    year ~ px(80),
    everything() ~ px(150)
  ) 

gt_example |>
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_body()
  ) |>
  gt_split(row_every_n = 5)
```

## Expected result

Like the example in the help file, the table should have split into 2 tables of 5 rows each, except with bold text in the body cells. Instead the following error is observed: 
```
Error in tmp_rownum[i] <- which(rownum_final == styles_tbl$rownum[i]) : 
  replacement has length zero
```
Note: applying the same styling to, say, `cells_column_labels()` works fine.

title: `opt_interactive` does not work in loops inside Quarto
description:
## Description

Using regular print or `knitr::knit_child()` tricks do not work to display `gt` tables when `opt_interactive` is used.

## Reproducible example

````qmd

title: "Quarto and Interactive Tables"
format: html
---

## Interactive (not working)

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
#| panel: tabset
library(gt)
for (i in 1:2) {
  cat(sprintf("\n\n## Tab %s\n\n", i))
  print(opt_interactive(gt(head(gtcars))))
}
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
#| panel: tabset
library(gt)
for (i in 3:4) {
  cat(sprintf("\n\n## Tab %s\n\n", i))
  cat(
    knitr::knit_child(
      quiet = TRUE,
      text = c(
        "```{r}",
        "#| results: asis",
        "#| echo: false",
        "print(opt_interactive(gt(head(gtcars))))",
        "```"
      )
    )
  )
}

title: Coloring NA values
description:
I have been trying to color only NA values without coloring other variables with the `data_color` function but without success.

There appears to be an inconsistency in the behavior of the row parameter:

```
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)

dset <- tibble(
               temperature = c(1, 2, NA),
               pulse = c(NA, 1, 1.2)
        )
```

This does not work

```
dset %>%
  gt() %>%
  data_color(rows = is.na(everything()))
```

``` 
Error in `get_contrast_ratio()`:
! At least one color defined for each of `color_1` and `color_2`.~
```

... but this does

```
dset %>%
  gt() %>%
  data_color(rows = is.numeric(everything()))
```

`is.na` and `is.numeric` in my knowledge evaluates to the same logical value(s)

```
dset %>%
  gt() %>%
  data_color(rows = where( ~ is.na(.)))
```

I want to color only the `NA` values without coloring any other value

![image](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/assets/11381582/e469baf3-c289-498c-b3de-be9378adfbf6)

Thanks.

title: Summary results shifted in Word output
description:
In Word output, the results in summary rows are shifted to the right as the summary row label and the column label appear in the same column. This appears, e.g., with the following:

```
iris %>% select(Species, everything()) %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  grand_summary_rows(c(everything(), -Species), fns = c("Total" = ~sum(.))) %>% 
  gtsave("reports/test.docx")
```

![image](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/assets/60155545/734e801f-5c78-4341-86ec-7639c737d287)

Other output format are fine. (Still, this might be related to #769 where a similar issue was reported for `rtf`, though `rtf` works now).

title: Adding column spanner removes column header separator from other columns
description: ## Question Hello all. I am having an issue where when I add a column spanner (via tab_spanner()), the separator line between column headers and the data disappears for the columns that are not included in the spanner. This issue is best illustrated using sample code -- I have included sample code for tables with and without a column spanner. These tables illustrate that the line "separator" under the Age and Freq. columns disappear when I add the spanner for the other two columns. How do I retain this separator? P.S. BONUS question: This is less important, but is there an easy way to alter the grand_summary_rows so that the "TOTAL" rowname is not in a separate column, and is instead listed under the Age column? Thanks! ``` #Sample data age_time <- data.frame( group = c("< 15", "15-19", "20-24", "25-29", "30-34", "35-39", "> 39"), margin_pct = c(0.005, 0.005, 0.25, 0.30, 0.20, 0.10, 0.14) ) %>% mutate(before = margin_pct*1000, after = margin_pct*5000) #With spanner table1 <- age_time %>% gt() %>% tab_header(title = html("Sample Table")) %>% fmt_percent(columns = c(margin_pct), decimals = 1) %>% fmt_number(columns = c(before, after), decimals = 0, use_seps = T) %>% tab_spanner( label = html("Counts"), columns = c(before, after) ) %>% cols_label( group = html("Age"), margin_pct = html("Freq."), before = html("Before"), after = html("After") ) %>% tab_options( heading.subtitle.font.size = "115%", table.width = "300px" ) %>% cols_align(c(-group), align = "center") %>% grand_summary_rows( fns = list(Total = ~sum(.)), columns = c(margin_pct), fmt = ~fmt_percent(.) ) %>% grand_summary_rows( fns = list(Total = ~sum(.)), columns = c(before, after), fmt = ~fmt_number(., use_seps = T, decimals = 0) ) table1 #Without Spanner table2 <- age_time %>% gt() %>% tab_header(title = html("Sample Table")) %>% fmt_percent(columns = c(margin_pct), decimals = 1) %>% fmt_number(columns = c(before, after), decimals = 0, use_seps = T) %>% cols_label( group = html("Age"), margin_pct = html("Freq."), before = html("Before"), after = html("After") ) %>% tab_options( heading.subtitle.font.size = "115%", table.width = "300px" ) %>% cols_align(c(-group), align = "center") %>% grand_summary_rows( fns = list(Total = ~sum(.)), columns = c(margin_pct), fmt = ~fmt_percent(.) ) %>% grand_summary_rows( fns = list(Total = ~sum(.)), columns = c(before, after), fmt = ~fmt_number(., use_seps = T, decimals = 0) ) table2 ```

title: Why only a LIST can be successfully converted to the markdown format?
description:
Dear GT team,

Can you please help me understand the below "issue"?

I tried to convert a web link to the Markdown (MD) format by using your helper function ```gt::md```. I attempted three approaches by versioning them as ```file_path_transform_md_v1```, ```file_path_transform_md_v2```, and ```file_path_transform_md_v3```.

```file_path_transform_md_v1``` was converted with the help of `purrr::map`.

```file_path_transform_md_v2``` was transformed by changing the data type to the LIST.

```file_path_transform_md_v3``` was generated purely by the ```gt::md``` function.

It turned out that only the ```file_path_transform_md_v1``` and ```file_path_transform_md_v2``` were successfully converted to clickable hyperlinks, but the ```file_path_transform_md_v3``` failed although all of them were the same data type `from_markdown`. 

I would like to learn the WHY of the above outcomes. I look forward to hearing from you.

Thanks for your help in advance.


The below is created on 2023-04-24 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org/) (v2.0.1)
```
rm(list = ls())
library(dplyr)
library(gt)

final_table <- tibble(url = "https://www.google.com") |>
  mutate(url_transform = stringr::str_glue("[link]({url})")) |>
  mutate(file_path_transform_md_v1 = purrr::map(url_transform, gt::md)) |>
  mutate(file_path_transform_md_v2 = list(md(url_transform))) |>
  mutate(file_path_transform_md_v3 = md(url_transform))

final_table |> gt()

str(final_table)
#> tibble [1 × 5] (S3: tbl_df/tbl/data.frame)
#>  $ url                      : chr "https://www.google.com"
#>  $ url_transform            : 'glue' chr "[link](https://www.google.com)"
#>  $ file_path_transform_md_v1:List of 1
#>   ..$ : 'from_markdown' chr "[link](https://www.google.com)"
#>  $ file_path_transform_md_v2:List of 1
#>   ..$ : 'from_markdown' chr "[link](https://www.google.com)"
#>  $ file_path_transform_md_v3: 'from_markdown' chr "[link](https://www.google.com)"
```

title: Error rendering HTML table with multiple higher level spanners and cell styles
description:
## Prework

* [x] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
* [x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue.

## Description

When multiple spanners are placed at level 2 or higher *and* styles are added to a a table, the resulting gt object fails to print and render in html.  The issue appears to be code in the function "create_heading_component_h" in "utils_render_html.R" for processing higher spanner rows.  There is a call to `dplyr::filter` which compares the group names in the style table to the vector `spanner_vars`; I believe this is meant to compare it to a specific *element* of `spanner_vars`

## Reproducible example

When no styles are included, the spanners render successfully:

```
randomData <- tibble(First=c("A","B","C"), 
					 GroupA1=1:3,
					 GroupA2=2:4,
					 GroupB1=c(8,10,12),
					 GroupB2=10+(5:7)/10,
					 Final=c("Red","Green","Blue"))

table1 <- randomData %>% gt() %>%
	tab_spanner(columns=c(1),label="Row",level=1) %>%
	tab_spanner(columns=c(2,3),label="Lower",level=1) %>%
	tab_spanner(columns=c(4,5),label="Higher",level=1) %>%
	tab_spanner(columns=c(6),label="White",level=1) %>%
	tab_spanner(columns=c(2,3),label="Group A",level=2) %>%
	tab_spanner(columns=c(4,5),label="Group B",level=2) %>%
	tab_spanner(columns=c(6),label="Color",level=2)

print(table1)
```

But when styles are added to two of the cells, the render fails:

```
table2 <- randomData %>% gt() %>%
	data_color(columns=6,rows=1,palette="red",apply_to="fill") %>%
	tab_spanner(columns=c(1),label="Row",level=1) %>%
	tab_spanner(columns=c(2,3),label="Lower",level=1) %>%
	tab_spanner(columns=c(4,5),label="Higher",level=1) %>%
	tab_spanner(columns=c(6),label="White",level=1) %>%
	tab_spanner(columns=c(2,3),label="Group A",level=2) %>%
	tab_spanner(columns=c(4,5),label="Group B",level=2) %>%
	tab_spanner(columns=c(6),label="Color",level=2)

print(table2)
```

## Expected result

This second table should have formatted a single cell (the sixth cell in the first row) with a red fill (and white text).  However, it instead gives the following error:

```
Error in `dplyr::filter()`:
i In argument: `grpname == spanners_vars`.
Caused by error:
! `..2` must be of size 1, not size 3.
```

title: Option to omit longtable environment in Latex
description:
Thank you for the great package! 

I think it would be great if the gtsave function had an option to omit the \begin{longtable} and \end{longtable} parts and only save the the text from \begin{tabular} to \end{tabular}. This would facilitate incorporating the output into Latex documents, and would be analogous to e.g. the contents_only option in xtable.

title: Add documentation to clarify when na_color is used in data_color()
description:
## Description

In https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/1301, @rich-iannone and I realized that the documentation for the `na_color` argument in `gt::data_color()` could be improved to clarify that it is ignored when the user specifies an argument to `fn`.

A suggested update is to add something to the documentation like:

```
@param na_color [...] ignored if the user specifies the value of `fn`, in which case the argument to `fn` should specify the color of NA arguments
```

## Reproducible example

The code below is what I tried that I expected would work, but didn't.

```
library(gt)
sza |>
       dplyr::filter(latitude == 20 & tst <= "1200") |>
       dplyr::select(-latitude) |>
       dplyr::filter(!is.na(sza)) |>
       tidyr::spread(key = "tst", value = sza) |>
       gt(rowname_col = "month") |>
       data_color(
             fn = scales::col_numeric(
                   palette = c("red", "white", "green"),
                   domain = c(0, 50, 100)
               ), 
             na_color = "white"   # <- Color NA cells to be white (does not seem to do anything)
         )
```

title: tab_footnote() in Rmarkdown corrupts word document with special character "<"
description:
## Description

When using `tab_footnote(footnote = "p < .05")` in an Rmardown document producing a word document. The word document get corrupted. 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/117753797/231565211-000b29e6-9b05-475d-9e58-dab40d25e60a.png)

I was able to pinpoint the faulty character being "<" in the footnote statement. Taking this character out solve the issue of corruption.

title: Add opts for caption alignment and/or location for HTML output
description:
Low-priority feature request: Super happy that you've added captions (yay for https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/635). Because it's the accessible label for a table for screenreaders, if I only use one title-ish function (e.g. `tab_header(), `tab_caption()`) for a table, it's caption. Currently, it listens to position arguments from yaml, but is always above the table and center aligned with gt (as far as I've been able to figure out).

You can get it left aligned with custom CSS, but something like `opt_align_caption()` (the caption-equivalent of `opt_align_table_header()`) and/or similar options for positioning it relative to the table for HTML output (similar to the arguments for exporting it to word, linked below), would be lovely.
https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/7aed84d865c55ddbf1c3d28e2feafabb547687f3/R/export.R#L799-L803

Apologies if this is already possible and I missed it. If so, happy to help with any documentation changes to make it more findable.

Thanks, Rich!

title: Using tab_source_note and tab_footnote together in quarto distorts table
description:
## Prework

* [x ] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
* [ x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue.

## Description

When using tab_source_note and tab_footnote together in a quarto document, the rendered document shows a broken/distorted table. However, running the code chunks interactively (i.e. not rendering in quarto) returns the correct, intended table.


## Reproducible example

I copy here the entire code of the quarto document. Running a reprex in an .r file doesn't reveal the error.

---
title: "Untitled"
format: html
---


```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
packageVersion("gt")
```


# only source note
```{r}
mtcars %>%
gt() %>%
tab_source_note(
  source_note="this is the source"
)
```

# only footnote
```{r}
mtcars %>%
gt() %>%
tab_footnote(
  footnote="this is the footnote",
  locations=cells_column_labels(columns=carb)
) 
```

# both: error
```{r}
mtcars %>%
gt() %>%
tab_source_note(
  source_note="this is the source"
) %>%
tab_footnote(
  footnote="this is the footnote",
  locations=cells_column_labels(columns=carb)
) 
```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9595585/230591704-a31b1f97-55d6-43f4-8099-1665d794b4a4.png)



## Expected result

Table should contain footnote and sourcenote and be rendered correctly in quarto.
