title: Request: mark NSE-friendly functions in documentation
description:
I maintain some metaprogramming tools that need to be NSE-aware to avoid flagging code with spurious "undefined objects" warnings from `codetools::checkUsage()`.

For tidyr and dplyr, I can search the documentation for certain links to get a good head start on which functions are NSE-friendly,

e.g. tidyr might use `<tidy-select>`:

![cols= argument of tidyr::pivot longer is described as "<tidy-select> Columns to pivot into longer format."](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7606389/229330894-457c60e3-bfad-4d89-939d-632e60975f09.png)

https://github.com/tidyverse/tidyr/blob/0764e65fad777b71aa2a81ffd5447d04a61f8d5e/R/pivot-long.R#L17-L18

Would it make sense for {gt} to offer similar hints in the documentation about where NSE might show up in its calls?

title: Make opt_interactive() faster via reactive computing
description:
`gt::opt_interactive()` could be potentially used as an alternative accessible viewer in place of the default `utils::View()` for both screen reader users and general users. It would be even nicer if we could make `gt::opt_interactive()` much faster to address a large dataset. We may want to avoid any overhead via reactive computing. For example, the following is too slow:

``` r
ggplot2::diamonds |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::opt_interactive()
```

title: Align tables from `gt_split()`
description:
## Proposal It would be cool to put multiple tables from `gt_split()` next to each other or onto a grid. One way this could be done is to modify the internal `print.gt_group` function so that it accepts CSS for both the container that contains a single table and the container that contains all tables. Here are a two drafts I came up with. ## Draft 1: Wrap `html_tbl_i` and the final output into `div()`. ``` library(gt) my_print.gt_group <- function (x, css_outer = NULL, css_inner = NULL, ..., view = interactive()) { html_tbls <- htmltools::tagList() seq_tbls <- seq_len(nrow(x$gt_tbls)) for (i in seq_tbls) { html_tbl_i <- htmltools::div( style = css_inner, gt:::as.tags.gt_tbl(grp_pull(x, which = i), ...) ) html_tbls <- htmltools::tagList( html_tbls, html_tbl_i, if (i != max(seq_tbls)) htmltools::HTML("
")) } htmltools::div( style = css_outer, html_tbls ) } ``` ``` metro |> dplyr::slice(1:10) |> dplyr::select(name, passengers) |> gt() |> cols_width(name ~ px(250), passengers ~ px(100)) |> gt_split(row_every_n = 5) |> my_print.gt_group( css_outer = 'display: flex;', css_inner = 'margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;' ) ``` ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/65388595/229305779-596eaf43-1540-458c-8e3d-580e381c0a14.png) For more than two tables one could ad `flex-wrap: wrap` to the outer `div`. ``` metro |> dplyr::slice(1:10) |> dplyr::select(name, passengers) |> gt() |> cols_width(name ~ px(250), passengers ~ px(100)) |> gt_split(row_every_n = 3) |> my_print.gt_group( css_outer = 'display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap;', css_inner = 'margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;' ) ``` ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/65388595/229305814-99f0c627-05bc-4a7c-85ce-e6361b264026.png) ## Draft 2: Remove line breaks The previous two approaches do not work if you use `display: grid` due to the line breaks. Hence, I had to make two changes: 1. Remove line breaks 2. Initialize taglist with first table and adjust loop accordingly ``` grid_print.gt_group <- function (x, css_outer = NULL, css_inner = NULL, ..., view = interactive()) { html_tbls <- htmltools::tagList( htmltools::div( style = css_inner, gt:::as.tags.gt_tbl(grp_pull(x, which = 1), ...) ) ) seq_tbls <- seq_len(nrow(x$gt_tbls)) for (i in seq_tbls[-1]) { html_tbl_i <- htmltools::div( style = css_inner, gt:::as.tags.gt_tbl(grp_pull(x, which = i), ...) ) html_tbls <- htmltools::tagList( html_tbls, html_tbl_i ) } htmltools::div( style = css_outer, html_tbls ) } ``` Then, using `display: grid` works. ``` metro |> dplyr::slice(1:10) |> dplyr::select(name, passengers) |> gt() |> cols_width(name ~ px(250), passengers ~ px(100)) |> gt_split(row_every_n = 3) |> grid_print.gt_group( css_outer = 'display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr);', ) ``` ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/65388595/229305909-74150901-d229-4066-bfed-1e5d954235f9.png) ## Remark In order for this to look good, the width of each column needs to be set with `cols_width()`. Otherwise, each sub-table will use the minimal necessary width for its data. Thus, if e.g. names are shorter than in the other tables, then that table will not align properly with the other tables. This could maybe be fixed in some iteration but I don't think that it's a big problem to apply `cols_width()`.

title: cols_width() is off by one column when row_group.as_column = TRUE
description:
## Description

Column selections in `cols_width()` are shifted one column to the left when creating a grouped table and setting `row_group.as_column = TRUE`.

## Reproducible example

```
library(gt)
library(dplyr)

# Example includes column borders via tab_style() to make is easy to see which columns are changing size

# Makes the hp column very wide, as expected
mtcars %>%
  select(cyl,mpg,hp) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_borders(),
    locations = cells_body(
      columns = everything(),
      rows = everything()
    )
  ) %>%
  cols_width(hp ~ px(200))

# With a grouped table, still correctly makes the hp column very wide
mtcars %>%
  select(cyl,mpg,hp) %>%
  group_by(cyl) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_borders(),
    locations = cells_body(
      columns = everything(),
      rows = everything()
    )
  ) %>%
  tab_options(row_group.as_column = FALSE) %>%
  cols_width(hp ~ px(200))

# When we set row_group.as_column = TRUE, now the mpg column
# is very wide and the hp column is unchanged
mtcars %>%
  select(cyl,mpg,hp) %>%
  group_by(cyl) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_borders(),
    locations = cells_body(
      columns = everything(),
      rows = everything()
    )
  ) %>%
  tab_options(row_group.as_column = TRUE) %>%
  cols_width(hp ~ px(200))
```

## Expected result

When setting `row_group.as_column = TRUE`, column selections in `cols_width()` should apply to the selected columns, not the one to the immediate left.

title: Column header IDs duplicated across tables
description:
## Prework

* [x] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
* [x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue.

## Description

Column header IDs are based only on the column, so a document with multiple tables that each have a "Total" column will result in 2 `th` elements being given the id `Total`.

## Reproducible example

````
---
title: "Untitled"
format: html
---


```{r}
library(gt)
```

```{r}
gt(cars)
```

```{r}
gt(cars)
```

````

## Expected result

There should be no duplicated IDs. But here the first and second tables both have `th` elements with id `speed` and `dist`.

According to https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn/HTML/Tables/Advanced, `scope` should be enough for accessibility purposes, so perhaps provide an option to disable assigning header and row IDs? Otherwise, I'd expect the header IDs to be prefixed by the table id.

title: Labelled data causes errors with `fmt_` functions (and perhaps others?)
description:
## Prework

(All confirmed...this is a new issue as far as I can tell, and I believe my reprex should work for anyone. The sjlabelled package is optional but allows clear viewing of the labels.)

## Description

When using labelled data (for example, the kind of data that can be read into a dataframe from an SPSS file using `haven::read_sav()`, functions like `gt::fmt_integer` and `gt::fmt_scientific` (and I imagine others, too, but I only tested those) throw an error: "The `fmt_number()` and `fmt_integer()` functions can only be used on `columns` with numeric data."

## Reproducible example
```
idvec <- haven::labelled(x = factor(c(1:25)), 
                         label = 'Participant ID')
labvec <- haven::labelled(x = c(1,2,3),
                labels = c(Low = 1, Medium = 2, High = 3),
                label = 'A variable w/ three possible values')

mytib <- tibble::tibble(id = idvec,
                        scores = sample(x = labvec,
                                        size = 25,
                                        replace = TRUE))

# first, show the labels:
mytib |> sjlabelled::get_label() # print VARIABLE labels
mytib |> sjlabelled::get_labels() # print VALUE labels

# next, attempt the function in question, before and after removing variable or value labels
mytib |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = everything(), decimals = 1) 
   # doesn't work -
   # "The `fmt_number()` and `fmt_integer()` functions can only be used on `columns` with numeric data."

mytib |>
  haven::zap_label() |> # remove VARIBLE labels
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = everything(), decimals = 3)
   # doesn't work -
   # "The `fmt_number()` and `fmt_integer()` functions can only be used on `columns` with numeric data."

mytib |>
  haven::zap_labels() |>  # remove VALUE labels
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = everything(), decimals = 3) 
   # works! Returns a GT object as expected
```
## Expected result

The first `fmt_number` function should work without having to zap the labels. The labels are incidental -- the relevant column(s) are still numeric. It seems the issue is in the VALUE labels, rather than the VARIABLE label. 

I noticed this when first encountering the error in the gtExtras package [gt_plt_summary](https://jthomasmock.github.io/gtExtras/reference/gt_plt_summary.html) function, and tracked it down to the gt package.

Social scientists like myself often use labelled data -- value labels are often useful information, and are contained in SPSS files (and maybe SAS and other software as well?). Would be nice to keep these without having to manually zap them whenever we want to use these functions in the gt package.

I suppose a quick and dirty solution could be to zap the labels internally. Better would be to ignore the labels completely, and keep that metadata. The class of the labelled objects is:

```
> mytib |> purrr::map(class)
$id
[1] "haven_labelled" "vctrs_vctr"     "integer"       

$scores
[1] "haven_labelled" "vctrs_vctr"     "double"
````

- [x] Search for duplicates among the [existing issues](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues) (both open and closed).

## Proposal

There are often cases when summary rows cannot be directly calculated from what is shown in the table (e.g., if each cell is a distinct count, and the summary row should also be a distinct count for the entire group or table). In these cases, it'd be useful to be able to access the column name of the current column so that, e.g., the summary function could perform a simple lookup. 

At the moment, I find myself passing constant-valued functions a lot to grand summary rows, and it gets a bit hairy when this needs to be done for multiple columns. Or perhaps there's a better way to just manually supply summary rows?

title: Using a heading with `tab_header()` causes an HTML table to not render correctly in Quarto (v1.3+)
description:
As originally reported in https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/4603, HTML-based gt tables with a heading (i.e., those produced through `tab_header()`) produce invalid HTML (two `<thead>` elements) which is understandably not parsed correctly by Pandoc (though browsers are okay with this markup).

To solve this, there should only be a single `<thead>` element. So, the heading (if present) should reside in the same element as the column labels (if they are to be displayed). The CSS classes will move to the child `<tr>` elements. This needs to be tested well to avoid any major regressions.

description:

* [x ] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/0/code_of_conduct/) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
* [x ] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue.
* [ x] Post a [minimal reproducible example](https://www.tidyverse.org/help/) so the maintainer can troubleshoot the problems you identify. A reproducible example is:
    * [ ] **Runnable**: post enough R code and data so any onlooker can create the error on their own computer.
    * [ ] **Minimal**: reduce runtime wherever possible and remove complicated details that are irrelevant to the issue at hand.
    * [ ] **Readable**: format your code according to the [tidyverse style guide](https://style.tidyverse.org/).

## Description

I want to flag an unintended consequence of the change from `{webshot}` to `{webshot2}` introduced in 0.7.0. This might also be related to #721.

When using v0.6.0 (the last version before the change to webshot2), saving a long table to pdf resulted in the table being printed on a single 'page' of a pdf. See
[sp500_table_0.6.0.pdf](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/files/10857007/sp500_table_0.6.0.pdf) as an example. Using v0.8.0, the table is split across multiple pages. See [sp500_table_0.8.0.pdf](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/files/10857011/sp500_table_0.8.0.pdf) as an example.

I'm not certain that this is a bug - some people might want the table split on multiple pages. But, there's no way that I could find to change the behavior. One option might just be to let users choose which package performs the webshot?

## Reproducible example

Here is the code to produce the examples. It's taken from the gt website.

```r
library(gt)
library(tidyverse)
library(glue)

# Define the start and end dates for the data range
start_date <- "2014-06-07"
end_date <- "2015-06-14"

# Create a gt table based on preprocessed
# `sp500` table data
sp500_table <-
  sp500 %>%
  filter(date >= start_date & date <= end_date) %>%
  select(-adj_close) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "S&P 500",
    subtitle = glue("{start_date} to {end_date}")
  ) %>%
  fmt_date(
    columns = date,
    date_style = 3
  ) %>%
  fmt_currency(
    columns = c(open, high, low, close),
    currency = "USD"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(
    columns = volume,
    suffixing = TRUE
  )

gtsave(
  data = sp500_table,
  filename = "sp500_table_0.8.0.pdf",
  zoom = 1)
```

## Expected result

I'd prefer for the old behavior to be maintained. Using the same code with different versions and getting different results is always a bit unexpected.

## Question

Hi @rich-iannone,

I created a couple of pharma tables lately for the rtrs-wg tables book and had the following idea: I often have to use `dplyr::add_rows()` to create first row stating something like `Patients with at least` in a column that would end up being a rowname_col, while the groupname_col would remain empty.

I attached an example code below and would like to ask, if there could be an option in `gt()` to omit the creating of groupname columns whenever the specified column contains NA's and create groups for the non-NA group values.

``` r
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)

gtcars |> 
  dplyr::filter(ctry_origin == "Germany") |> 
  dplyr::select(1:5) |> 
  dplyr::add_row(
    mfr = NA_character_,
    model = "Some great German cars:",
    .before = 1 
  ) |> 
  gt(
    rowname_col = "model",
    groupname_col = "mfr"
  )
```  

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/46823209/219076996-f956ed6e-5835-46dd-9454-48bc8aba7033.png)

What I would like to be able to do is something like this:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/46823209/219078643-584187f0-56cc-4eae-beee-3bcf01408212.png)

The latter is of course a result of the below code, but for data with a lot of groups and only one NA row, the feature could save a lot of coding:

``` r
gtcars |> 
  dplyr::filter(ctry_origin == "Germany") |> 
  dplyr::select(1:5) |> 
  dplyr::add_row(
    mfr = NA_character_,
    model = "Some great German cars:",
    .before = 1 
  ) |>
  gt() |> 
  tab_row_group(
    label = "BMW",
    rows = mfr == "BMW"
  ) |> 
  tab_row_group(
    label = "Audi",
    rows = mfr == "Audi"
  ) |> 
  tab_row_group(
    label = "Mercedes-Benz",
    rows = mfr == "Mercedes-Benz"
  ) |> 
  tab_row_group(
    label = "Porsche",
    rows = mfr == "Porsche"
  ) |> 
  row_group_order(
    groups = c(NA_character_, "BMW", "Audi", "Mercedes-Benz", "Porsche")
  ) |> 
  cols_hide(
    columns = "mfr"
  )
```

Thanks a lot, Rich!

title: Pagination - advanced
description:
## Prework

- [x] Read and abide by **gt**'s [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/0/code_of_conduct/) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Search for duplicates among the [existing issues](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues) (both open and closed).

## Proposal

Expanding on #1211, functions to identify patterns of how to paginate the input data so the user doesn't have to split it themselves
 - rowwise splitting based on
   - n rows
   - group
   - split when group length would slip onto the next page (maybe a bit harder, would require working out nrows available per page)
   
 - colwise splitting
   - "grouped columns" - which columns group together when a table is too wide and move together
   - "sticky columns" is there a column _in addition to the stub_ the user would want to duplicate
  
  - Collation rules -  given if both row and colwise splitting occurs, how to present the data
    -  rows are grouped together, so rows 1:20 of A-C split are presented, then 1:20 of D-F, then 21:40 if A-C,  21:40 if D-R, then 41:60...
    - columns are grouped together, so rows 1:20 of A-C split are presented, then 21:40 if A-C, through all rows of A-C, then 1:20 of D-F, 21-40 of D-F, etc.

This might look like:

```{r}

library(tidyverse)
library(gt)

paginated_gt <- gtcars |>
  gt() |>
  paginate_by(
    row_splits = mfr, # just pass the column when splitting on column values, pass a number if its n rows
    col_groups = list( model:bdy_style, hp:mpg_h,  trsmn:msrp), ## Group information to display together if splits are needed col_wise
    collate_by = "rows"# (or "columns") there may be additional collation rules, but with the proposal above there are two. This 
  )

## feeds into the updated gtsave
paginated_gt |> 
  gtsave("paginated_gtcars_by_mfr.pdf")

```

This is a suggestion to allow gtsave to accept a list of gts (and perhaps some meta information such as entries into tab_options or special titles, etc too?) to created paginated reports of gts. ## tables by car make

library(tidyverse)
library(gt)

 map(function(x){
  x |>
   select(-mfr) |>
   gt() |>

 gtsave("tables_by_mfr.pdf")

```

    * [ x ] **Minimal**: reduce runtime wherever possible and remove complicated details that are irrelevant to the issue at hand.

## Description

Hi @rich-iannone,

still a huge fan of your package and grateful for the update of the `summary_rows()` function. I tried to apply summary rows to two columns and after that, merge them using `cols_merge*()`, but noticed that the merging pattern was ignored in the summary row. The summary row below only contains the sum of prices in USD, but would ideally include a summary in the form of `$105.25 (98.36€)`.

## Reproducible example

``` r
library(gt)

pizzaplace |> 
  head() |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    price_euro = price/1.07
  ) |> 
  gt() |> 
  fmt_currency(
    columns = "price",
    currency = "USD"
  ) |> 
  fmt_currency(
    columns = "price_euro",
    currency = "EUR",
    decimals = 2
  ) |> 
  tab_row_group(
    label = "First 6 records of pizzaplace",
    rows = everything()
  ) |> 
  summary_rows(
    groups = "First 6 records of pizzaplace",
    columns = "price",
    fns = list(label = "Total Sales US Dollar (Euro)", fn = "sum"),
    side = "top"
  ) |> 
  cols_merge_n_pct(
    col_n = "price",
    col_pct = "price_euro"
  ) 
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/46823209/218437205-b865920a-fa8c-49cb-bbb8-2d21e0cb0278.png)

## Expected result

The summary row should include a summary in the form of the specified merging pattern after one of the `cols_merge*()` function have been applied.

title: problems exporting math symbols to latex
description:
hello. firstly, thank you for the package, when I first learned about it was one of those "I love R"'s days. 

I am having problems exporting to latex, specifically when I have math symbols in the column header. 
The backslashes and dollar signs are being parsed but that breaks the latex. 

MWE:

````
tibble(
  filter = c("a", "b", "c"), 
  lambda_pivot = c(637.4, 879.0, 912.8)
  ) |> 
  gt() |> 
  cols_label(
    filter = "Filter",
    lambda_pivot = r"($\lambda_{pivot}$)",
  ) |> 
  gtsave(filename = "output/table_test.tex")
````
produces the output:

```
\begin{longtable}{lr}
\toprule
Filter & \$\textbackslash{}lambda\_\{pivot\}\$ \\ 
\midrule
a & 637.4 \\ 
b & 879.0 \\ 
c & 912.8 \\ 
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}
```
The problem is in the line:
`Filter & \$\textbackslash{}lambda\_\{pivot\}\$ \\ `

when I expect it to be:
`Filter & $\lambda_{pivot}$ \\ `
which will be correctly parsed by latex. 

I also tried doubling the $ and \ or using `espace_latex()` but the output is the same. 

I tried to look into the other issues here related to latex but all of them seemed more complicated than mine. 

Am I missing something? How can I get a raw `$\lambda_{pivot}$` in the output file?
thx

title: Parentheses can break latex longtables produced by gt()
description:
As discussed [here](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/228755/undefined-control-sequence-on-left-parenthesis-after-midrule-in-longtable), an open paren cannot follow `\midrule` in a longtable latex environment.  This causes things like `(Intercept)`, produced by `broom::tidy() |> gt()` to produce latex errors.

A simpler example is shown below.

``` r
tibble::tribble(
  ~ a, ~b,
  "(a)", "b") |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::as_latex() |>
  cat()
#> \begin{longtable}{ll}
#> \toprule
#> a & b \\ 
#> \midrule
#> (a) & b \\ 
#> \bottomrule
#> \end{longtable}
```

<sup>Created on 2023-01-09 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

The latex error produced if we stop at gt::gt() is

```
compilation failed- error
Undefined control sequence.
<argument> ...al \expandafter \let \cmrsideswitch 
                                                  \@tempa \fi \fi
```

It looks like one solution would be to use `\midrule\relax ` in place of `\midrule` to prevent `\midrule` from trying to apply `(a)` as an optional argument.

I'm pretty sure the same issue would arise for a paren after `\toprule`, but that doesn't happen in my `broom::tidy()` use case.

title: Reconsider choice of CSS inliner with system dependency on V8
description:
#1114 switched to using the Javascript library [juice](https://github.com/Automattic/juice) (via [juicyjuice](https://github.com/rich-iannone/juicyjuice)) for CSS inlining. But this requires V8 (via [V8](https://github.com/jeroen/v8)), which is a gigantic system dependency for a relatively marginal feature. For example, it took almost an hour to compile it on Arch Linux, (8.0 GiB, i5-6200U × 4). For me this makes gt itself too heavy a dependency for e.g. research compendiums.

Some googling tells me there are a few options for CSS inlining libraries in other languages, e.g. [Python/Rust css-inliner](https://github.com/Stranger6667/css-inline), [Perl CSS::Inliner](). Otherwise, is is feasible to port juice (or the features needed) to R? Or at least make juicyjuice an optional dependency?

## Question

Hi @rich-iannone, I really like your package, which is why I'm starting with a big thank you for all the hard work you put in to make it even more awesome!

I know that {gt} supports page breaks for long tables. Is there an option to add this feature for wide tables as well? We would need this for clinical data summary tables with lots of doses (typically the case for phase 1 dose escalation studies):

``` r
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)

dose_escalation <- dplyr::tribble(
        ~stat,  ~dose_1,  ~dose_2,  ~dose_3,  ~dose_4,  ~dose_5,  ~dose_6,  ~dose_7,  ~dose_8,
          "n",        4,        4,        4,        5,        4,        3,        3,        2,
       "Cmax",     0.08,     0.48,     1.51,     3.08,     8.75,    24.19,    27.84,    31.46,
  "AUC 0-Inf",       82,      498,     1492,    3781,     9203,     25843,    43587,    50014,
)


dose_escalation |> 
  gt() |> 
  tab_header(
    title = "Dose Escalation Study"
  ) |> 
  fmt_integer(
    columns = starts_with("dose"),
    rows = stat %in% c("n", "AUC 0-Inf")
  ) |> 
  cols_width(
    stat ~ px(100),
    starts_with("dose") ~ px(150)
  )
```

The resulting table is too wide:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/46823209/208692976-5d5b47c1-af10-45f0-b0cf-daee457f8c28.png)

I would like to add a page break, displaying the first four doses and their summary stat label (column stat) on the first page and the other four doses with the stat column as identifier on the second page.

Would you rather recommend to break the wide `tribble` up prior to the table creation, or could there be an option for wide table page breaks in {gt} someday?

Thanks a lot for your help!

dose_escalation |>

    locations = cells_body(

    )
  ) %>%

I'm trying to take a gt table with groupname and rowname columns set that renders beautifully in R Studio, but when I convert it to html, the groupname_cols vals get moved to the top and get all jammed together, and the other columns get moved to the left.

title: Updates to `cols_merge()`
description:
Proposed updates to `cols_merge()`
- Add `cols_merge(rows=)` argument. Only columns and rows selected will merged. But we will need some sort of mechanism for handle default values
- Add `cols_merge(pattern_missing=)` argument. This would specify what the default value of the cell should be when the cell is not merged with others. A reasonable default value here would be an empty string (like how `<<>>` handles missing cells. We also would like to be able to add something like `cols_merge(pattern = "{1} ({2})", rows = !is.na(ci), pattern_missing="{1}")`

title: cols_align_decimal() fails with accounting = TRUE when summary rows are added.
description:
Since you seem to have `summary_rows` on the mind right now . . . `cols_align_decimal()` fails for accounting formatting on the summary rows when `summary_rows` are included. Grouping *without* adding summary rows works as intended.

## Reproducible example
Reprexes include `gtsave()` to get the correct representation, since the normal reprex output is not indicative.

**1. Grouped without summary rows (working correctly):**
``` r
# Grouped, no summaries
library(gt)
dplyr::tibble(
  char = LETTERS[1:8],
  num = c(1.2, -33.52, 9023.2, -283.527, 0.401, -123.1, NA, 41),
  group = c(rep("Group 1", 4), rep("Group 2", 4))) |> 
  dplyr::group_by(group) |> 
  gt() |> 
  fmt_currency(num, 
               accounting = TRUE, 
               decimals = 2) |> 
  cols_align_decimal() |> 
  gtsave("out.png")
```

<sup>Created on 2022-12-09 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

**2. Grouped with summary rows, 2 decimals (bug)**
``` r
# Grouped, no summaries, decimals = 2
library(gt)
dplyr::tibble(
  char = LETTERS[1:8],
  num = c(1.2, -33.52, 9023.2, -283.527, 0.401, -123.1, NA, 41),
  group = c(rep("Group 1", 4), rep("Group 2", 4))) |> 
  dplyr::group_by(group) |>

## Description

Math in gt tables renders when within Rmarkdown document, but equivalent code does not result in rendered math when within a quarto document.

```{r}

title: Can `data_color` provide a deprecation message through `lifecycle` or `rlang`?
description:
https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/e263689c4fdb33e0b6f1cfc8805dbdafee4d80e6/R/data_color.R#L567-L584

gt 0.9.0 deprecates the `colors` argument in data_color and prints the warning on every call. 

Can this be changed to a "once every 8 hours" deprecation warning?

It's possible to do this with either `lifcycle` (which is a reverse dependency through ggplot2) or by passing `.frequency` and `.frequency_id` arguments in the cli_warning like

``` r
cli::cli_warn(
  c(
    "Since gt v0.9.0, the `colors` argument has been deprecated.",
    "*" = "Please use the `palette` argument to define a color palette."
  ), 
  .frequency = "regularly",
  .frequency_id = "data_color_warning"
)
#> Warning: Since gt v0.9.0, the `colors` argument has been deprecated.
#> • Please use the `palette` argument to define a color palette.
#> This warning is displayed once every 8 hours.
```

title: Broaden casting behaviour in `data_color()`
description:
## Prework

- [x] Read and abide by **gt**'s [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/0/code_of_conduct/) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Search for duplicates among the [existing issues](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues) (both open and closed).

## Proposal

Would it be possible to broaden the coercion behaviour in `data_color()` to make it friendlier to custom colour classes from packages other than **paleteer**?

When something other than a function is passed to `palette` (currently `colors` in v0.8) it's evaluated like this:

https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/e877073634feb0473a324eacab7ea47f9b98ce4c/R/data_color.R#L594-L670

Currently only paleteer palettes are cast to character. This is needed because they have a custom `colors` class.

https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/e877073634feb0473a324eacab7ea47f9b98ce4c/R/data_color.R#L668

I was wondering if it would be possible to broaden the casting behaviour to apply to anything evaluated in the `if (is.null(fn)) { ... }` environment. The change would look like this (see the last line here):

```r
  # Defuse any function supplied to `fn`; if function supplied to `colors`
  # (previous argument for this purpose) then let that take precent and
  # provide deprecation warning
  if (!is.null(colors)) {


    fn <- rlang::enquo(colors)


    if (is.character(rlang::eval_tidy(fn))) {


      palette <- rlang::eval_tidy(fn)
      fn <- NULL


      cli::cli_warn(c(
        "Since gt v0.9.0, the `colors` argument has been deprecated.",
        "*" = "Please use the `palette` argument to define a color palette."
      ))


    } else {


      cli::cli_warn(c(
        "Since gt v0.9.0, the `colors` argument has been deprecated.",
        "*" = "Please use the `fn` argument instead."
      ))
    }


  } else if (!is.null(fn)) {


    fn <- rlang::enquo(fn)


  } else {


    fn <- NULL
  }


  # Ensure that the `palette` contains something that can be used if no
  # function (as `fn`) was provided
  if (is.null(fn)) {


    # If no palette is provided, use the default palette
    if (is.null(palette)) {
      palette <- palette()
    }


    # Obtain a palette from the paletteer package if the
    # `palette` value is of the special form `<package>::<palette>`
    if (
      is.character(palette) &&
      length(palette) == 1 &&
      grepl("^.+?::.+?$", palette)
    ) {


      # Determine if the paletteer package is installed and stop the
      # function if it is not present


      if (!requireNamespace("paletteer", quietly = TRUE)) {


        cli::cli_abort(c(
          "The paletteer package is required for accessing palettes with
          the `<package>::<palette>` syntax.",
          "*" = "It can be installed with `install.packages(\"paletteer\")`."
        ))
      }


      # Parse the `palette` string and extract the two different
      # components: the package that the palette comes from and the
      # name of the palette
      palette_pkg <- unlist(strsplit(palette, "::"))[1]
      palette_name <- unlist(strsplit(palette, "::"))[2]


      # Get the table of discrete palettes hosted in the paletteer package
      palettes_tbl <- paletteer::palettes_d_names


      # Use a `filter()` statement to determine if the package part of the
      # string provided exists in paletteer
      palettes_tbl <- dplyr::filter(palettes_tbl, package == palette_pkg)


      # If the filtering results in a zero-row table, then stop the
      # function and provide messaging on what went wrong and how
      # to diagnose
      if (nrow(palettes_tbl) < 1) {
        cli::cli_abort(c(
          "The palette package name (supplied with the `<package>::<palette>`
          syntax) cannot be found in the paletteer package.",
          "*" = "Ensure that it exists in the vector accessed with
          `paletteer::paletteer_packages$Name`."
        ))
      }


      # Use a second `filter()` statement to determine if the palette name
      # component exists in paletteer for the color package
      palettes_tbl <- dplyr::filter(palettes_tbl, palette == palette_name)


      # If this filtering results in a zero-row table, stop the function
      # and provide messaging on what went wrong and how to diagnose
      if (nrow(palettes_tbl) < 1) {
        cli::cli_abort(c(
          "The palette name (supplied with the `<package>::<palette>`
          syntax) is not associated with the {palette_pkg} package as a
          discrete palette.",
          "*" = "Ensure that the combination of palette package and palette
          name exists as a record in the table accessed with
          `paletteer::palettes_d_names`."
        ))
      }


      # Getting to this stage means the palette exists in the user's
      # installation of paletteer; extract the palette with the
      # `paletteer::paletteer_d()`
      palette <- paletteer::paletteer_d(palette = palette)
    }

    # Cast palette to a character vector
    palette <- as.character(palette)
    
  }
```

This would allow other packages that implement colour classes to be compatible with `data_colour()` without forcing users to work around the current restrictions by casting colour palettes with `as.character()` themselves. You can see see an example of the required workaround in my package vignette on [using a custom colour class with gt](https://mccarthy-m-g.github.io/palettes/articles/gt.html#adding-colour). From that example, it would be nice if users could supply the colour vector directly to `data_colour()` without needing to pass it to `as.character()` first.

This change would also require updating the `@param palette` documentation. Here's a suggestion:

```r
#' @param palette A vector of color names, a color class that can be cast to a
#'   vector of color names, the name of an **RColorBrewer** palette, the name of
#'   a **viridis** palette, or a discrete palette accessible from the
#'   **paletteer** package using the `<package>::<palette>` syntax (e.g.,
#'   `"wesanderson::IsleofDogs1"`). If providing a vector of colors as a

title: Feature Request: `cols_label_with()` relabeling by function
description:
## Prework

- [x] Read and abide by **gt**'s [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/0/code_of_conduct/) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Search for duplicates among the [existing issues](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues) (both open and closed).

## Proposal

Implement a `cols_label_with()` that parallels `rename_with()`'s relationship with `rename()`. Ideally, it would  operate on the _existing_ labels, rather than names directly so that
  - you can iteratively build up with multiple functions
  - `tidyselect`ions can overlap without undoing prior work
  - weird transformations can be done manually but still wrapped in `md` or `html` via a later function call 

## Related Issues

- #701: Alternate to allowing `tidyselect`ion on the right hand side 
  - makes implementation easier and arguably easier to use, though does mean a second function
  - helps resolve the potential confusion when a `tidyselect`ion captures a column more than once.
- #817: Alternate to adding a `.fn` argument to `cols_label()`
- #1146: Would allow you to use `cols_label_with(fn = md)` to avoid places where the `from_markdown` class is lost

## Proof of Concept

```
#' Relabel columns with a function
#'
#' @param .data A table object that is created using the [gt()] function.
#' @param fn The function to apply to existing column labels.
#' @param columns The column names to apply `fn` to. Applies to all columns by default.
#' @param ... arguments to pass to
#'
#' @return An object of class `gt_tbl`.
#' @export
#'
#' @section Examples:
#'
#' Use [`countrypops`] to create a **gt** table. Relabel all the table's columns
#' with the `cols_label_with()` function to improve its presentation. It applies
#' to existing labels, rather than just names, so we can make more difficult
#' changes directly.
#'
#' ```r
#' countrypops %>%
#'   dplyr::select(-contains("code")) %>%
#'   dplyr::filter(country_name == "Mongolia") %>%
#'   tail(5) %>%
#'   gt() %>%
#'   cols_label(
#'     country_name = "Name"
#'   ) %>%
#'   cols_label_with(
#'     tools::toTitleCase
#'   )
#' ```
cols_label_with <- function(.data, fn, columns = everything(), ...) {
  fn <- rlang::as_function(fn)
  cols <- tidyselect::eval_select(
    rlang::enquo(columns),
    dt_data_get(data = .data),
    allow_rename = FALSE
  )

  names <- dt_boxhead_get_vars(data = .data)
  old_label_list <-  dt_boxhead_get(data = .data)$column_label[cols]

  nm_labels_list <- names[cols]
  labels_list <- lapply(old_label_list, function(x) fn(x, ...))

  if (!all(vapply(labels_list, is_character, logical(1L)))) {
    cli::cli_abort(
      "{.arg fn} must return a character vector, not {.obj_type_friendly {labels_list}}."
    )
  }
  if (length(labels_list) != length(nm_labels_list)) {
    cli::cli_abort(
      "{.arg fn} must return a vector of length {length(nm_labels_list)}, not {length(labels_list)}."
    )
  }

  # If no labels remain after filtering, return the data
  if (length(nm_labels_list) == 0) {
    return(.data)
  }

  for (i in seq_along(labels_list)) {
    .data <-
      dt_boxhead_edit_column_label(
        data = .data,
        var = nm_labels_list[i],
        column_label = labels_list[[i]]
      )
  }

  .data

}
```

Example of how this would work:

``` 
countrypops %>%
  dplyr::select(-contains("code")) %>%
  dplyr::filter(country_name == "Mongolia") %>%
  tail(5) %>%
  gt() %>%
  cols_label(
    country_name = "Name"
  ) %>%
  cols_label_with(
    tools::toTitleCase
  )
``` 

Output:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/28026893/204964284-bc2cb8c2-cd0a-4267-a0e5-35ca75bbd56c.png)

Or with a bit more complication, `~`, `...` and `tidyselect` (a bit contrived, but simple for quick experimentation)

```
countrypops %>%
  dplyr::filter(country_name == "Mongolia") %>%
  tail(5) %>%
  gt() %>%
  cols_label_with(
    fn = stringr::str_replace,
    pattern = '_',
    replacement = '\n'
  ) %>%
  cols_label_with(
    ~tools::toTitleCase(.) %>% md()
  ) %>% 
  cols_label_with(
    stringr::str_remove,
    pattern = '_\\d+',
    columns = -contains('3')
  )
```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/28026893/204965326-8377fd99-777e-4430-9d21-e0202bd78e27.png)


This is a bit of an opinionated approach to resolving these types of issues, particularly in that it builds off of existing _labels_ rather than column names, as that what makes sense to me conceptually. Happy to discuss and/or propose a PR if it this type of approach is useful.

title: Pass additional arguments through fmt (or support purrr-style anonymous functions)
description:
The `fmt()` function is very helpful, yet rather verbose. Some similar functions use `...` to pass through additional arguments, which would make calls simpler. Alternatively, the use of purrr-style anonymous functions would be a step forward?

In code:

```r
# Instead of
mtcars %>% gt() %>% fmt(3, fns = function (x) round(x, digits = 3)

# ... I'd love to call
mtcars %>% gt() %>% fmt(3, fns = round, digits = 3)

# ... or even purr-style anonymous functions
mtcars %>% gt() %>% fmt(3, fns = ~round(.x, digits = 3))

# base-R anonymous functions work, yet are a bit longer and still less widely known (?)
mtcars %>% gt() %>% fmt(3, fns = \(x) round(x, digits = 3))
```

If this does not seem worth the development time, maybe it would be worth giving an example of base-R anonymous functions in the docs?

title: Add `md()` and `html()` features to list argument in `cols_label()`
description:
## Prework

- [ x ] Read and abide by **gt**'s [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/0/code_of_conduct/) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [ x ] Search for duplicates among the [existing issues](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues) (both open and closed).

## Proposal

I really love the feature to add a named list of column labels to `cols_label()`. In most cases this list evolves during my data processing work prior to the table creation. I would like to use `md()` here to add a line break to my column labels. The below code works fine:

```{r}
library(gt)
library(tidyverse)

col_list1 <- list(
  "mfr" = "Manufacturer",
  "model" = "Model",
  "hp_rpm" = md("Horse Power  \n(rpm)")
)

gt::gtcars |> 
  dplyr::filter(mfr == "BMW") |> 
  dplyr::select(mfr, model, hp_rpm) |> 
  gt() |> 
  cols_label(
    .list = col_list1
  )
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/46823209/203966419-b2b495fb-a578-4c6a-8b06-71b8b78d6666.png)

However, these ones don't:

```{r}
library(gt)
library(tidyverse)

col_list2 <- as.list(c("Manufacturer", "Model", md("Horse Power  \n(rpm)"))) |> 
  purrr::set_names(c("mfr", "model", "hp_rpm"))

gt::gtcars |> 
  dplyr::filter(mfr == "BMW") |> 
  dplyr::select(mfr, model, hp_rpm) |> 
  gt() |> 
  cols_label(
    .list = col_list2
  )

col_list3 <- as.list(c("Manufacturer", "Model", "Horse Power  \n(rpm)")) |> 
  purrr::set_names(c("mfr", "model", "hp_rpm"))

gt::gtcars |> 
  dplyr::filter(mfr == "BMW") |> 
  dplyr::select(mfr, model, hp_rpm) |> 
  gt() |> 
  cols_label(
    .list = md(col_list3)
  )
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/46823209/203967045-815f36e6-e5fe-4469-b5fc-8633c9427302.png)

Thanks so much in advance!

title: Get tab_spanner_delim to retain md formatting or document that it drops it
description:
## Description

When column labels are formatted with `md()`, e.g., in `cols_label()`, that formatting gets silently dropped when you call `tab_spanner_delim()`. Ideally, I think that `tab_spanner_delim()` should retain the format - otherwise, this behaviour should be documented (and possibly even a warning issued, given that the user is unlikely to want to drop formatting that was explicitly assigned)?

## Reproducible example

``` r
library(gt)
iris[1:5,] %>%
  gt() %>% 
  cols_label(Sepal.Width = md("Sepal.*W*idth")) %>% 
  tab_spanner_delim(".")
```

## Expected result

The italics on the *W* should have been kept.

title: Some css styles cannot be isolated from Quarto's default settings
description:
## Description

As discussed in #1113 some css styles are not isolated from Quarto's defaults even when using `as_raw_html()`. I think this mainly relates to styles that are inherited from `body`. Some styles can be isolated from Quarto's defaults by wrapping the code chunk in a `div` with `style="all:initial;"`.

## Reproducible example

Multiple examples documented at https://guileless-mousse-1c0b8b.netlify.app/ (in a Quarto book to see effects).

title: Color or style a column by values in another column
Handling missing values in a col_merge
description:
Thanks for the great package! It's super useful. I wondered if it would be possible to add an option for dealing with missing data in `cols_merge` so that you could either override `sub_missing` or somehow provide an alternative pattern for cells where you only have missing data. I'm encountering a situation where I have a subgroup of data for a particular column that is missing data, so my summary with the median, min, and max are all missing. I would like to just have a single "n.p" in that cell rather, but currently, it doesn't appear as if this is possible. ``` library(tidyverse) library(gt) tibble( category = c("a","b","c","d"), median = c(5,10,8, NA_real_), min = c(1,6,4,NA_real_), max = c(8,25,12,NA_real_), ) %>% gt(rowname_col = "category") %>% cols_merge(columns = c(median, min, max), pattern = "{1}
({2},{3})") %>% tab_spanner( label = "Measurement", columns = c(median) ) %>% cols_label( median = html("Median
(min,max)") ) %>% sub_missing(columns = c(median), rows = everything(), missing_text = "n.p.") %>% sub_missing(columns = c(min,max), rows = everything(), missing_text = "") %>% tab_source_note( source_note = "n.p. = annotation not provided by authors" ) ``` Would something like this be possible?

title: Enable ability to specify order of rows **within** a group
description:
## Prework

- [x] Read and abide by **gt**'s [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/0/code_of_conduct/) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Search for duplicates among the [existing issues](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues) (both open and closed).
    - Verified in [this discussion](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/discussions/1110) 

## Proposal

Currently, the user is able to specify the order of the groups in relation to each other using  `row_group_order()`, but there is not a way to specify the order of rows within each group. This would be helpful for ordering rows within groups that have some inherent order to them that may not be obvious to {gt}.

One way would be to make it similar to the `factor()` function by adding an `ordered = ` option within the `tab_row_group()`:

```r
gt_tbl |>
    tab_row_group(
        md("**Education**"), 
        c(
            less_than_high_school,
            high_school_diploma,
            some_college,
            college_diploma
        ),
        ordered = TRUE
    )
``` 

Another way would be to add an `order_by =` option which defaults to alphabetic, but can be set as user-specified.

title: Color column based on numeric values of another column
description:
It would be great to be able to color one column based on the value of another - i.e. to specify a different target for `data_color`. Various SO discussions (e.g., [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/68673721/gt-data-color-some-columns-based-on-anothers) and [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/67722820/r-gt-color-a-column-by-another-columns-value)) have failed to come up with a solution, and #637 would need to be addressed to restore a (not very intuitive) workaround.

A possible desired code (and illustration for a use-case that I regularly encounter) would be the following, though something else might fit better in the gt API.


```
library(gt)

data <- data.frame(cat = LETTERS[1:3],
                   M_SD = c("1.1 (0.7)", "3.5 (0.6)", "2.0 (0.7)"),
                   M = c(1.1, 3.5, 2.0))

# DESIRED code
gt(data) %>% 
  cols_hide(3) %>%
  data_color(SOURCE_columns = 3, TARGET_columns = 2, 
    colors = scales::col_numeric(palette = c("red", "green"), domain = c(1, 4)))
```

title: Add function to display all ID values/labels for a gt table
description:
It can become increasingly difficult to recall the ID values associated with different labels in a gt table. There are also processes where gt will generate ID values (e.g., `tab_spanner_delim()`, etc.) while ensuring that duplicate ID values aren't produced. For the latter case, it is impossible to know what those ID values are unless one were to examine to correct component of the `gt_tbl` object.

Because it's important to know these ID values for targeting (for styles, creating borders, adding footnote marks), we should have a convenient function (`tab_info()`) that summarizes (by location) the ID values and their labels.

title: Disable Math Mode
description:
## Description

I try to include a table inside a PDF document using gt and xelatex. The tables contains formatted numbers. If I knit the document, all formatted numbers change into math mode. I postet the question [here](https://community.rstudio.com/t/gt-fmt-number-changes-font-style-to-italic/151398/) and found an answer by myself after reading through some parts of the source code.

I would like to know, if there is an easier solution than changing the default behaviour of a hidden function in the gt package I am missing right now.

## Reproducible example

```{r}
\---
title: "Reprex"
format:
  pdf:
    documentclass: article
    classoption: a4paper
    tbl-cap-location: top
    fontsize: "12pt"
    pdf-engine: xelatex
    mainfont: Arial
    sansfont: Arial
    mathfont: Arial
    include-in-header: 
      text: |
        \usepackage{lipsum}
\---

## A Header

\```r
#| label: theIssue
#| echo: false

library(gt)

my_table <- data.frame(var = rep(c("count","share"), 2),
                       group = rep(c("male","female"),each = 2),
                       value_formatted = c(850,42.5,1150,57.5),
                       value_unformatted = c(850,42.5,1150,57.5))

my_table |>
  gt(
      groupname_col = 'group',
      rowname_col = 'var'
    ) |>
  fmt_number(columns = 3, rows = c(1,3), locale = 'de_DE', decimals = 0) |>
  fmt_number(columns = 3, rows = c(2,4), locale = 'de_DE', decimals = 1) |>
  tab_spanner(label = "A Spanner", columns = 3: 4) |>
  cols_label(.list = c('var' = '','group' = '','value_formatted' = 'value_formatted','value_unformatted' = 'value_unformatted')) |>
   tab_footnote(
      footnote = "I also have a footnote.",
      locations = cells_column_spanners(spanners = 1)
    )
\```
\lipsum[5]
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/109534630/199043050-28d4f2f8-763b-47d8-b628-09dab90541ea.png)

## Expected result

Using my "hacky" workaround:

```{r}
#| label: Fix math mode
#| echo: false

# create the new function
num_fmt_factory_multi_ <- function (pattern, use_latex_math_mode = FALSE, format_fn) 
{
  names(all_contexts) <- all_contexts
  lapply(all_contexts, FUN = function(x) {
    num_fmt_factory(context = x, pattern = pattern, use_latex_math_mode = use_latex_math_mode, 
                    format_fn = format_fn)
  })
}

# https://stackoverflow.com/questions/24331690/modify-package-function
# redefine the function
environment(num_fmt_factory_multi_) <- asNamespace('gt')
assignInNamespace("num_fmt_factory_multi", num_fmt_factory_multi_, ns = "gt")

```

## Description

Texts are not left-aligned when a factor-column is used. 

## Reproducible example

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
penguin_weights <- palmerpenguins::penguins |> 
  filter(!is.na(sex)) |> 
  group_by(species) |> 
  summarise(
    Min = min(body_mass_g),
    Mean = mean(body_mass_g),
    Max = max(body_mass_g)
  )

# Species column is center-aligned
penguin_weights |> gt()

# Species column is left-aligned as expected
penguin_weights |> mutate(species = as.character(species)) |> gt()
```

I ran this code with `reprex::reprex()` but in that output everything works. I think that's because the output is not html. If I run the above code and check the html table output in both RStudio and Firefox, the `species` column is center-aligned (first code) and left-aligned (second code)

## Expected result

I would expect a consistent output in both cases. Preferably the column `species` is left-aligned.

title: Request for additional functionality for cols_align_decimal
description:
Accidentally commented on merged PR . . .probably makes sense as separate issue. This is great, @rich-iannone! It's fairly common, when using `accounting = TRUE`, that numbers are rounded (so `decimals = 0`). That combination of options (unless `drop_trailing_dec_mark = FALSE` is also used) doesn't align properly, which obviously makes sense given that there are no decimals for `cols_align_decimal()` to attack. Do you think there's any way to address that combination of options (for example by (a) faking the decimal by imputing the `drop_trailing_dec_mark = FALSE` option, running `align_to_char()`, then stripping out the decimal or (b) applying the original approach of inserting an invisible parenthesis after nonnegative numbers)? Happy to take a stab but not sure of the best approach. Thanks! ``` r library(gt) dplyr::tibble( char = LETTERS[1:8], num = c(1.2, -33.52, 9023.2, -283.527, 0.401, -123.1, NA, 41)) |> gt() |> tab_header("fmt_currency / accounting = TRUE / decimals = 0") |> fmt_currency(num, accounting = TRUE, decimals = 0) |> cols_align_decimal() ```

title: Allow for decimal alignment for Word output
description:
Now that decimal alignment is available, it can, in-principle, be added to the Word output option.

## Prework

- [x] Read and abide by **gt**'s [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/0/code_of_conduct/) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Search for duplicates among the [existing issues](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues) (both open and closed).

## Proposal

``` r
library(gt)
dplyr::tibble(
  char = LETTERS[1:9],
  num = c(1.2, -33.52, 9023.2, -283.527, NA, 0.401, -123.1, NA, 41)
) %>%
  gt() %>%
  fmt_number(
    columns = num,
    decimals = 3,
    drop_trailing_zeros = TRUE
  ) %>%
  cols_align_decimal() %>% 
  gt::gtsave("test.docx")
```

title: Repeating headers and/or column labels on multiple pages (LaTeX output)
description:
## Proposal

When a table is converted to LaTeX the column labels are only printed on the first page of output. If the table extends onto subsequent pages, only the data rows are show. It would be handy to have an option to include headers and/or column labels at the top of each page. In the `longtable` environment, this is fairly simply done by adding `\endhead` at the end of what is considered the table header.

For example, here's a random table of numbers that spans two pages in LaTeX:

```r
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)

random <- tibble(
  id = seq(1:50),
  random = runif(50)
)

t <- gt(random) %>%
  as_latex() %>%
  as.character()
```

The raw TeX (`t`) is:

    \\begin{longtable}{rr}\n\\toprule\nid & random \\\\ \n\\midrule\n1 & 0.26041117 \\\\ \n2 & 0.78843314 \\\\ \n...

The top of the second page looks like this when the TeX is rendered to PDF:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2984138/191106837-fc5dd50f-eb7a-4d6c-bddf-91a7c70bfd4c.png)

If `\\endhead\n` is placed just after `\\midrule\n` in the raw output, the table will be rendered with the "id" and "random" headers on each page.

Like this:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2984138/191106915-8db1b2c4-f10b-4ea9-98a7-0d7c2ae79548.png)

I took a quick look at the code and it seems like this could be added to `latex_heading_row` and/or `latex_group_row` of `R/utils_render_latex.R`, but I'm not sure how options might get passed in here and there would be some additional logic to handle the placement of `\endhead` when there's both gt headers and column labels.

Maybe similar to #194

## Description

When rendering to word (docx) format with quarto, adding captions with `#|tbl-cap` breaks the formating of tables with groupname rows or footnotes. The cells of the groupname or footnote rows will not be merged in Word as they should be.
I'm not sure if this is actually an issue with quarto (1.1.245).
Possibly related to #994 

## Reproducible example

format: docx
---
```

```{r}
library(gt)
library(tidyverse)
footnote <- "Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit, ..."
```

```{r}
head(mtcars) %>% 
	group_by(cyl) %>% 
	gt() %>% 
	tab_footnote(footnote=footnote)
```

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "A caption"
head(mtcars) %>% 
	group_by(cyl) %>% 
	gt() %>% 
	tab_footnote(footnote=footnote)
```

Footnotes and groupname rows should be merged in .docx like this (as is produced with the caption-free code chunk of the reprex):

title: span labels not emitted correctly to rtf
description:
To reproduce:
```
library(gt)

mydf <- data.frame(x = 5, y = "hi", z = "what?")
mygt <- mydf |>
  gt() |>
  tab_spanner(label ="spaannning", columns = c(y, z))

rtf_str <- as_rtf(mygt)
```

Then `cat` `rtf_str` to the file of your choice and open the file in an editor/viewer that supports RTF.

For me, I tried TextEdit  (Version 1.17 (380.2)) and LibreOffice 7.3.5.2. Both of these display (different) incorrect tables:

![gt_rtf_loaded_screenshot](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/908721/189775730-aa2a41f9-58c6-45c2-9794-7be8b66c1b3f.png)

Looking at `rtf_str` we see:

title: consequence of breaking change in htmltools `0.5.3`
description: I see from the release of [0.5.3](https://github.com/rstudio/htmltools/releases/tag/v0.5.3) and issue https://github.com/rstudio/htmltools/issues/305 that there was no expected use-case, so just want to flag this. Inline printing `gt::gt()` tables (though not `knitr::kable()` tables) leaves the ``{=html} tag in the printed output. ```` # no problem ```{r} x <-gt::gt(head(mtcars)) x ``` # prefix/afix `r x` ```` How the tagged output looks - # Use case example My frequent use case in reports is rendering tables/graphs _or_ text _or_ nothing, depending on available data and/or other specific conditions. ```` ```{r} knitr::opts_chunk$set( echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE ) output_fun <- function(x){ if(x <.5){ "some text" } else if(x < .8){ x } # implied else NULL } a <- output_fun(.3) b <- output_fun(.6) c <- output_fun(.9) ``` ```{r} a b c ``` `r a` `r b` `r c` ```` I don't know if this is a "normal" use-case, or whether this matches the expected behaviour on your end, or whether there is a satisfactory work-around. Seeing that there didn't seem to be an expected use-case made me think it would be reasonable to bring it to your attention. For the time-being, I'm just going to roll-back to 0.5.2. Many thanks for continuing to provide such excellent tools!

title: background colors render to word document in rmd but not qmd
description:
If you render the below in an rmarkdown document, colors appear in the `color` column just fine when you output to DOCX. In a quarto document however the background colors do not display.

````
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)

df_text <- tibble::tibble(index = c("C-1", "C-2"),
                          finding = c("A finding.", "Another finding."),
                          color = c("red", "blue")) 

df_text %>% 
  gt::gt() %>% 
  gt::tab_style(
    style = gt::cell_fill(color = "red"),
    locations = gt::cells_body(
      column = color,
      rows = stringr::str_detect(color, "red")
    )
  ) %>% 
  gt::tab_style(
    style = gt::cell_fill(color = "blue"),
    locations = gt::cells_body(
      column = color,
      rows = stringr::str_detect(color, "blue")
    )
  ) 

````

title: Set table header height
description:
Hi!

Is there any way to set a table header to a specific height?

I have a collection of tables, all with same width. Depending on how long is the text on the title, it breaks a line and the header height increases. It is great for a single table, but I need all the collection to match their heights.

Thanks in advance!

title: Best practice for cross-output indentation with gt
description:
Hey @rich-iannone ! Thank you for all the amazing work you do on {gt} ❤️ 

In {gtsummary}, I've been using `tab_style()` to indent rows in the resulting tables (example below). But this method only works for HTML.

```r
gt::tab_style(
  style = gt::cell_text(indent = gt::px(10), align = "left"),
  locations = gt::cells_body(...)
)
```

I want to update to use non-breaking spaces for the indentation, as this is supported by HTML, PDF, RTF, and Word. I am using the HTML non-breaking space `" "` to place the indentation. To get {gt} to recognize the spaces, I am formatting the cells with `fmt_markdown()`.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26774684/187100852-69e86d62-522d-4cba-8ac9-98ed43d815e3.png)

My testing indicates that this solution works well for all the output types. But I don't feel 100% confident about the solution. It feels strange to me to process cells with a function that formats markdown text to get gt to recognize the HTML code in the cell. I do not want to implement an "off-label" use of `fmt_markdown()` in case the off-label use to later turned off.

**Finally the question** Is this how you recommend I implement indentation for all the output formats? Is it ok to use the markdown formatting function for HTML code? THANK YOU @rich-iannone !

One limitation of this method, is that it cannot be applied to numeric columns that have a formatting function applied to them. For example, if a column is numeric and I am applying `fmt_percent()` to the cell, I can't update the formatter to also place the `" "` in front of the formatted result to indent it.

title: Allow `suffixing` of `vec_fmt_*()` to accept custom scales and suffixes
description:
## Prework

- [x] Search for duplicates among the [existing issues](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues) (both open and closed).

## Proposal

First of all, thanks for providing the `vec_fmt_*()` functions! This is going to be so useful when making quarto/rmarkdown reports.

For non-English users, there's a good chance that the existing suffixes (K, M, B, T) for `vec_fmt_number()`, etc. is not a good choice for local readers. However, currently there's no way to change the scaling factors along with the suffixing characters. I suggest allowing the use of named vectors for the `suffixing` option to achieve the goal. For example, to define a list of large numbers in ten thousands (with suffix "w") and a hundred millions (with suffix "y"), one would write: `vec_fmt_number(x, suffixing = c("w" = 10000, "y" = 100000000))`.

title: Warning in print method: `length(x) = 2 > 1' in coercion to 'logical(1)`
description:
## Description

I the recent release of R 4.2.1 (or maybe 4.2.0?), additional messaging to users have been included when a `if ()` statement includes a logical with length greater than one.

It appears that this messaging is now being triggered in the gt print method when certain attributes are applied to the gt table. Example below!

title: Footnote placement is ignored in summary rows
description: Footnote marks can be placed to the left or right of the content in the targeted location. While this works fine for table body cells, it does not for any summary cells. In the following gt table, both footnote glyphs should be located on the left of the summary values (using the default `"auto"` value for `placement` in `tab_footnote()` should internally yield a `"left"` value placement based on cell content alignment). ```r library(gt) library(tidyverse) # Create a table that creates a stub and # row groups based on magic column names # Input table tbl <- dplyr::tribble( ~groups, ~rowname, ~value, ~value_2, "A", "1", NA, 260.1, "A", "2", 184.3, 84.4, "A", "3", 342.3, 126.3, "A", "4", 234.9, NA, "B", "1", 190.9, 832.5, "B", "2", 743.3, 281.2, "B", "3", 252.3, 732.5, "B", "4", 344.7, NA, "C", "1", 197.2, 818.0, "C", "2", 284.3, 394.4 ) # Create a display table with summary rows summary_tbl <- tbl %>% gt(groupname_col = "groups") %>% summary_rows( groups = c("A", "C"), columns = "value", fns = list( ~mean(., na.rm = TRUE), ~sum(., na.rm = TRUE), ~sd(., na.rm = TRUE) ) ) %>% tab_footnote( footnote = "Note for Summary A.", locations = cells_summary( groups = "A", columns = value, rows = 1 ) ) %>% tab_footnote( footnote = "Note for Summary C.", locations = cells_summary( groups = "C", columns = value, rows = 1 ) ) %>% sub_missing(columns = c(value, value_2)) %>% tab_options( summary_row.background.color = "#FFFEEE", row_group.background.color = "lightblue" ) summary_tbl ```

title: Generating better reprex with gt
`rows_hide()` function to compliment `cols_hide()`
description:
## Proposal for `rows_hide()` function

After the gt object has been created and formatted, it is possible to hide particular columns. There are cases were hiding rows would also be useful. 

This is especially important for groups of data scientists where `gt` is the basis of table formatting. For example, complex report tables with titles, footnotes, and other styling choices might get made by some centralized process, but then individuals might want to grab the stylized table, select just certain rows and columns, and then update the title but *not* have to worry about copying over the footnotes or other formatting details.

    # Some function has produced a table
    my_table <- iris |>
      group_by(Species) |>
      summarize(across(where(is.numeric), mean)) |>
      gt(rowname_col = 'Species') |>
      # Now have a bunch of formating
      gt::tab_header('Some Title')
    
    # And now I need to take extract just a subset of the rows/colums
    # for a report, but we shouldn't copy/paste all of the formatting
    # code
    
    my_table |>
      cols_hide(contains('Sepal')) # this works to hide extraneous columns...
    
    # But why isn't there a rows_hide() equivalent? What if I need to 
    # hide the setosa row?
    my_table |>
      cols_hide(contains('Sepal')) |>
      rows_hide(Species == 'setosa')   # This function doesn't exist.

I would expect that `rows_hide()` would be able to specify a body row in all the usual ways that `cells_body(rows=)` can select rows.

Looking into the code for `cols_hide()`, it appears that there is a flag being set that marks if the column is to be displayed. Is it reasonable to create a corresponding rows flag that will control if a particular row is displayed?

A design question is "What to do if there are summary rows?" Because we are *hiding* (and not removing), I think that the summary rows shouldn't be changed. However, there should be a way to also hide the `summary_row()` output.

title: Aggregation of column summary feature requests
description:
## Prework - [x] Read and abide by **gt**'s [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/0/code_of_conduct/) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Search for duplicates among the [existing issues](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues) (both open and closed). ### Duplicates or related issues - #382 - add `summary_column()` to match `summary_rows()` - #632 - specify subset of columns to summarize ACROSS column in a `rowwise()` fashion - #690 - when calculating a summary of a specific column, reference another column - #952 - reference multiple columns in a summary - potentially generate a new column ## Proposal Provide an equivalent to `gt::summary_rows()` but for columns (ie `dplyr::rowwise()` operation). This is "possible" today but not as low-level as it could be and relies on a somewhat clunky `gtExtras::duplicate_columns()` to create a duplicate column and modify it in place, rather than a `gt`-native approach. Components working: - grouped/ungrouped data column `rowwise()` operations - Basic support for any summarizing function by `name` or `"name"` - control placement of output column Components that will still need to be hashed out: - Optionally affect summary row outputs (currently ignored) - `summary_rows()` to optionally reference column summaries - Convert to proper `gt` internals rather than `gtExtras::duplicate_column()` hack - Should it be added to last column of table with visual separation like `summary_rows()` double line
gt_sum_column() function definition ``` r library(gt) library(gtExtras) library(dplyr,w=F) gt_sum_column <- function(gt_object, columns, fn = sum, name = "sum_col", after = dplyr::last_col()){ summary_fn <- function(all_df, sum_type){ all_df %>% rowwise() %>% mutate(sum_col = do.call(sum_type, list(c_across({{ columns }})))) %>% ungroup() %>% pull(sum_col) } res_col_names <- gt:::resolve_cols_c( expr = {{ columns }}, data = gt_object ) gt_object <- gtExtras::gt_duplicate_column( gt_object, column = res_col_names[1], after = {{ after }}, dupe_name = name ) gt_object[["_data"]] <- gt_object[["_data"]] %>% dplyr::rowwise() %>% dplyr::mutate({{ name }} := do.call(fn, list(dplyr::c_across({{ columns }})))) %>% dplyr::ungroup() gt_object } ```
```r base_gt <- dplyr::tibble( group = c(rep("A", 3), rep("B", 2)), a = 1:5, b = 5:1, c = seq(0.1, 0.5, length.out = 5) ) %>% gt(groupname_col = "group") base_gt %>% gt_sum_column(c(a:c), fn = max, after = c) ``` ``` r base_gt %>% gt_sum_column(c(a:c), fn = min, after = c) ``` ``` r base_gt %>% gt_sum_column(c(a:c), fn = "mean", after = c) ``` ``` r base_gt %>% gt_sum_column(c(a:c), fn = "sum", after = c) ``` Created on 2022-06-17 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1) To help us read any code you include (optional) please try to follow the [tidyverse style guide](https://style.tidyverse.org/). title: Convert gt to grob for cowplot + patchwork
description:
## Prework

- [x] Read and abide by **gt**'s [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/0/code_of_conduct/) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Search for duplicates among the [existing issues](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues) (both open and closed).

## Proposal

In some situations it would be helpful to add a table into the layout of some graphics. While this is possible in RMarkdown/Quarto/HTML/etc, some users prefer `patchwork` or `cowplot` when aggregating their plots for other tools.

This would add a dependency for `grid` (already there from `ggplot2`) and `png`.

This is related to https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/420 and https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/180 - but per Rich, opening as a new issue/FR.

``` r
library(patchwork)
library(ggplot2)
library(cowplot)
library(gt)

gt_tab <- head(mtcars) |> 
  gt()

test_plot <- mtcars |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = disp, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    alt = "a plot with text"
  )

gt_grob <- function(gt_object, ...){
  
  out_name <- file.path(
    tempfile(pattern = "file", tmpdir = tempdir(), fileext = ".png")
  )
  
  gtsave(gt_object, out_name, ...)
  
  in_png <- png::readPNG(out_name)
  
  on.exit(file.remove(out_name), add=TRUE)
  
  grid::rasterGrob(in_png)
  
}

gt_plot <- gt_grob(gt_tab)

combo_plot <- test_plot +
  wrap_elements(gt_plot)

cow_plot <- plot_grid(test_plot, gt_plot)

ggsave("patchwork.png", combo_plot, height = 3.5, width = 10)
ggsave("cowplot.png", cow_plot, height = 3.5, width = 10)
```

title: Ensure that LaTeX output does not use `\caption` for the table heading since that should be reserved for a functional caption
description:
If I generate a LaTeX table with a table heading (using `tab_header()`) the resulting LaTeX code generated contains the use of a `\caption` command. For example, I could use

```r
exibble %>% gt() %>% tab_header("title") %>% as_latex() %>% as.character() %>% cat()
```

and get

```
\captionsetup[table]{labelformat=empty,skip=1pt}
\begin{longtable}{rlclllrll}
\caption*{

title: Spanners do not exist when chaining tab_spanner_delim into tab_footnote
description:
## Description

I have some code written with gt version ~3.*, which uses `tab_spanner_delim(delim="#")` to create spanners for the columns of my dataframe, and immediately pipe that into tab_footnote(footnote="abc", locations=cells_column_spanners(spanners="name_of_spanner")). As of gt version ~5.* this has stopped working, and I receive an error stating that "The following spanner(s) do not exist in the data:". However, when I look at the created gt object, the spanners were correctly created, and are listed under spanners > spanner_labels. I have tried using the examples from the wiki using the Iris dataset, and receive the same errors.

## Reproducible example
### Create a gt object with the spanner labels
`gt <- iris %>%
      dplyr::group_by(Species) %>%
      dplyr::slice(1:4) %>%
      gt() %>%
      tab_spanner_delim(delim = ".")` 

### Pipe to footnote and receive error
`gt <- iris %>%
      dplyr::group_by(Species) %>%
      dplyr::slice(1:4) %>%
      gt() %>%
      tab_spanner_delim(delim = ".") %>% tab_footnote(footnote = "test", locations=cells_column_spanners("Sepal"))` 

## Expected result

This used to work and allow me to specify a footnote for a specific spanner.

title: Indicating rows by number is inconsistent on grouped tables
description:
## Prework

* [x] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/0/code_of_conduct/) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
* [x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue.
* [x] For any problems you identify, a [minimal reproducible example](https://www.tidyverse.org/help/) so the maintainer can troubleshoot. A reproducible example is:
    * [x] **Runnable**: post enough R code and data so any onlooker can create the error on their own computer.
    * [x] **Minimal**: reduce runtime wherever possible and remove complicated details that are irrelevant to the issue at hand.
    * [x] **Readable**: format your code according to the [tidyverse style guide](https://style.tidyverse.org/).

## Question

What would you like to know?

In a traditional `gt` table without groups - the literal row number is equivalent to the row "ID". However, when using `groupname_col` in `gt` - the row ids are maintained as the "input" dataframe even though the represented data is now "out of order".

This can make referring to specific rows by number very inconsistent between the "represented" data in the table and the actual data as passed to `gt()`.

I have written one function that "corrects" for this nuance in [`tab_style_by_grp`](https://jthomasmock.github.io/gtExtras/reference/tab_style_by_grp.html), part of the complexity is that the "groups" are created according to when they are first "observed" in the data - so unless passed as an already ordered factor the groups can be unpredictable on top of the ordering of the rows themselves.

It would be great if there was either a helper function to "correct" for this behavior or if the row numbering was always consistent with the final output representation rather than the input dataframe.

I've included an example below of the inconsistent row number/id.

``` r
library(gt)

OkabeIto <- c("#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#F0E442", 
              "#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#CC79A7", "#999999")

scales::show_col(OkabeIto)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/Qk6TIOU.png)

``` r

row_sty <- function(tab, row){
  
  OkabeIto <- c("#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#F0E442", 
                "#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#CC79A7", "#999999")
  tab %>%
    tab_style(
      cell_fill(color = OkabeIto[row]),
      locations = cells_body(rows = row)
    )
}

df <- head(mtcars) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(row_id = dplyr::row_number(), .before = 1)


tab1 <- gt(df) %>%
  row_sty(1) %>% 
  row_sty(3) %>% 
  row_sty(5) %>%
  gtExtras::gtsave_extra("ordered.png", selector = "table")

magick::image_read("ordered.png")
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/iOZw3mY.png)

``` r

tab2 <- gt(df, groupname_col = "cyl") %>%
  row_sty(1) %>% 
  row_sty(3) %>% 
  row_sty(5) %>%
  gtExtras::gtsave_extra("scrambled.png", selector = "table")

magick::image_read("scrambled.png")
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/1k6vA73.png)

title: Using paletteer in data_color has name conflicts
description:
## Description

When using `paletteer` inside `data_color()` there is a potential for name conflict, specifically when `type` is a column within the underlying dataframe it is interpreted within the context of the dataframe inside `paletteer` functions that AFAIK shouldn't be accessing/referncing the underlying data. As discovered in [`gtExtras` Issue 50](https://github.com/jthomasmock/gtExtras/issues/50)

## Reproducible example

``` r
library(gt)

base_gt <- dplyr::tibble(
  "name" = c("A", "B", "C"),
  type = c("a", "b", "c"), 
  value = c(0.1, 0.6, 0.9)
) %>%
  gt()

# type is not present in the global env
type
#> Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos): object 'type' not found

# evaluates type from the underlying dataframe
base_gt %>% 
  data_color(
    columns = value,
    colors = scales::col_numeric(
      palette = 
        paletteer::paletteer_d(
          palette = "ggsci::red_material",
          type = type
        ) %>% as.character(),
      domain = c(0,1)
    )
  )
#> Error in match.arg(type): 'arg' must be of length 1

# allows for operations on type, where type == "a"
# so it throws an error not matching discrete or continuous

base_gt %>% 
  data_color(
    columns = value,
    colors = scales::col_numeric(
      palette = 
        paletteer::paletteer_d(
          palette = "ggsci::red_material",
          type = type[1]
        ) %>% as.character(),
      domain = c(0,1)
    )
  )
#> Error in match.arg(type): 'arg' should be one of "discrete", "continuous"
```
