title: Add row spanner label feature
description:
Is there a way to make spanner row labels (similar to spanner column labels, but for rows) or to re-position the row group label to the side? 
![gt_row_spanners](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/64860407/81456364-e1c8e880-9146-11ea-83a3-1dc72e16d1a6.png)

For example, data with two rows per "group" would be much cleaner with a single group label to the left of the plot than as many small tables stacked vertically (with the row group feature) or with duplicate labels (with the stub feature).

Here is a mock-up of one potential use: 
![gt_row_spanners_example](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/64860407/81455465-27d07d00-9144-11ea-97e4-9e85f31fbcc4.png)

Filed as issue here per request from [RStudio community](https://community.rstudio.com/t/gt-row-group-formatting-spanner/64717?u=megan_huber)

title: Retain data attributes in `gt()`?
description:
Would it be possible to retain the attributes of the data in the return of gt()? That way, one could create a table with footnotes etc from one data object in one pipe. 

Tracing the gt() function with two extra lines 
` attribs <- attributes(data)` at the start and `attributes(data)$original <- attribs` at the end
allows me to run the following, which I find very helpful:

```
my_fun(x) %>% gt::gt() %>%
  gt::tab_header(attributes(.)$original$title) %>% gt::tab_footnote(footnote = attributes(.)$original$footnote, location = gt::cells_column_labels("indirect"))
```

title: Update GitHub Actions workflow to use the new RSPM location
description:
Currently for Ubuntu R CMD check jobs we use the `https://demo.rstudiopm.com/all/__linux__/xenial/latest` location. However, that has been decommissioned and the replacement for that is `https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/cran/__linux__/xenial/latest`.

With this change, there is also the opportunity to put a version number in *all* key names (for both the R CMD check and the pkgdown workflows).

title: Can't simultaneously change the formatting of all cells
description:
I am trying to change the formatting of each cell in the gtable to create multiline cells when multiple entries exist per cell. This works fine when I target a single row across all columns, but when I target all rows, the contents of the first row get copied to the remaining rows. So the function doesn't iterate through rows correctly. Further, I can't seem to find a way (although maybe I'm just missing it) to loop the fmt() call to iteratively format each row. Thanks!! ```r ``` [CNVsAnnotatedReshaped.txt](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/files/4565078/CNVsAnnotatedReshaped.txt) cnvDTcast <- fread("CNVsAnnotatedReshaped.txt", header = T) tab1 <- cnvDTcast %>% dplyr::group_by(Treatment) %>% gt(rowname_col = "Replicate") %>% fmt(columns = everything(), fns = function(x) { parts <- strsplit(x, "\\|")[[1]] splitLoop <- unlist(lapply(seq(1, length(parts), 2), function(y){ string <- paste0(parts[y], ",", "
", parts[y+1], ",") return(string) } ) ) allConcat <- paste(splitLoop, collapse = "
") fixConcat <- sub(",
NA,$", "", allConcat) html(fixConcat) } )

title: Decimal mark alignment
description:
Perform alignment on decimal marks in all number-based `fmt_*()` functions. This adds the option `dec_mark_align`, which either takes `TRUE` or `FALSE` (the default).

Originally suggested by @drolejoel in https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/535, but moved to this issue since there were multiple requests in that issue.

title: Could fmt_percent() have a 'scale_by' argument?
description:
I commonly use tables where the percent values are already percents, not proportions. Could we add a `scale_by` argument like the one that already exists in `gt::fmt_number()`?

This would also match the `scale` argument commonly used in ggplot2 legend labels using `scales::percent_format()`.

Thanks for considering!

title: creating gt is very slow even on small datasets
description:
I am looking for an output like this.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22342596/79754397-1c541800-8335-11ea-843f-f2d01fd7060f.png)

I wrote a function to get that output. It takes a transformed data and some values to generate that table dynamically.

```
createGT <- function(dtTransformed,
                     uniqueZones,
                     Title = "Defects Data",
                     SubTitle = "filtered",
                     rowStudHead = "Defect Names") {
  
  setDT(dtTransformed)
  
  numericCol <- names(dtTransformed[, .SD, .SDcols = -c("defect")])
  
  dtnames <- names(dtTransformed)
  
  newdtnames <- stri_replace_all_regex(str = dtnames,
                                       pattern = "_[^_]+",
                                       replacement = "")
  
  colLables <- mapply(
    FUN = function(x, y) {
      x = y
    },
    dtnames,
    newdtnames,
    SIMPLIFY = FALSE,
    USE.NAMES = TRUE
  )
  
  mainTable <- gt(data = dtTransformed,
                  rowname_col = "defect")  %>%
    cols_label(.list = colLables) %>%
    tab_stubhead(label = rowStudHead) %>%
    tab_header(title = Title,
               subtitle = SubTitle)

  lapply(uniqueZones, function(x) {
    mainTable <<- mainTable %>%
      tab_spanner(label = x,
                  columns = stri_detect_regex(str = dtnames,
                                              pattern = x))
  })

  
  mainTable <- mainTable %>%
    grand_summary_rows(
      columns = numericCol,
      fns = list(
        MINIMUM = ~ min(., na.rm = TRUE),
        MAXIMUM = ~ max(., na.rm = TRUE),
        AVERAGE = ~ mean(., na.rm = TRUE),
        TOTAL = ~ sum(., na.rm = TRUE)
      ),
      formatter = fmt_number,
      use_seps = FALSE
    ) %>%
    data_color(
      columns = numericCol,
      colors = scales::col_numeric(
        palette = RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(n = 9, name = "Reds"),
        domain = NULL
      )
    ) %>%
    tab_style(style = list(
      cell_fill(color = "black", alpha = 0.7),
      cell_text(
        color = "#fff",
        weight = "bold",
        size = "xx-large"
      )
    ),
    locations = (cells_title(groups = c("title")))) %>%
    tab_style(style = list(
      cell_fill(color = "white"),
      cell_borders(sides = "bottom", weight = "2px")
    ),
    locations = (cells_title(groups = c("subtitle")))) %>%
    tab_style(
      style = list(
        cell_fill(color = "lightcyan"),
        cell_borders(
          sides = c("right", "left"),
          color = "#d3d3d3",
          weight = "2px"
        ),
        cell_text(weight = "bold",
                  size = "large")
      ),
      locations =
        cells_column_spanners(spanners = uniqueZones)
    ) %>%
    tab_style(style = list(
      cell_fill(color = "lightcyan"),
      cell_text(weight = "bold", style = "italic"),
      cell_borders(sides = "bottom", weight = "2px")
    ),
    locations = cells_stubhead()) %>%
    tab_style(
      style = list(
        cell_fill(color = "lightcyan"),
        cell_text(style = "italic"),
        cell_borders(sides = "bottom", weight = "2px")
      ),
      locations = (cells_column_labels(columns = numericCol))
    ) %>%
    tab_style(style = cell_fill(color = "lightcyan"),
              locations = cells_stub())
  
  return(mainTable)
}
```

title: Summary rows shouldn't require that the table be presorted by the group variable
description:
I attach a data frame. If I run the following code on it, then the summary row is calculated wrong.

```
data = gt(data = costs2 %>% mutate(COSTS=as.numeric(COSTS)), rowname_col = "REF", groupname_col = "LAB" ) %>%
  summary_rows(
    groups = TRUE,
    columns = vars(COSTS),
    fns = list(total = ~sum(., na.rm = TRUE)))
```

If I resort the data as follows then it calculates correctly.

data = gt(data = costs2 %>% mutate(COSTS=as.numeric(COSTS)) %>% dplyr::arrange(LAB), rowname_col = "REF", groupname_col = "LAB" ) %>%
  summary_rows(
    groups = TRUE,
    columns = vars(COSTS),
    fns = list(total = ~sum(., na.rm = TRUE)))
```

This is not very user friendly, expecting people to know to do this. I really recommend changing this, I nearly ditched using the package because of it.

Nice work otherwise!

[costs2.rda.zip](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/files/4497209/costs2.rda.zip)

title: Typical table 1 in medical science
description:
Thank you for your great efforts to develop a package that provides a general grammer for tables.
I am always looking for new packages to make reproducable "print-ready" tables. Unfortenately most previous attempts do not really fit my needs. In the medical sciences, the typical table 1 (patient characteristics) has one important feature. Here, most of the times, patient groups are in columns and the variables are in the rows (kind of transposed wide format). Moreover, mostly, one cell contains different aggregated information such mean +- standard deviation, counts with percentage in brackets, or median with interquartile range in brackets.
So I would like to have package to build my tables row by row with optional grouping and optional concatination of statistical results. 
Something like the table "Tech giants invade each other's turf". But in google picture search (table 1 patient characteristics) you can find many other examples.
I am not sure, how I would do this with the gt package.

title: Line breaks in cells need additional CSS in `gt_table` style to display correctly for HTML output
description:
Hello! Another line break issue which I can't seem to find an answer for.

When including \n to break a line within cells these do not accurately display within an html table.

To correctly display line breaks the addition to the table style of: white-space:pre resolves this issue. This could be an optional flag in the gt() function if you didn't think it should be included permanently.

Thanks in advance.

example:

`gtcars %>%
  mutate(hp(rpm) = paste0(hp, "\n", "(", hp_rpm, ")")) %>%
  select(mfr, model, hp(rpm)) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "mfr")`

produces this table with no line breaks
![egz](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/54158784/79410957-c65e3800-7ff5-11ea-8e99-4b98507e4580.PNG)

by including white-space:pre in the gt_table css style
![eg2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/54158784/79410986-da099e80-7ff5-11ea-81ea-8677e17d5aa0.PNG)

we can now display line breaks correctly
![eg3](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/54158784/79411011-e7268d80-7ff5-11ea-91ca-27832cf95f27.PNG)

title: `summary_rows()` for one group in multi-group table
description:
When a table has multiple grouping variables (and therefore the groupnames show up as Group 1 - Subgroup 1), is it possible to generate `summary_rows` for the group higher in the hierarchy (Group 1 in this example)? 

I have tried calling out only the "higher" group in addition to the subgrouping you get with `groups = TRUE`  but get an error.


``` r
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)

exibble %>%
  mutate(subgroup = c(1,1,2,2,1,1,2,2)) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = c("group", "subgroup"),
     rowname_col = "row") %>%
  summary_rows(groups = TRUE,
               columns = vars(num),
               fns = list(Total = ~sum(., na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  summary_rows(groups = "group",
               columns = vars(num),
               fns = list(Total = ~sum(., na.rm = TRUE)))
#> Error: All `groups` should be available in the gt object:
#>  * The following groups aren't present: group
```

title: The `data_color()` function is slow
description:
When using the `data_color()` function in an example (where a few dozen cells needed to be colored), I noticed sluggish performance (in the range of 6-8 seconds on my system). Here is a reproducible example demonstrating this: ```r library(gt) library(tidyverse) library(glue) library(omsvg) library(eqn2svg) library(paletteer) # Define a formula for SZA (Solar Zenith Angle) sza_formula <- "\\cos \\theta_s = \\sin \\alpha_s = \\sin \\Phi \\sin \\delta + \\cos \\Phi \\cos \\delta \\cos h" %>% eqn2svg::eqn2svg() # Create a gt table based on the `sza` dataset sza %>% dplyr::filter(latitude == 20) %>% dplyr::select(-latitude) %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(sza)) %>% tidyr::spread(key = "tst", value = sza) %>% gt(rowname_col = "month") %>% fmt_missing( columns = TRUE, missing_text = "" ) %>% data_color( columns = TRUE, colors = scales::col_numeric( palette = paletteer::paletteer_d( palette = "ggsci::orange_material" ) %>% as.character(), domain = c(0, 90), na.color = "#FFFFFF" ) ) %>% tab_stubhead(label = html("month
(20°N)")) %>% tab_header( title = glue::glue("{omsvg::SVG_la('sun')} SZA {omsvg::SVG_la('moon')}") %>% md() ) %>% tab_source_note( glue::glue( "These calculations are made possible with the SZA formula: {sza_formula}.
", "More details in this Wikipedia article.") %>% html() ) %>% tab_options( heading.title.font.size = px(24), heading.border.bottom.style = "none", column_labels.border.top.style = "none", column_labels.font.size = "smaller", table.font.size = "smaller", data_row.padding = px(4) ) %>% opt_align_table_header("left") %>% opt_all_caps() ``` The underlying implementation for `data_color()` needs to be refactored. We can use **profvis** for the profiling study.

title: add significant figures to number formatting

- The alignment should be left, right, centered or on the decimal point. The latter is very important for pharma reporting and is pretty much impossible to do currently. An example of decimal alignment is available in [Microsoft Word's decimal tabulator in tables](https://www.datanumen.com/blogs/line-numbers-decimal-points-word-tables/)

title: Release gt 0.2.0
description:
- [x] If not a new package, make sure any warnings/errors in CRAN check results page are fixed

- [x] Create a GitHub issue called "Release checklist for [version]". Include the steps below as checklist steps.

- [x] Create branch labelled v[version]-rc, for example, v1.5.2-rc (the "rc" stands for "Release Candidate").

- [x] Change the DESCRIPTION and NEWS on this branch to change the version number to the desired version for CRAN, e.g. from 1.5.1.9008 to 1.5.2.

- [x] Commit and push to the RC branch.

- [x] Clean your package directory to remove any extraneous files, including ones that are git-ignored. (Warning, this will delete any unsaved buffers in RStudio! Also, be sure to close RStudio before taking this step!) git clean -xdf .

- [x] Build your package. I (jcheng) personally do it from the Mac command line like this:
PATH=$PATH:/Applications/RStudio.app/Contents/MacOS/pandoc R CMD build [pkgdir]

- [x] Do a sanity check by installing/testing the built package.

- [x] Perform revdep check using https://github.com/r-lib/revdepcheck, if this is not the initial CRAN release.

- [x] Run R CMD check --as-cran pkg_version.tar.gz both locally and on win-builder. You can also use https://r-hub.github.io/rhub/. I (jcheng) don't know how much it matters but I have this file as my ~/.R/Makevars:
CFLAGS +=              -Wall -pipe -pedantic -std=gnu99 -g -O0
CXXFLAGS +=            -Wall -pipe -Wno-unused -pedantic -g -O0
CXX11FLAGS +=            -Wall -pipe -Wno-unused -pedantic -g -O0
**jcheng5: win-builder r-devel queue was really long so I compiled R-devel locally on my Mac. Windows was covered by win-builder old and release.**

- [x] Read every bullet point in the CRAN Policies document if this is the first release of the package. I usually print it out and check off the items one by one.

- [x] Submit to CRAN via their online form.

- [x] If there are R CMD check warnings that are unavoidable, make sure to explain them in the comments.

- [x] If rejected, make changes on the RC branch and bump the fourth (patch) version component, i.e. 1.5.2.1.

- [x] When accepted, tag the RC branch with a v1.5.2.1 tag (or whatever version you finally ended up getting accepted), and push the tag to origin.

- [x] Merge RC into master.

- [ ] On master, change the package version to 1.5.2.9000.

title: Audit all internal and unsafe uses of `glue::glue()`
description:
There are several instances where `glue::glue()` is used to generate strings with local variables. The problem is that, by default, the search path for `glue()` includes all environments. There are some steps to make the (convenient) use of `glue()` safer:

(1) Use the `base::get()` function as the transformer function (supplying it to the `.transformer` arg).
(2) Specify an environment for the `.envir` arg; `new.env()` is a pretty good choice, `emptyenv()` is even better if that's possible.
(3) Use named arguments in the `glue()` call for replacements, if possible; these will take precedence over vars in the search path.

The dev version of **glue** has the `glue_safe()` function. Once that's available in a CRAN release of **glue**, it should be used.

title: A random table id shouldn't be stored in the `gt_tbl` object
description: The `id` value is used for isolating a gt table's CSS from the rest of the document. However, currently, this is stored as an option value inside the `_options` table. A problem arises when we are reusing a gt object multiple times in an RMarkdown doc for instance, and `tab_options()` are used. We effectively get the same 'random' id in multiple HTML tables, and thus styling is applied *across* tables. Here's an example .Rmd: ```` ```{r setup, include=FALSE} knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE) library(gt) library(tidyverse) ``` ```{r} tab_1 <- exibble %>% dplyr::select( -c(fctr, date, time, datetime) ) %>% gt( rowname_col = "row", groupname_col = "group" ) %>% tab_header( title = md("Data listing from **exibble**"), subtitle = md("`exibble` is an R dataset") ) %>% fmt_number(columns = vars(num)) %>% fmt_currency(columns = vars(currency)) %>% tab_footnote( footnote = "Using commas for separators.", locations = cells_body( columns = vars(num), rows = num > 1000) ) %>% tab_footnote( footnote = "Using commas for separators.", locations = cells_body( columns = vars(currency), rows = currency > 1000) ) %>% tab_footnote( footnote = "Alphabetical fruit.", locations = cells_column_labels( columns = vars(char)) ) ``` Modify the table's background color to be "lightcyan". ```{r} tab_1 %>% tab_options( table.background.color = "lightcyan" ) ``` Modify the table width to `100%` (which spans the entire content width area). ```{r} tab_1 %>% tab_options( table.width = pct(100) ) ``` ```` We never see the table with a 'lightcyan' background, but if we reversed the order of the last two chunks then both tables would have that background color applied. What should be done is to insert a `::random` keyword as a result of the default `random_id()` function. In the `compile_scss()` function, if `::random` is seen as the option value for `table_id`, then generate the random id. If anything else (because the user can manually enter an `id` value), preserve that id value.

title: Improve NA handling for cols_merge_range
description:
```r
tbl <-
  dplyr::tribble(
    ~value_1, ~uncertainty, ~value_2, ~uncertainty_2,
    0.352,    0.10,         0.32,     NA_real_,
    0.983,    0.13,         NA_real_, NA_real_,
    0.639,    NA_real_,     0.21,     0.10,
    NA_real_, 0.17,         0.74,     0.15
  )

tbl %>%
  gt() %>%
  cols_merge_range(
    col_begin = vars(value_1),
    col_end = vars(value_2)
  )
```

The current behavior is that if the `col_begin` value is `NA`, the merged output is `NA`; if the `col_end` is `NA`, the unmerged `col_begin` value is used.

A better behavior would be to always replace missing values with NA (or let user specify).

title: indexing in cells_data()
description:
R uses row major indexing.

Named arguments for cells_data(columns = NULL, rows = NULL) are defined to occur in the reverse order one would expect. Maybe not a big problem if spelling out the argument names in a call to that function. But if you are shorthanding it and passing in bare arguments, you have to remember that the first arg is col and the second row, contrary to all other indexing in R. 

This makes writing and reading code with cells_data() much more error prone than it needs to be.

A simple solution is to reverse the order of arguments in the function definition, recognizing that this will break existing code where bare arguments are passed to cells_data().

title: Bug: Detecting a subtitle when none present - fails to knit to latex.
description:
**Problem Description**
When using ```as_latex``` and knitr in RStudio, gt LaTeX table fails giving the following error:

>! LaTeX Error: There's no line here to end.

**Reproducible Example**
```
library(gt)
library(tidyverse)

summary_single_table <- tribble(~study, ~N, ~Observation,
                                1,      25,     0.555, 
                                2,      55,     0.777,
                                3,     109,     0.355)



gt_tab <- summary_single_table %>% 
          gt(rowname_col = "study") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Table S1: Summary of Clinical Study Data by Study")


gt_tab %>% as_latex()
```


The LaTeX is failing because gt is registering a subtitle that is not actually present. If I do:

```
g <- gt:::build_data(gt_tab, context='latex')
gt:::dt_heading_has_subtitle(data = g)

>>> [1] TRUE

gt:::dt_heading_get(data = g)

>>>$title
[1] "Table S1: Summary of Clinical Study Data by Study"

$subtitle
character(0)
```

The ```dt_heading_has_subtitle``` function is:

```
dt_heading_has_subtitle <- function(data) {

  heading <- dt_heading_get(data = data)

  length(heading) > 0 && !is.null(heading$subtitle)
}
```

If I change this to:

```
dt_heading_has_subtitle <- function(data) {

  heading <- dt_heading_get(data = data)

  length(heading$subtitle) > 0 && !is.null(heading$subtitle)
}
```

It accurately returns ```FALSE```  instead of ```TRUE``` and knitr does not fail to render the LaTeX table. 


Note the ```dt_heading_has_title``` should also probably be changed from:

```
dt_heading_has_title <- function(data) {

  heading <- dt_heading_get(data = data)

  length(heading) > 0 && !is.null(heading$title)
}
```
To:
```
dt_heading_has_title <- function(data) {

  heading <- dt_heading_get(data = data)

  length(heading$title) > 0 && !is.null(heading$title)
}
```

title: Minimum version for scales package is incorrect
description:
I was unable to successfully run R CMD check (`devtools::check()`) due to a failure  of one unit test in the test-data_color.R file (line 36 "the correct color values are obtained when defining a palette"). 

The test fails because the call to `data_color` throws an error which is due to call to `scales::col_factor` having an unused argument (alpha = TRUE). The alpha argument was [added on Aug 18 2018](https://github.com/r-lib/scales/commit/7cd81215ba1f0da3e03418871ffccef7dbc7b523), just after the release of v1.0.0.

Currently the DESCRIPTION file list scales >=1.0.0 as an import. When I updated my local setup to have version 1.1.0 of scales package I no longer have these errors. My proposed fix would be to update the DESCRIPTION file to scales >= 1.1.0. 

``` r
library(dplyr)
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'dplyr'
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':
#> 
#>     filter, lag
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
#> 
#>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union

test_tbl <- tibble::tibble(x = 1:12)
# Obtain a palette of 12 colors in #RRGGBB format
pal_12 <-
  paletteer::paletteer_d(palette = "rcartocolor::Vivid") %>% as.character() %>%
  gsub("FF$", "", .)

color_fn <- scales::col_factor(pal_12, domain = test_tbl$x)
color_fn <- scales::col_factor(pal_12, domain = test_tbl$x, alpha = TRUE)
#> Error in scales::col_factor(pal_12, domain = test_tbl$x, alpha = TRUE): unused argument (alpha = TRUE)
```

title: Have each function that operates on a gt table verify that the input is a gt table
description:
It's very easy to do this:

```r
exibble %>% 
  tab_header(title = "A title")
```

or this:

```r
gtcars %>%
  dplyr::select(
    -mfr, -trim, bdy_style, drivetrain,
    -drivetrain, -trsmn, -ctry_origin
  ) %>%
  dplyr::slice(1:8) %>%
  tab_spanner(
    label = "performance",
    columns = vars(
      hp, hp_rpm, trq, trq_rpm,
      mpg_c, mpg_h)
  )
```

The thing that's missing, and is easy to forget, is the `gt()` call. When it's missing you either get a strange looking table returned, or `Error: No tidyselect variables were registered`, or, worse!

Anyway, I think a good idea is to validate that the incoming data object is indeed a `gt_tbl` and provide a suitable message (with advice) for when we inevitably forget.

title: Adding a footnote to a cell stub sometimes results in error (different from issue #437)
description:
I'm trying to add a footnote to a cell stub in a table built with ```gt``` by ```modelsummary```, but when the package tries to render the table, I get an error.

Here is a simple, reproducible example:
```r
library(MASS)
library(modelsummary)
library(gt)

url <- 'https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/Rdatasets/csv/HistData/Guerry.csv'
dat <- read.csv(url)

model <- lm(Literacy ~ Crime_prop + Infants, dat)

gt <- msummary(model) %>% 
  tab_footnote(                                                                                                                                                                               
    footnote = "This is a footnote.",                                                                                           
    locations = cells_stub(rows = vars(Infants))
  )

gt
```

The error I get when I try to run this script is: ```Can't find column NA in `.data`.```

When I run ```rlang::last_error()```, here is what I get:
```
Can't find column NA in `.data`.
Backtrace:
  1. base::source(...)
  3. gt:::print.gt_tbl(yy$value)
  4. gt:::as.tags.gt_tbl(x, ...)
  5. gt:::render_as_html(data = x)
  6. gt:::build_data(., context = "html")
 14. gt:::apply_footnotes_to_output(data = data, context = context)
 15. tibble:::`[.tbl_df`(body, footnotes_data_marks$rownum[i], footnotes_data_marks$colname[i])
 17. tibble:::check_names_df(j, x)
 18. tibble:::check_names_before_after_character(j, names(unclass(x)))
 19. base::source(...)
```

So the error seems to be occurring in ```apply_footnotes_to_output```, but of course the source of the error may be elsewhere, perhaps in ```build_data```.

Note that, when I try with other types of footnotes, it works fine:
```
library(MASS)
library(modelsummary)
library(gt)

url <- 'https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/Rdatasets/csv/HistData/Guerry.csv'

    locations = cells_data(columns = vars(`Model 1`), rows = vars(Infants))

gt
```

This issue may be related to #437, but it's distinct, since in the case I'm talking about it's not just that the glyph doesn't appear in the cell stub, but trying to render the table results in an outright error. I was able to reproduce #437 and there was no error:

description:
I've illustrated the unusual behavior with three datasets. The `exibble` dataset works as expected but not `mtcars` and `countrypops`.

I called the `columns` arg in `cells_column_labels` three different ways (vars, names, index) and all show the consistent incorrect behaviour - the column label to the right of the intended column label is targeted instead.

```
  library(gt)
  library(tibble)
  
  # exibble: highlight "char"
  exibble %>% 
    head(5) %>% 
    gt(rowname_col = "row") %>% 
    tab_style(
      list(cell_fill(), cell_text(weight = "bold")),
      cells_column_labels(2)
      )
  
  # mtcars: highlight "cyl"
  ## vars
  mtcars %>% 
    head(5) %>% 
    as_tibble(rownames = "model") %>% 
    gt(rowname_col = "model") %>% 
    tab_style(
      list(cell_fill(), cell_text(weight = "bold")),
      cells_column_labels(vars(cyl))
      )
  
  ## names
  mtcars %>% 
    head(5) %>% 
    as_tibble(rownames = "model") %>% 
    gt(rowname_col = "model") %>% 
    tab_style(
      list(cell_fill(), cell_text(weight = "bold")),
      cells_column_labels(c("cyl"))
      )
  
  ## index
  mtcars %>% 
    head(5) %>% 
    as_tibble(rownames = "model") %>% 
    gt(rowname_col = "model") %>% 
    tab_style(
      list(cell_fill(), cell_text(weight = "bold")),
      cells_column_labels(2)
      )
  
  # countrypop: highlight `country_code_3`
  ## var
  gt::countrypops %>% 
    head(5) %>% 
    gt(rowname_col = "country_name") %>% 
    tab_style(
      list(cell_fill(), cell_text(weight = "bold")),
      cells_column_labels(vars(country_code_3))
    )
  
  ## names
  gt::countrypops %>% 
    head(5) %>% 
    gt(rowname_col = "country_name") %>% 
    tab_style(
      list(cell_fill(), cell_text(weight = "bold")),
      cells_column_labels("country_code_3")
    )
  
  ## index
  gt::countrypops %>% 
    head(5) %>% 
    gt(rowname_col = "country_name") %>% 
    tab_style(
      list(cell_fill(), cell_text(weight = "bold")),
      cells_column_labels(2)
    )
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/42796157/70766829-038d9180-1d9a-11ea-9d62-05d3a0de3f75.png)


There is no issue when `rowname_col` arg in `gt` is not supplied.
```r
gt::countrypops %>% 
  head(5) %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  tab_style(
    list(cell_fill(), cell_text(weight = "bold")),
    cells_column_labels("country_code_3")
    )
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/42796157/70766413-a0e7c600-1d98-11ea-8220-ec1b5888a21e.png)

# Create a display table
cell_styles_tbl <-
  gt(tbl) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(size = px(50)),

title: IE11 - Column labels and Spanner column labels are always shown in bold text
description: On IE11, the column labels and spanner column labels are always shown in bold text (when not expected). Steps: 1. Run the following examples in RStudio IDE and open the gt table on IE11 2. Notice that the column labels are always shown bold Example 1 ``` library(tidyverse) library(gt) library(stringi) long_text <- stringi::stri_rand_lipsum(3) %>% stringr::str_c(., collapse = "\n") tbl <- dplyr::tibble( index = c("I want this", "at the top", "of each cell"), text = long_text, ) tbl %>% gt() %>% tab_style( style = cell_text(v_align = "top"), locations = cells_data() ) ``` Example 2 ``` library(gt) library(tidyverse) tibble( letter = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 3), id = rep(1:3, 2), x = runif(6), y = runif(6) ) %>% gather(var, value, x:y) %>% unite(column, letter, var) %>% spread(column, value) %>% gt(rowname_col = "id") %>% tab_spanner_delim(delim = "_", columns = everything()) %>% tab_footnote( footnote = "Source: the definitive guide to the alphabet", locations = cells_column_labels(columns = everything()) ) %>% tab_footnote( footnote = md("This is **A** and **B**. Nothing more, nothing less."), locations = cells_column_spanners(spanners = everything()) ) %>% tab_header("A gt Table") ``` Example 3: ``` library(tidyverse) library(gt) library(dplyr) countrypops %>% dplyr::filter(country_name == "Mongolia") %>% dplyr::select(-contains("code")) %>% tail(10) %>% gt() %>% tab_options(row.striping.include_table_body = FALSE) %>% data_color( columns = vars(population), colors = c("red", "orange", "green", "blue"), alpha = 0.5 ) ```

title: `tab_style` with `cells_column_labels` not working in the presence of a `tab_spanner`
description:
I want to produce a table with all column labels set in **bold**. The code below does it:

``` r
library(gt)
library(magrittr)

df <- data.frame(
  fn = c('a', 'b'),
  ln = c('c', 'd'),
  value = c(1, 2)
)

df %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  cols_label(fn = 'First', ln = 'Last') %>% 
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = 'bold'),
    locations = cells_column_labels(columns = 1:3)
  )
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1002949/69984941-06c28b00-1519-11ea-9684-59974c72e6e5.png)


But the formatting does not work for labels of columns that are under a spanner, as in the code below:

``` r
library(gt)
library(magrittr)

df <- data.frame(
  fn = c('a', 'b'),
  ln = c('c', 'd'),
  value = c(1, 2)
)

df %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  cols_label(fn = 'First', ln = 'Last') %>% 
  tab_spanner('Name', vars(fn, ln)) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = 'bold'),
    locations = cells_column_labels(columns = 1:3)
  )
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1002949/69984971-19d55b00-1519-11ea-9090-8b5082db67ce.png)

HOWEVER, this only happens when I set the column names via `cols_label`. If the table uses the original column names from the dataframe, the formatting is correctly applied:

``` r
library(gt)
library(magrittr)

df <- data.frame(
  fn = c('a', 'b'),
  ln = c('c', 'd'),
  value = c(1, 2)
)

df %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  # cols_label(fn = 'First', ln = 'Last') %>% 
  tab_spanner('Name', vars(fn, ln)) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = 'bold'),
    locations = cells_column_labels(columns = 1:3)
  )
```

title: Feature:  Automatic scrolling of cell content
description:
First off, kudos are in order. This is a fantastic R package and, for us, the most significant one since dplyr and ggplot before that. Thanks so much for the beautiful documentation, clear examples, and excellent features. We are planning on integrating gt more and more into our analytical pipelines so keep being awesome!

Anyway onto the ask. I know you’re getting a lot of feature requests but at least put this one under consideration. We want to make mostly non-interactive HTML tables, which are supported really well in gt. However it would be great to have an option for automatic horizontal scrolling of longer text inside of specific table cells. This way, we can have columns that are of fixed-width but occasionally longer strings will still be readable without an ellipsis or user interaction. 

Thanks again! You really hit it out of the park with this package.

```
unlined_tbl <-

title: Make it easy to insert a Fontawesome icon into a new text element of a table
description: Perhaps this can already be done with the fontawesome package, not sure, but having an easy way to get an icon into a title or footnote or some other location is something that would be very valuable.

title: Support columns of values that use units (from the units R package)
description:
The units R package (<https://github.com/r-quantities/units>) supports vectors that have units attached. When in a table, and introduced to gt, these values have their units well-defined (separately as numerator and denominator) and they can be `mixed_units` (where each element should be checked for their units).

It would be really cool if gt could take advantage of these attached units and display them with nice typography. I guess the package could automatically format a column with units or there could be a specialized formatter function that would have to be used to force the formatting to occur. Either way, this would be really great.

title: [FR] a way to not escape the row group label
description:
After PR #252, the row group label will be escaped. However, the user (like me) may need some styled or complicated row group label. I was able to do this by using the raw HTML text as the group column value. Now, it displays raw HTML text and the "escaping behavior" seems unavoidable.

I think being able to use raw HTML text as the row group label is a nice-to-have feature. So I'm here to ask for a feature request.

Thanks.

title: Error with `fmt_number()` when applied to a column that is entirely `NA`
description:
We get an error when formatting a column that is entirely `NA_real_` with `fmt_number()`. Here is the reproducible example:

```r
library(gt)
library(tidyverse)

tbl <- 
  dplyr::tibble(
    groups = c(rep("one", 5), rep("two", 5)),
    rows = 1:10 %>% as.character(),
    a = NA_real_
  )

tbl %>%
  gt() %>%
  fmt_number(columns = vars(a))
```

```
 Error: The length of the `x_side` vector must be 1 or the length of `x`. 
```

Originally reported in https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/353.

title: Error with `matches()` tidy select helper in `fmt_number()`
description:
When using `rows = gt::matches(<string>)` in `gt::fmt_number()`, there is the following error:

```
Error: The length of the `x_side` vector must be 1 or the length of `x`
```

When using the tbl:

```r
tbl <- 
  dplyr::tibble(
    groups = c(rep("one", 5), rep("two", 5)),
    rows = 1:10 %>% as.character(),
    a = 1:10,
    b = 11:20,
    c = 21:30
  )
```

This will work:

```r
tbl %>%
  gt() %>%
  fmt_number(
    columns = vars(a, b, c),
    rows = 1
  )
```

and this won't work:

```r
tbl %>%
  gt() %>%
  fmt_number(
    columns = vars(a, b, c),
    rows = gt::one_of("1")
    )
```

Originally reported in https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/353.

title: Allow selection of a font for the table (and maybe specific parts)
description: Right now, there is no choice in the font selection. It would be awesome if we could choose a webfont for the HTML table or at least monospace fonts in certain columns (for numbers).

title: Add a format function to make a duration value
description: This could be in terms of numbers of days. The number 0.5 could make 12h but you could optionally add other time parts (e.g., 12h 0m 0s).

title: Add a format function to generate fractions from numbers
description:
This is one of the best packages in R. Thanks so much for making it!

My idea is to make fractions from numbers. Where if you had 0.5, it becomes 1/2, 2.33 becomes 2 33/100 (or 2 1/3, depending on the accuracy which could be 1, 2, 3 digits in the denominator). You could also specify that the denominator must be of a certain type (1/3s, 1/2s, 1/4s, 1/8s).

title: Feature Request: Support for Lists of Tables
description:
This is somewhat related to #399.

Often I will want to generate a near-identical table for equivalent data sets.  As an example from my work, I may want to summarize clinical laboratory measurements where I would want the exact same table structure for cholesterol and then again for red blood cell count.

While it is perfectly feasible to loop (or `lapply`) over a list of tables, there are operations that can occur with having a generalized list class that could not easily happen with a list.  An example of something that would be more straight-forward with a list class, ensuring that column widths were identical between tables and automatic optimization of those widths would be hard with separate objects and simpler with a list class.

I understand that this is nor likely to be a short-term goal of the package, but as design decisions are made around information handling, it would be nice if this were considered.

title: Feature Request: Allow Nested Row Groups
description:
Groups of rows in data often are nested, and it would be helpful to have row groups support multi-level nesting.  As an example from my work, I generate tables to describe adverse events (side effects) in clinical trials of new medicines.  Those tables are grouped by organ system (like neurological) then another level of nesting is the group of symptoms (like brain and peripheral nerves) then the actual event (like headache, hallucinations, tremors, or pain in extremities).  In practice, there is more complexity than this (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MedDRA).

It would help if the tables could have this multi-level representation like:

```
|              Title             |
| Stub         | Col1   | Col2   |
| Group level 1                  |
|    Group level 2               |
|       Row 1  | R1C1   | R2C2   |
```

title: FYI/Feature Request: LaTeX topiclongtable Package Aligns with gt
description:
This is vaguely related to #387.

This is a combination of FYI and feature request.  The LaTeX topiclongtable package (https://ctan.org/pkg/topiclongtable?lang=en) has some overlapping functionality with the goals of `gt`.  Specifically, it allows for something very similar to row group labels to be generated and it will repeat them when a table crosses multiple pages automatically at the LaTeX compilation stage.

There are examples of the types of tables that can be generated within the CTAN documentation.

title: Error in values[index] (only 0's may be mixed with negative subscripts) when one variable in df contains only zeroes
description:
First of all, let me say congrats for this awseome package gt you are building! :-)

Issue detected: If you have a dataframe more than one variable, and one of them contains only empty values, you end up hitting this error: 

`Error in values[index] : only 0's may be mixed with negative subscripts` 
(using R 3.6.x under GNU/Linux 64 bits, in case it matters)

Reproducible example:

```r
  data.frame(x=rnorm(10), y=rep(0,10)) %>% 
  gt() %>%
  fmt_number(
    columns = vars(x,
                   y),
    decimals = 2,
    suffixing = TRUE
  )
```

FYI, If you attempt to make the similar reprex but only with one  column (y in the previous example), then no error is triggered and the expected result is produced.

```r
  data.frame(y=rep(0,10)) %>% 
  gt() %>%
  fmt_number(
    columns = vars(y),
    decimals = 2,
    suffixing = TRUE
  )
```

title: Error knitting to PDF when table has (Intercept) in a row
description:
Really liking the look of gt so far and exploring it for an analysis. I'm attempting to knit regression tables generated by gt in an R Markdown document to PDF. I came across a (I think) bug where if the summary table has a variable called "(Intercept)", I get a knitting error. Removing the "(Intercept)" row allows the document to knit to PDF, and removing the ('s also allows the document to knit to PDF (i.e. replacing "(Intercept)" with "Intercept"). Not sure how to submit a reprex here since the error comes while knitting, but content of the .Rmd below. All three examples below work when knitting to HTML. 

Working on gt version 0.1.0,  tinytex 0.16

 ## `.Rmd` file

```

---
title: "test"
author: "Dan"
date: "11/7/2019"
output:
  pdf_document: default
  html_document: default
  bookdown::pdf_document2: default
---

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(broom)
library(gt)

```

Attempting to knit this chunk to PDF causes error "! Undefined control sequence."
 
```{r, eval = TRUE}

mod <- lm(mpg ~ cyl, data = mtcars)

broom::tidy(mod) %>% 
  gt()
```


Works if I filter out the row with "(Intercept)" in it. 
 

```{r, eval = TRUE}

mod <- lm(mpg ~ cyl, data = mtcars)

broom::tidy(mod) %>% 
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>% 
  gt()
```

```{r, eval = TRUE}

mod <- lm(mpg ~ cyl, data = mtcars)

broom::tidy(mod) %>% 
  mutate(term = ifelse(term == "(Intercept)","Intercept",term)) %>% 
  gt()
```
```

title: Use 'longtabu' instead of 'longtable' for exporting to latex to avoid table overflowing page width
description:
**Description of Issue:**

I was using gt to make a table and export to latex and while doing so, the table width kept running off the page whenever I would knit it to pdf in markdown using RStudio. (Image and reproducible code below).

**Code to Reproduce**

```r
library(gt)
library(tidyverse)


summary_single_table <- tribble(
 ~ Study, ~n_indiv_mich, ~ n_elig_mich, ~n_unreg_mich,  ~fract_voted_mich, ~n_indiv_fl, ~ n_elig_fl, ~n_unreg_fl, ~ fract_voted_fl, ~n_indiv_nh, ~n_elig_nh, ~ n_unreg_nh, ~ fract_voted_nh,
   1,     150       ,    950  ,       508,              0.535,            16      ,    101 ,       53 ,        0.525,         166,          1051,           561,       0.534,         
   2,       6       ,     28  ,       17,               0.607,            NA      ,     NA ,       NA ,           NA,           6,            28,            17,       0.607,
   3,      NA       ,     NA  ,       NA,                  NA,            20      ,    123 ,       40 ,        0.325,          20,           123,            40,       0.325
)


find.sum <- function(., df){
  c <- names(df)[which(df== ., arr.ind=T)[, "col"]]
  c <- names(sort(table(c),decreasing=TRUE))[[1]]
  if(!startsWith(c, 'n_')){
    FALSE
  } else {
    TRUE
  }
}

#gt summary rows not appearing on export to latex, creating a summary row and binding to table
summary.row.total <- function(df){
  df <- df %>% bind_rows(summarise_all(., list(function(.){if(find.sum(., df)) sum(., na.rm=TRUE) else NA})))
  df[dim(df)[1], 1] <- 'Total'
  df
}

gt_tab <- summary_single_table %>% summary.row.total()


#function that will be used to rename columns later
rename_col <- function(df){
  col_nm <- names(df)[2:length(names(df))]
  v <- as.list(rep(c('N Individuals', 'N Eligible', 'N Unregistered', 'Fraction Voted'), 3))
  names(v) <- col_nm
  v
}

gt_tab  %>%
  
  #set the column named 'Study' to the rownames.
  gt(rowname_col = "Study") %>%
  
  #Switch all NA's in every column to show as lines in output table
  fmt_missing(everything(), rows = NULL, missing_text = "---") %>%
  
  #Create multindex:
  tab_spanner(
    label = "Michigan",
    columns = ends_with("mich")
  ) %>%
  

  tab_spanner(
    label = "Florida",
    columns = ends_with("fl")
  ) %>%
  
    tab_spanner(
    label = "New Hampshire",
    columns = ends_with("nh")
  ) %>%
  tab_stubhead(label = "Study") %>%
  cols_label(.list=rename_col(gt_tab)) %>%

  #add table title
  tab_header(title = "Table S1: Summary of Swing State Voting Registry Study Data by Study") %>%
  
  #add table caption
   tab_source_note(
    source_note = "Studies 1, 2, and 3 were all included in model estimation. See section 3 for further study details. 'N Individuals' represents the total number of surveyed individuals in each study, 'N Eligible' represents the total number of eligible voters in each study including those that were not registered at time of study ('N Unregistered' represents the number of unregistered voters in each study, and 'Fraction Voted' indcates the fraction of eligible voters that voted in the previous presidential election in each study.')"
  ) %>% 
  
  #add bold text style at table stubhead location (the 'Study' label)
  tab_style(
    style = list(
      cell_text(weight="bold")
    ), 
    locations = cells_stubhead()
    ) %>% 
  
  #in the cell_stub (rows), find the row that is 'Total', add style to it. 
  tab_style(
    style = list(
      cell_text(weight="bold")
      ),
    locations = cells_stub(rows =c('Total'))
  ) %>%
 as_latex()
```

**Output of code snippet**

[overflow_table.pdf](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/files/3815502/overflow_table.pdf)


**Possible Solution**

 I did find a solution, but it required me to modify some of the source code for gt. Gt right now uses the `longtable` latex dependency, which doesn't give a lot of options for auto-fitting tables to the page width. Swapping to using `tabu`, which has a `longtabu` environment that is based on `longtable` but has features of the `tabu` environment (like the auto-fit), ended up being the perfect solution - table could stretch out several pages length wise, but the width was not spilling off the page. 

**Solution output (produced by same above code)**

[fixed_overflow.pdf](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/files/3815526/fixed_overflow.pdf)

 I forked this repo and pushed my changes to there. For right now, my changes force auto-fitting to page by setting the columns as a special `tabu` type "X", which manually calculates each column width so that the full table fits to the width of the page. This could be easily adjusted to a customizable setting in the future (similar to `KableExtra` `kable_styling(latex_options="scale_down")`. 

I created a pull request so the author's could review and determine if they wanted this functionality in the actual package. Also, great work with gt so far by the way- love it!

title: Add vertical alignment inside rows for tab_style()
description:
Hi team, An older version of `gt` allowed for passing raw CSS style rules as strings which allowed for vertical alignment within rows of a table. I spoke with Rich about this and he suggested posting it as an Issue. Problem: The current version of `gt` disallows the use of CSS rules as strings in `tab_style()` and only accept a subset of options (really, the argument list). This is totally fine as I think there are long-term goals of accomplishing additional styling, but a vertical alignment option in addition to horizontal alignment. Specifically this is useful for tables with large chunks of text, where the less verbose columns end up way down the page. See below for a reprex and a representation of the table. see [Community](https://community.rstudio.com/t/vertical-alignment-of-gt-cell-contents/23174) for a past thread and attempted work-around that has since been removed. --- ``` r library(tidyverse) library(gt) library(stringi) long_text <- stri_rand_lipsum(3) %>% str_c(., collapse = "\n") df <- data.frame( index = c("I want this", "at the top", "of each cell"), text = long_text ) df %>% gt() ```

description:
The `fmt_markdown()`, `html()`, and `md()`  functions should be able to convert LaTeX math formulas to inline SVGs. This will allow math formulas in table cells and in any other label areas (e.g., column labels, header title, etc.). 

The rendered formula SVGs should entirely consist of paths.

title: groups argument in `cells_column_labels` ignores a vector of spanner titles
description:
Loving this package! I have a table, however, with multiple tab spanner labels. I would like to format them all within a single call to `tab_spanner`, e.g.:

```
library(gt)
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))
my_gt <- mtcars %>% 
  select(mpg, cyl, gear, vs) %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  tab_spanner(
    label = "Car Stuff 1",
    columns = vars(mpg, cyl)
  ) %>% 
  tab_spanner(
    label = "Car Stuff 2",
    columns = vars(gear, vs)
  ) %>% 
  tab_style(
    style = cells_styles(text_color = "Red",
                         text_font = "Times"),
    locations = cells_column_labels(groups = c("Car Stuff 1", "Car Stuff 2"))
  )
```
Unfortunately when the `groups` argument is greater than length 1, `gt` ignores all styling. Thus, I have to style each tab spanner individually:

```
my_gt %>% 
  tab_style(
    style = cells_styles(text_color = "Red",
                         text_font = "Times"),
    locations = cells_column_labels(groups = "Car Stuff 1")
  ) %>% 
  tab_style(
    style = cells_styles(text_color = "Red",
                         text_font = "Times"),
    locations = cells_column_labels(groups = "Car Stuff 2")
  )
```
Is it possible to do all the formatting in one `tab_style` call?

summary_df_display_list[[i]] %>%

title: Feature request: Support packed data frame (data frame with data frame columns)
description:
Upcoming tidyr has `pack` and `unpack` to  treat data frame columns.
Supporting *packed* data can reduce calling `tab_spanner` and will improve experience in `gt`.
Here's my prototype implementation.

``` r
library(dplyr, warn.conflict = FALSE)
library(tidyr)
library(gt)

x <- data.frame(
  w = c("a", "b", "b"), x = c("A", "B", "B"),
  y1 = 1:3, y2 = 1:3, z1 = 1:3, z2 = 1:3
) %>%
  pack(y = starts_with("y"), z = starts_with("z")) %>%
  group_by(w)

f <- function(x) {
  df_col <- names(x)[vapply(x, is.data.frame, TRUE)]
  
  .gt <- gt(unpack(x, !!df_col))
  
  for(i in df_col) {
    .gt <- tab_spanner(.gt, label = i, names(x[[i]]))
  }
  
  .gt
}
f(x)
```

Whereas this
```
gt::gtcars %>%
  dplyr::select(mfr, model, year, hp) %>%
  dplyr::top_n(n = 10) %>%
  gt::gt() %>%
  gt::cols_label(hp = 'Horsepower') %>%
  gt::tab_style(
    style = gt::cells_styles(text_size = '30px'),
    locations = gt::cells_column_labels(columns = TRUE)
  )
```
yields this
![Rplot2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/46826199/60226068-7469dd00-983e-11e9-9105-0d36c0b86d4f.png)
Ordering of the functions and other ways of trying to select the column header for styling don't seem to make a difference, so this
```
gt::gtcars %>%
  dplyr::select(mfr, model, year, hp) %>%
  dplyr::top_n(n = 10) %>%
  gt::gt() %>%
  gt::tab_style(
    style = gt::cells_styles(text_size = '30px'),
    locations = gt::cells_column_labels(columns = gt::vars(hp))
  )
```
yields this
![Rplot3](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/46826199/60226159-d4608380-983e-11e9-8a30-72d9bd6be8e0.png)
But this
```
gt::gtcars %>%
  dplyr::select(mfr, model, year, hp) %>%
  dplyr::top_n(n = 10) %>%
  gt::gt() %>%
  gt::tab_style(
    style = gt::cells_styles(text_size = '30px'),

I know you can include markup in the cols_label function, so I'm possibly just using these functions incorrectly... but I ended up just working around this by relabeling my columns with dplyr before funneling them to gt() so that I wouldn't have to do manual formatting of the column headers in markdown or html.

title: Refactor add_location_row callers
description:
Right now, there are a proliferation of methods around 1) types of metadata to store, and 2) types of locations to be targeted. If there are `m` types of metadata and `n` types of locations, I think we are talking about `m*n` methods.

- add_location_row
    - add_location_row_styles
        - set_style.cells_stub
        - set_style.cells_data
        - ...
    - add_location_row_footnote
        - set_footnote.cells_stub
        - set_footnote.cells_data
        - ...
    - ...

If the individual `set_style`, `set_footnote` methods are doing nothing distinct from each other besides unpacking locations into locname/locnum/groupname/etc., these can be pushed down into the `add_location_row`. In other words, `add_location_row` could become a generic that takes location objects.

With that change, there would only need to be a single `set_style`, a single `set_footnote`, etc. that call `add_location_row`; and there would be `m` method impls of `add_location_row`.

Incidentally I'd also remove `row` from the function name `add_location_row` only because it exposes the underlying table implementation.

Note that this proposal doesn't affect anything on the retrieving/reading/resolving side of things (i.e. `build_data`, render pipeline), this is just about cleaning up the insertion side.

--@jcheng5

title: drake and gt: gt modifies global environment
description:
Briefly: Using gt within an Rmd built by [drake](https://github.com/ropensci/drake) with `rmarkdown::render()` results in the error

```
target report
fail report
Error: Target `report` failed. Call `diagnose(report)` for details. Error message:
  cannot remove bindings from a locked environment. 
Please read the "Self-invalidation" section of the make() help file.
```

I tracked the error to gt registering the S3 methods for `"knitr", "knit_print", "gt_tbl"` on package load in [zzz.R](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/456b23242e55b11e1e6d3ab50d07f9d0e2fb6db3/R/zzz.R#L104).

I'm not sure whether this should be addressed in gt or drake (cc @wlandau), but I opened here in case there's an easy fix in gt.

### Reprex

Here's a minimal drake plan that would be saved in **drake.R**:

```r
library(drake)
library(gt)

plan <- drake_plan(
  data = mtcars,
  report = rmarkdown::render(
    knitr_in("report.Rmd"),
    output_file = file_out("report.html")
  )
)

make(plan)
```

And in **report.Rmd**:

````r
---
title: "Example GT Report"
output: html_document
---

```{r}
library(drake)
library(gt)
loadd(data)
gt(data)
```
````

In a fresh session, run

```r
source("make.R")
## target report
## ...
## fail report
## Error: Target `report` failed. Call `diagnose(report)` for details. Error message:
##   cannot remove bindings from a locked environment. 
## Please read the "Self-invalidation" section of the make() help file.
```

### User-level Fixes

A user can add `lock_envir = FALSE` to `drake::make()`, but [this is not recommended](https://github.com/ropensci/drake/issues/664#issuecomment-453160930).

A user can also use a custom environment for the drake build, for example by modifying the `make()` step of **drake.R**

```r
drake_env <- new.env()
make(plan, envir = drake_env)
```

but for larger drake projects this is less desirable because the user need to source all scripts tracked by drake into `drake_env`.

I also noticed that the problem _does not_ occur when using `knitr::knit()`, so there may be an interaction here with `rmarkdown::render()`. The downside of this approach is that `rmarkdown::render()` is required for Rmd v2 documents.

Finally, I confirmed that commenting out the `register_s3_method()` [line](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/456b23242e55b11e1e6d3ab50d07f9d0e2fb6db3/R/zzz.R#L104) does also "resolve" the problem, but I'm not sure what downstream consequences that might cause.

title: cols_split_delim works only with ordered columns?
description:
`cols_split_delim()` seems to work only if the colums are sorted on toplevel. Is this intended behaviour or a bug?

```r
library(gt)
library(dplyr)
iris %>%
  filter(Species == 'setosa') %>%
  select(-Species) %>%
  dplyr::slice(1:2) %>%
  gt() %>%
  cols_split_delim(delim = ".")
```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/849616/58097244-37735080-7bd7-11e9-9f55-421234fdcf61.png)

```r
iris %>%
  filter(Species == 'setosa') %>%
  select(-Species) %>%
  dplyr::slice(1:2) %>%
  select(1, 3, 2, 4) %>%
  gt() %>%
  cols_split_delim(delim = ".")
```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/849616/58097293-5540b580-7bd7-11e9-944b-74b1401d0ccf.png)

Fix is easy, just sort by the string before the split:

```r
iris %>%
  filter(Species == 'setosa') %>%
  select(-Species) %>%
  dplyr::slice(1:2) %>%
  select(1, 3, 2, 4) %>%
  select(order(gsub('^(.*)\\..*$', '\\1', names(.)))) %>%
  gt() %>%
  cols_split_delim(delim = ".")
```

Feature Request: cols_merge handling of missing values
description:
Hi Rich, Thank you for your amazing work on this package!

I am using the `cols_merge()` function, and I wanted to put out a proposal for an enhancement regarding missing value handling.  When merging two columns if one of the two columns is missing, I may want to see the merged column with the missing value in the output (like `glue()` where `glue("{5}, {NA}")`, resolves to `5, NA`).

Here's an example:

This is what the default output looks like
```
library(tidyverse)
library(glue)
library(gt)

title: Scaled values in `fmt_scientific()` can result in `x 10^0`-type output
description: The `fmt_scientific()` formatter is designed to internally label numeric values that would lead to power-of-zero figures (e.g., 1.53 x 10^0 should just be 1.53). This results in the exclusion of those labeled numbers in getting a `x 10^y` part (which would end up being `x 10^0`). However, the current method can result in incorrect formatting when values are scaled with `scale_by != 1`. Some scaled numbers incorrectly get formatted with a `x 10^0` and others don't get a required `x 10^y` part. Here is an example: ```r dplyr::tibble( unscaled_num = c(0.1, 0.5, 1.5, 7.5, 10.5), unscaled_sci = c(0.1, 0.5, 1.5, 7.5, 10.5), scaled_num = c(0.1, 0.5, 1.5, 7.5, 10.5), scaled_sci = c(0.1, 0.5, 1.5, 7.5, 10.5) ) %>% gt() %>% fmt_number( columns = vars(unscaled_num) ) %>% fmt_scientific( columns = vars(unscaled_sci), ) %>% fmt_number( columns = vars(scaled_num), scale_by = 3 ) %>% fmt_scientific( columns = vars(scaled_sci), scale_by = 3 ) ``` where rows 2 and 4 are incorrectly formatted. The solution is to scale the incoming values first, and then perform the checks for excluding the `x 10^0` part.

title: Add option to remove column labels
description: There are some situations where you wouldn't want column labels in a table. This might be text heavy table where headings are implied or this could be a table for arranging content in an email message. Here is an example of how this might work in practice with a table made from Markdown elements. We could have the argument `hide_column_labels` in `tab_options()` and set it to `TRUE` when we don't want to display the column labels. ```r # Create a few Markdown-based # text snippets text_1a <- " ### This is Markdown. Markdown’s syntax is comprised entirely of punctuation characters, which punctuation characters have been carefully chosen so as to look like what they mean... assuming you’ve ever used email. " text_1b <- " Info on Markdown syntax can be found [here](https://daringfireball.net/projects/markdown/). " text_1c <- "" text_2a <- " The **gt** package has these datasets: - `countrypops` - `sza` - `gtcars` - `sp500` - `pizzaplace` - `exibble` " text_2b <- " There's a quick reference [here](https://commonmark.org/help/). " text_2c <- " Yes, gifs should work. " # Arrange the text snippets as a tibble # using the `dplyr::tribble()` function; # then, create a gt table and format # all columns with `fmt_markdown()` dplyr::tribble( ~Markdown, ~md, text_1a, text_2a, text_1b, text_2b, text_1c, text_2c, ) %>% gt() %>% fmt_markdown(columns = TRUE) %>% tab_options( table.width = px(500), hide_column_labels = TRUE ) ```

title: Add location helper function `cells_stubhead_caption()`
description:
There are a few locations that are still not yet accessible by `tab_footnote()` and `tab_style()`. One of them is the stubhead caption (which is an optional label for the optional stub). So, we need to have a `cells_stubhead_caption()` location.

It's currently not possible to style the text of the stubhead caption. Also, if we were to supply a `cells_all()` location helper (that can be used exclusively with `tab_style()` to, say, modify font styling or apply a background color), we need to have all locations accessible. The `cells_all()` function was suggested in #176.

title: Error with `data_color` when only one row in data
description:
Hi,
thanks for the wonderful package. I gave it a try for a small table I needed in a report recently, since I needed grouped columns.
The problem I found is the following: When I have a data.frame with **only one row** the basic table rendering works fine. But when I want to color a cell/column it breaks
Error message:
_Error: All column or row indices given must be present in `data`._

With two rows no problem.

Is this a bug or an issue of my code?

```r
library(gt)

mydf <- data.frame(KPI1 = 3.6123, KPI2 = 5.235, count = 12345, KPI1_2 = 3.457, KPI2_2 = 5.8132, count_2 = 12344)
mydf$diffKPI1 <- mydf$KPI1_2 - mydf$KPI1
mydf$diffKPI2 <- mydf$KPI2_2 - mydf$KPI2

# this works
mydf %>% gt() %>%
  fmt_number(columns = vars(KPI1, KPI2, KPI1_2, KPI2_2, diffKPI1, diffKPI2),
             decimals = 2) %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "solution 1", columns = vars(KPI1, KPI2, count)) %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "solution 2", columns = vars(KPI1_2, KPI2_2, count_2)) %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "Difference", columns = vars(diffKPI1, diffKPI2)) %>%
  tab_header(title = "Stats of my project") %>%
  cols_label(KPI1_2 = "KPI1",
             KPI2_2 = "KPI2",
             diffKPI1 = "Diff KPI1",
             diffKPI2 = "Diff KPI2",
             count_2 = "count")

# this not
mydf %>% gt() %>%
  fmt_number(columns = vars(KPI1, KPI2, KPI1_2, KPI2_2, diffKPI1, diffKPI2),
             decimals = 2) %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "solution 1", columns = vars(KPI1, KPI2, count)) %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "solution 2", columns = vars(KPI1_2, KPI2_2, count_2)) %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "Difference", columns = vars(diffKPI1, diffKPI2)) %>%
  tab_header(title = "Stats of my project") %>%
  cols_label(KPI1_2 = "KPI1",
             KPI2_2 = "KPI2",
             diffKPI1 = "Diff KPI1",
             diffKPI2 = "Diff KPI2",
             count_2 = "count") %>%
  data_color(columns = vars(diffKPI1), 
             colors = function(x){ifelse(x<0,"red","green")})


# with two rows it works
mydf <- rbind(mydf, mydf) # just duplicate the data

mydf %>% gt() %>%
  fmt_number(columns = vars(KPI1, KPI2, KPI1_2, KPI2_2, diffKPI1, diffKPI2),

title: Consider removing sass as a hard requirement *if at all possible*

I just installed the latest github version on R 3.5.2 Windows 7

Installing the `sass` package prerequisite took over 11 minutes, the rest of the installation proceeded in less than a minute.

If `sass` is absolutely integrated into the package and required then not much can be done, but if there's any way to make a few changes and to remove that dependency without degrading performance and code quality, it might be worth it to investigate.

title: Suggestion: use consistent argument names
description:
When looking at the function signature of `gt()`, I noticed that 3 of the arguments use underscore naming scheme, and one of the parameters is `stub_group.sep` which has both an underscore and a period. I sort of understand the reason, it looks like `group.sep` is a "property", but IMO this naming convention is awkward and will be very easy to get wrong.

Here's another example: I was scrolling through the `tab_options()` parameters, and it just doesn't look right IMO:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/952340/53856518-3f403300-3fa0-11e9-8b15-abb8b9cb3041.png)

title: Feature request (shiny): Allow basic interactivity with the table
description:
Related to #207 

A few basic interactivity controls would make this package a lot more useful for shiny apps. Off the top of my head, extremely common features that people generally want in a table:

- Ability to click on a column to sort by it
- Ability to search
- Ability to click on one/multiple rows and get a shiny callback specifying what rows are chosen

title: Suggestion: warn user before rendering N rows
description:
Just an idea. I just tried running `gt::gt(gt::pizzaplace)` in the rstudio console and I thought my RStudio got frozen. I tried it several times, and each time I had to abort the operation. Eventually I realized it just took a full minute to complete the render.

Perhaps it'd be friendly to the user to show a message confirming that the user indeed wants to print the entire table if gt notices that there are above N number of rows? Of course only do this in interactive mode. Or maybe even just showing a message would be enough.

title: Suggestion (shiny): rename or add alias from gt_output to GTOutput and render_gt to renderGT
description: In the shiny universe, all the inputs and outputs follow this naming convention. In the tidyverse things have shifted to use underscore, but in shiny even new features still use the shiny naming convention for consistency. I think it would make it easier for shiny developers to not have to switch contexts and use non-shiny naming conventions.

title: Feature request (shiny): Allow a dataframe to be easily rendered by gt_output without explicit conversion to gt object
description:
It would be very handy to have the following work:

```
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  gt::gt_output("table")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$table <- gt::render_gt(
    mtcars
  )
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

In this case I would expect the table to just be a plain boring gt object that simply gets created around `mtcars` with no parameters. This is opinion-based so if you disagree, feel free to close. It kind of goes against the philosophy of making the developer be super precise, and is more along the philosophy of trying to be useful in common expected cases.

title: Feature request (shiny): Allow pagination
description:
When creating a gt table in an html file (I'm thinking specifically shiny, but this could apply for rmarkdown or just any html output that can include javascript), it would be great to be able to add pagination. This way long tables are not just one massive table that you have to scroll down for.

With the ability to paginate, it'd be nice to be able to specify the page length.

A related feature would be to allow server-side pagination, so that if I have a table with 10000 rows, instead of sending all that data to the browser and making it slow, only eg. 25 rows get sent to the browser

title: Feature request (shiny): Allow setting width and height of gt table
description:
For shiny output objects, it's standard practice to allow setting the width and height, so that an object doesn't take up the entire page. It's just the polite thing to do :)

I usually like to be able to do something like `gt_output("table", width = "500px")`

title: Formatters do not check column types, leading to confusing outputs/messages
description:
Currently, the `fmt_*()` functions do not check the types of columns being operated on. This can variously lead to errors, incorrect outputs, or surprising outputs. Here are a few examples:

Formatting a character column as numeric leads to an error (as it should, but we should provide our own error message).

```r
exibble %>%
  gt() %>%
  fmt_number(columns = vars(char))
```

```
>> Error in round(x[non_na_x], decimals) : 
>>  non-numeric argument to mathematical function 
```

Formatting a numeric column as markdown results in no change (it should result in an error).

```r
exibble %>%
  gt() %>%
  fmt_markdown(columns = vars(num))
```

Formatting a time column as a date leads to all values being `Thursday, January 1, 1970`.

```r
exibble %>%
  gt() %>%
  fmt_date(columns = vars(time))
```

And there are several more.

We just need to validate `x` and stop when the class doesn't match what's required for each formatter function.

title: The `fmt_date()` function doesn't accept column data of class `Date`
description:
The `fmt_date()` function only works with character-based columns with an ISO formatted date or date-time (the time component is stripped away if detected). It should be possible to accept values of type `Date`. The example in the README gets around this limitation by mutating a date column (with `Date`s) to a `character` column:

```r
sp500 %>%
  dplyr::filter(date >= start_date & date <= end_date) %>%
  dplyr::select(-adj_close) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(date = as.character(date)) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "S&P 500",
    subtitle = glue::glue("{start_date} to {end_date}")
  ) %>%
  fmt_date(
    columns = vars(date),
    date_style = 3
  ) %>%
  fmt_currency(
    columns = vars(open, high, low, close),
    currency = "USD"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(
    columns = vars(volume),
    scale_by = 1 / 1E9,
    pattern = "{x}B"
  )
```

Basically, this should be made to work without that `mutate()` call.

title: Install
Repeating column labels for groups (a la "Freeze Panes" on Excel)
description:
---

Thanks so much for the development and support of this package. It's the best table package we have on R and it renders beautifully to web pages and reports.

I'm often using it for larger tables split into two groups (>10 observations for each group), so the _n_ and _p_ are pretty close (somewhere between 10 and 15 variables). 

Excel has a **freeze panes** option that allows you to scroll down a long table/grouped table and not lose track of which variable you're tracking. 

I'm not sure if there's functionality to mimic that in grouped tables at the moment (hopefully there is and I've just missed this!), but it seems worthwhile for longer tables if there's not.

Imagine if country pops had many variables about population, and we could repeat the tab spanners/column names above both United States and Russian Federation). Example included has a wishful function called **col_name_repeat**.

```r
library(gt)

country = countrypops %>% filter(country_name %in% c("United States", "Russian Federation"),  year >= 1985)

gt_tbl <-  gt(data = country ) %>%
    group_by(country_name) %>%
  tab_spanner(
    label = "Population statistics",
    columns = vars(population, 2:10)
  ) %>%
  tab_spanner(
    label = "Political system/info",

title: `fmt_scientific()` should have an option to set the number of power

`fmt_scientific()` should have an option to set the number of power so that the difference in magnitude is more obvious. Consider the following example:

title: Facilitate direct use of matrix
description:
I would to be able to use `gt` to format a grid of text, which is represented as a matrix:

1.  I need to place names randomly on a 10x10 grid and create a pretty printable PDF.
2. The most natural way to place the names is to create a 10x10 matrix of empty strings, then overwrite the empty strings in some locations with names. (I'm using a matrix rather than a tibble because I don't think of the columns as being meaningful---they're just locations.)

Code to date is included below; it assumes a CSV file with one name per line.

```
# Grid size.
SIZE <- 10
SIZE_2 <- SIZE * SIZE

# Command-line arguments.
args <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
filename <- args[[1]]
seed <- args[[2]]

# Read names.
names <- read_csv(filename)$Name

# Determine XY positions (0-based to make subsequent math easier).
set.seed(seed)
shuffle <- sample(0:(SIZE_2 - 1))

# Fill matrix (converting back to 1-based indices).
table <- matrix(rep("", SIZE_2), SIZE, SIZE)
for (i in 1:length(names)) {
    x <- (shuffle[i] %% SIZE) + 1
    y <- (shuffle[i] %/% SIZE) + 1
    table[x, y] <- names[i]
}
print(table)
```

title: The `cols_merge_range()` function requires a `locale` argument
description:
Across different locales, ranges are formatted differently. This is both in terms of space characters and the range-based character. Taking `{0}` and `{1}` as the two entities that constitute the range, here are the correct patterns by locale:

`{0} - {1}`: my, pt_PT, ro
`{0} – {1}`: bg, bs, hr, jv, sk
`{0}-{1}`: ca, da, es, eu, fil, fy, gu, it, ka, ml, nl, sq, th, tt, vi, yue, yue_Hans, zh, zh_Hant
`{0}‒{1}`: et, nn, sv
`{0}—{1}`: to
`{0}~{1}`: ko
`{0}～{1}`: ja
`{0}–{1}`: all others

A `locale` argument is required here. The default should be set to `NULL` which then utilizes the `{0}–{1}` pattern (which is different than the `{0} — {1}` pattern that is in use now).

title: `escape_latex` should be applied to stub
description:
`escape_latex` is not applied to the stub, which breaks latex compilation when the stub includes invalid characters. Below, the first example produces valid LaTeX, since `test_this` in cells is properly escaped. The second example does not compile because `test_this` is in the stub column and `escape_latex` function is not applied there.

``` r
library(gt)
library(magrittr)

# "test_this" is properly escaped
data.frame('first' = c('test_this', 'test'),
           'second' = 1:2) %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  as_latex %>% 
  cat()
#> \captionsetup[table]{labelformat=empty,skip=1pt}

#> \toprule
#> first & second \\ 
#> \midrule
#> test\_this & 1 \\ 
#> test & 2 \\ 
#> \bottomrule
#> \end{longtable}

data.frame('first' = c('test_this', 'test'),
           'second' = 1:2) %>% 
  gt(rowname_col = 'first') %>% 
  as_latex %>% 
  cat()
#> \captionsetup[table]{labelformat=empty,skip=1pt}

title: Disable random div id generation?
description:
Right now, [print.R generates a random name](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/0df27115d1453c5c100c98aaeb189c5a34d522a4/R/print.R#L47) for the wrapping div for gt tables (e.g. `<div id="joisdfjkdf">`). This is nice for uniqueness in HTML, but it causes issues with version control, since the table ID changes often (forcing new changes in git). 

Right now, my solution is to use `set.seed()` before any `gt()` stuff, and that's working, but it might be nice to have an argument to `gt()` or something that disables the random id generation and allows users to supply their own.

title: Suppress row group label and double horizontal rule
description:
It would be nice if users could suppress group labels when using the `tab_row_group` or the `group_by` strategies. Currently, we can use the `tab_row_group` function and leave the `group` argument empty, but this produces a double horizontal rule.

A workaround would be to allow users to insert horizontal rules where they want (is there such a function now?).



```r
library(gt)
library(dplyr)

dat <- data.frame('a' = 1:4,
                  'b' = c('groupA', 'groupA', 'groupB', 'groupB'))

# idiomatic grouping strategy prints group labels by default
dat %>%
  dplyr::group_by(b) %>%
  gt()
```

![screen shot 2019-01-21 at 13 56 31](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/987057/51493844-97bac880-1d84-11e9-849f-dcacb65be13e.png)

```r
# hack to suppress group labels. Unfortunately, this keeps a double horizontal rule.
dat %>%
  select(-b) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_row_group(group = "", rows = 1:2)
```

title: Specify width of LaTeX table
description:
The setting `tab_options(table.width = pct(100))` doesn't seem to be respected when rendering to LaTeX, see reprex below. Is this something you'd consider supporting?

The fairly new [`xltabular`](https://ctan.org/pkg/xltabular) package could be an option to render long tables with support for the `X` column modifier, which could perhaps be applied to all columns that are left-aligned.

Related: setting column width (#111).

``` r
library(gt)

default_latex <-
  data.frame(a = 1, b = 2) %>%
  gt() %>%
  as_latex()

full_width_latex <-
  data.frame(a = 1, b = 2) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_options(table.width = pct(100)) %>%
  as_latex()

identical(default_latex, full_width_latex)
#> [1] TRUE
```

title: Add option to gather columns when using `tab_spanner()`
description: Currently, `tab_spanner()` will not modify the positions of the table columns when non-contiguous columns are included in the call. This is acceptable when you want a repeating spanner column label across the top of the column labels. However, it may be convenient to have the option to automatically gather the columns that are part of a single spanner column label. Here's how you might move a column to join a group of columns with `cols_move()` and use `tab_spanner()`: ```r gtcars %>% dplyr::select( -mfr, -trim, bdy_style, drivetrain, -drivetrain, -trsmn, -ctry_origin ) %>% dplyr::slice(1:8) %>% gt(rowname_col = "model") %>% tab_header(title = "gtcars") %>% tab_spanner( label = "performance", columns = vars( hp, hp_rpm, trq, trq_rpm, mpg_c, mpg_h) ) %>% cols_move(vars(msrp), after = vars(bdy_style)) %>% tab_spanner( label = "model info", columns = vars( year, bdy_style, msrp) ) ``` The `cols_move()` call could be made unnecessary by implementing a `gather` argument. So the code would be simplified to this: ```r gtcars %>% dplyr::select( -mfr, -trim, bdy_style, drivetrain, -drivetrain, -trsmn, -ctry_origin ) %>% dplyr::slice(1:8) %>% gt(rowname_col = "model") %>% tab_header(title = "gtcars") %>% tab_spanner( label = "performance", columns = vars( hp, hp_rpm, trq, trq_rpm, mpg_c, mpg_h) ) %>% tab_spanner( label = "model info", columns = vars( year, bdy_style, msrp), gather = TRUE ) ``` Which yields this table: Issue originally discovered and suggested by @tareefk .
